uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: The tidiest corner prize went to Shy. Shy had arranged twelve perfect pebbles behind a rock where nobody could see them. It counts, said Bossy carefully.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Grumpy won the grumpiest face competition that Cheeky invented. Grumpy won immediately. I am not sure that is a compliment, said Grumpy. It absolutely is, said Cheeky.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Fancy held a Best Sail competition. Fancy was the only one with a sail. Fancy gave themselves first prize. This seems fair, said Fancy.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Fancy held a Best Sail competition. Fancy was the only one with a sail. Fancy gave themselves first prize. This seems fair, said Fancy.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy floated on a cloud past the Rainbow Waterfall. But in the dream, the waterfall was made of warm golden light. Oh, said Dozy. This is very nice.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Back in the meadow, Dozy's eyes opened. All the Dino Pals were sitting in a circle, waiting. What was it like? said Sunny.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy ran harder. The scarf was flat out behind. Everything was a blur.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy crossed the line first. Just. The second runner arrived a heartbeat later.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Bouncy bounced up to reach the high branches and secure anything at risk. Only bumped into three things. A new record, said Bouncy.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: "You need a bath," said Clucky.

uses.title: Woolly Can't Sleep
uses.pageText: Buzz! went a bug.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: Grumpy had a lot of cake.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: Then a bug sat on Noisy.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: Then Noisy saw a worm.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "A WORM! A WORM! A WORM!"

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "A WORM! A WORM! A WORM!"

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "A WORM! A WORM! A WORM!"

uses.title: Splashy Finds a Puddle
uses.pageText: Splashy sees a puddle.

uses.title: Splashy Finds a Puddle
uses.pageText: It is a small puddle.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: Cuddly wants a hug.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: Woolly gave Cuddly a big hug.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: Tiny has lost a hat.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Cuddly wants a hug. Cuddly looks and looks.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Cuddly got a hug.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Shy got a hug too.

uses.title: Sleepy's Big Dream
uses.pageText: Sleepy had a dream.

uses.title: Sleepy's Big Dream
uses.pageText: In the dream, Sleepy was a superhero!

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: "We will bake a cake," said Clucky.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: It was a very flat cake.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Clucky had a bit. Then Clucky giggled too.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Muddy made a mud cake.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Clucky made a big cake.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Grumpy had a lot of cake.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip was walking through Moonwood when his foot kicked something small. It was a tiny stone. It glowed with a soft gold light.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip was walking through Moonwood when his foot kicked something small. It was a tiny stone. It glowed with a soft gold light.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Burrow appeared from a nearby tunnel. "That is a Bravery Stone," said Burrow. "Whoever holds it will feel brave."

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Burrow appeared from a nearby tunnel. "That is a Bravery Stone," said Burrow. "Whoever holds it will feel brave."

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: His legs felt wobbly. The ground was a long way below. But he did not stop. He reached the top.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone for a long time. "I'll keep it," he said. "To remember."

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She said a growing spell. Just a small one. Just to help it along.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She said a growing spell. Just a small one. Just to help it along.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She tried a slowing spell. The plant kept growing. She tried a stopping spell. The plant kept growing.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She tried a slowing spell. The plant kept growing. She tried a stopping spell. The plant kept growing.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: Luna was inside. "Fern," said Luna, through a curtain of leaves, "do something, please."

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: Fern sat down and thought. Spells had made it grow. But a growing thing needed something different.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She did not use a spell. She sang to it, very softly. She sang the song her mother had taught her about seeds.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By evening, it was a large, beautiful plant beside the Hollow Oak. Not too small. Not too large. Luna came out through the door.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: There was a rope bridge over the Crystal Stream. Everyone crossed it without thinking. Everyone except Stone.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone would not cross the bridge. "There is a troll under the bridge," said Stone. "I do not want to meet it."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Pip thought for a moment. "Stone," said Pip carefully. "You are a troll."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Pip thought for a moment. "Stone," said Pip carefully. "You are a troll."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone thought about this for a long time. "Yes," said Stone. "But I still don't like the bridge."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Halfway across, Stone looked straight ahead. The bridge swayed a little. The Crystal Stream sang below. Stone kept walking.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: "You crossed the bridge," said Pip. "Yes," said Stone. "But there might still be a troll under it." Stone looked at the bridge. "I should probably check."

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Every morning, Glimmer practised. Fire breathing was the most important thing a dragon could do. And Glimmer could not do it yet.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the first day: a small puff of smoke. Just smoke. No fire at all.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the fifth day, Glimmer breathed in as deeply as possible. A warm puff came out. It smelled of cinnamon. "That's something," said Pip.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: That evening, a Fog Marsh fox came creeping into Moonwood. It had found Fern's seed collection. The seeds were small and precious. Glimmer saw the fox.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: And a jet of brilliant orange fire came out. The fox ran. The seeds were safe.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren wanted to be taller. She had found a spell in her book. A growing spell, she was sure. She read it very carefully.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren wanted to be taller. She had found a spell in her book. A growing spell, she was sure. She read it very carefully.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: She said the spell. There was a flash of bright blue light. Then it was quiet.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren looked at her hands. Her hands were a very long way away. She was not taller. She was one inch tall.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren picked up her spell book. She turned to the next spell. "But I am going to find a better one," she said. She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint had decided to map every single path in Moonwood. He had a new roll of parchment and a good quill. He started at the Hollow Oak and walked north.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint had decided to map every single path in Moonwood. He had a new roll of parchment and a good quill. He started at the Hollow Oak and walked north.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint sat down on a mossy rock. He looked at the map for a long time. It was very beautiful. It was also completely wrong.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint sat down on a mossy rock. He looked at the map for a long time. It was very beautiful. It was also completely wrong.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint took out a new piece of parchment. "I'll make another one," he said. He was not upset about this. He had always known the paths would move.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: One morning, a new fish appeared. It was silver with a bright blue stripe. Dewdrop had never seen a fish like it.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: One morning, a new fish appeared. It was silver with a bright blue stripe. Dewdrop had never seen a fish like it.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: One morning, a new fish appeared. It was silver with a bright blue stripe. Dewdrop had never seen a fish like it.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop was not sure any of this was true. She knew the Deep Dark secrets. They were kept by a very old badger, not a fish.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop was not sure any of this was true. She knew the Deep Dark secrets. They were kept by a very old badger, not a fish.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Can fish lie? Dewdrop asked Burrow. Some of them can, said Burrow. Which fish? The new one with the blue stripe, said Dewdrop. Burrow had not seen a new fish.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: The fish was quiet for a while. It swam a small, slow circle. Then it came back. Because I am new here, said the fish. And I wanted to sound interesting.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: The fish was quiet for a while. It swam a small, slow circle. Then it came back. Because I am new here, said the fish. And I wanted to sound interesting.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: You are interesting, said Dewdrop. You are the only fish in this stream with a blue stripe. The fish looked at its own stripe. That is true, it said.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow was digging a new tunnel. He dug down, and he dug sideways, and he dug carefully around the roots. Then his spade hit something hard and wooden.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow set down his spade. He felt around it very carefully. It was a door. A small, very old wooden door, deep underground.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow set down his spade. He felt around it very carefully. It was a door. A small, very old wooden door, deep underground.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: He polished his glasses and looked more closely. On the door was a small carving. A tree with roots going in every direction. It was very old.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: He polished his glasses and looked more closely. On the door was a small carving. A tree with roots going in every direction. It was very old.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: I have found something, Burrow told everyone. They gathered at the Hollow Oak. A door, said Burrow, underground. Very old. I don't know what is inside.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow opened the door. A warm golden light came from inside. Everyone leaned forward.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Inside was a small round room. The walls were covered in tiny glowing drawings. Trees and streams. Creatures and old paths. Every living thing that had ever been in Moonwood.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They stayed for a long time. No one wanted to leave. The room was very quiet and very warm.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow found a blank patch of wall. He picked up a small flat stone. Very carefully, he drew the Hollow Oak. Now we are in it too, he said.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow found a blank patch of wall. He picked up a small flat stone. Very carefully, he drew the Hollow Oak. Now we are in it too, he said.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: He sneezed at breakfast. The porridge turned into a bird. The bird flew out of the window. Spark stared at his empty bowl.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Every fish in the stream turned purple. The water sang in a different key. One fish turned into a frog for a moment, and then turned back.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Every fish in the stream turned purple. The water sang in a different key. One fish turned into a frog for a moment, and then turned back.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Every fish in the stream turned purple. The water sang in a different key. One fish turned into a frog for a moment, and then turned back.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: I think, said Dewdrop slowly, we should find you a cold remedy before anything else changes.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Wren found a cold remedy in her spell book. She read it very, very carefully. Forwards? said Spark. Forwards, said Wren.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark breathed in carefully. I think, he said, I might need to sneeze again. Everyone took a large step back.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it a meeting? asked Fern. I don't think so, said Luna. Was it something to collect? asked Burrow. Possibly, said Luna. I cannot quite say.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it something to do with the Crystal Stream? asked Dewdrop. Luna stopped walking. She looked at the stream for a moment. Wait, said Luna.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna flew to the Crystal Stream. She landed on a stepping stone. She looked down into the water.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: She opened the box. Inside were twelve small seeds. Each one glowed with a soft gold light. Oh, said Fern, very quietly.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: They planted the seeds in a ring around the Hollow Oak. One from each of them. In the golden afternoon light.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip and Stone were sitting outside the Hollow Oak.
Then a noise came from the Fog Marsh.
It was very, very loud.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the source, they found it.
A great boulder had fallen.
It lay across the singing stones.
The stones could not sing.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.
"Ready?" said Fern.
"Ready," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the Hollow Oak, everyone heard it.
"The stream is singing again!" said Pip.
"We just moved a stone," said Fern.
"And asked the water nicely," said Dewdrop.
"It did the rest."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer and Spark made a deal.
Spark would teach Glimmer to breathe fire properly.
Glimmer would teach Spark to fly.
They shook on it.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
That afternoon, it was Glimmer's turn to teach.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer hovered for a moment.
Then landed.
"Like that," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"Spark," said Glimmer.
"You are trying too hard."
"Fire is not thinking."
"It is feeling."
Spark looked at Glimmer for a long time.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark put down his wand.
He put down his notes.
He stood very still.
He stopped thinking.
A small real flame came.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.
Wren had a direction spell.
"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.
Wren had a direction spell.
"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They sat down under a large mushroom.
They were tired.
They were lost.
The mushroom glowed cheerfully.
Wren looked at it.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
The mushroom's glow changed.
It pulsed once — pointing.
Another mushroom far away pulsed the same way.
And another.
A trail of glowing mushrooms lit up through the trees.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow was digging a new tunnel.
He dug every morning.
He liked the quiet of it.
He liked the dark of it.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Then his tunnel fell open.
He tumbled into a room.
It was large.
It was old.
It was not a tunnel.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Then his tunnel fell open.
He tumbled into a room.
It was large.
It was old.
It was not a tunnel.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow went up to find Luna.
"Come with me," he said.
"Bring a light."
Luna said nothing.
She came.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna was very large for a tunnel.
She came anyway.
She did not say anything about this.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"Have you been here before?" asked Burrow.
"Yes," said Luna.
She looked around the room.
"A very long time ago."
"What is it?" asked Burrow.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna settled on a ledge.
She folded her wings.
She looked at the carvings for a moment.
"The first story of Moonwood," she began,
"is this."

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna settled on a ledge.
She folded her wings.
She looked at the carvings for a moment.
"The first story of Moonwood," she began,
"is this."

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
It was very late when Burrow noticed.
"Will you tell me the rest?" he asked.
"Yes," said Luna.
"There is quite a lot."
They both settled in.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
One morning, things had moved in the night.
Pip's boots were not where he had left them.
A bench was tipped over.
Someone had been in the clearing.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then — a sound.
A shuffling.
A round shape moving through the clearing.
Pip and Glimmer looked at each other.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then — a sound.
A shuffling.
A round shape moving through the clearing.
Pip and Glimmer looked at each other.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then — a sound.
A shuffling.
A round shape moving through the clearing.
Pip and Glimmer looked at each other.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
In the morning, Burrow woke up.
He looked around.
Pip and Glimmer were standing in front of him.
"Good morning," said Burrow.
There was a long pause.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern's garden was her favourite place.
One morning, Wren arrived with a cauldron.
"I have a potion," said Wren.
"It will help your plants."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern's garden was her favourite place.
One morning, Wren arrived with a cauldron.
"I have a potion," said Wren.
"It will help your plants."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren poured the potion on the plants.
The plants stood very straight.
Then they leaned.
Then one of them took a step.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Then all the plants began to walk.
They were very polite about it.
They walked around Fern.
They walked around Wren.
They went for a stroll.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants walked into the Hollow Oak.
Some walked toward the Crystal Stream.
A very small plant walked very slowly toward Burrow's tunnel.
They were not in a hurry.
They were just walking.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants walked into the Hollow Oak.
Some walked toward the Crystal Stream.
A very small plant walked very slowly toward Burrow's tunnel.
They were not in a hurry.
They were just walking.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren found the problem.
She had used the wrong book.
"This is the motion recipe," she said.
"Not the growing recipe."
She showed Fern.
They were both quiet for a moment.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop was at the Crystal Stream.
She was looking at something in the water.
It was a large fish.
It was stuck.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop found Stone at the Hollow Oak.
"I need your hands," she said.
"Just to reach in and move a rock."
Stone understood immediately.
Then Stone understood all of it.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
"Just your arm," said Dewdrop.
"Just the one arm."
"Just for a moment."
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the water.
Stone sat down on the bank.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
The fish made a very large splash.
Stone was completely wet.
All of Stone.
Dewdrop was not wet.
"I'm sorry," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
They sat by the stream together.
Stone dripped for a long time.
The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.
And meant it.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
The magic seeds were gone.
The box that held them was open and empty.
Luna looked at the box for a long time.
"This is not good," she said.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
They split into groups.
Each group took a different path.
Each path led somewhere different.
"Find the seeds," said Luna.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Fern stopped.
She knelt down.
There were small green shoots in the ground.
They glowed.
Just a little.
Just like the seeds.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The small things landed and bounced.
They bounced along the ground.
They made a sound like giggling.
They left gold trails where they bounced.
"What ARE they?" said Pip.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Stone raised their hands high.
Pip and Spark added a little push.
The star spirits lifted.
Up.
And up.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
It was late in the Hollow Oak.
Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip noticed it on a Tuesday.
The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip noticed it on a Tuesday.
The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
At the centre of the marsh, they found it.
A figure made of grey mist.
It sat against a dead tree.
It was very still.
It looked very sad.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
At the centre of the marsh, they found it.
A figure made of grey mist.
It sat against a dead tree.
It was very still.
It looked very sad.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
They marked the boundary at the Hollow Oak.
Everyone placed a stone.
"The marsh is the marsh," said Luna.
"Moonwood is Moonwood."
"And we leave space for both."

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
There was a sign on the Hollow Oak door.
GLIMMER'S FIRE PERFORMANCE — TODAY.
Everyone came.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer breathed in.
Deeply.
Glimmer breathed out.
A jet of orange fire came out.
Small.
Perfect.
Real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer did it again.
Longer.
The fire was steady.
It was warm.
Glimmer's scales caught the light.
Glimmer had never looked so much like a dragon.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire was very large.
It was taller than Glimmer.
It caught the torch on the Hollow Oak door.
The torch lit the first lamp.
The lamp lit a mushroom.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
It was the deepest part of the night.
Moonwood was very quiet.
Then there was a sound at the edge of the clearing.
Something small was there.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip opened the door.
A small creature was at the edge of the clearing.
It had very large silver eyes.
It was frightened.
It did not run.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip brought it inside.
Everyone woke up.
Stone brought a piece of acorn biscuit.
The creature ate it very carefully.
It watched everyone with its large silver eyes.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The Deep Dark was very dark.
The trees had no glow.
The light went only a little way ahead.
They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Beyond the roots, a small clearing.
Silver moss lit the ground.
It was warm.
Other creatures were there.
They looked up.
They had the same enormous silver eyes.

It can sing.

Hot soup!
It is hot. Mmm!

uses.pageText:
Cold milk!
It is cold. Yum!

It is a circle.

It is a square.

uses.title: Shapes

It is a rectangle.

It is a triangle.

What shape is it?
Can you find it?

What shape is it?
Can you find it?

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see a big dog.
It runs fast.

uses.title: In the Sea
uses.pageText:
A whale can swim far.
It is huge.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
An apple is red.
It is sweet.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
A banana is yellow.
It is soft.

A plum is purple.

An orange is round.
It is bright.

A grape is small.
It is round.

It is red! It is yellow!
I love fruit!

It is red! It is yellow!
I love fruit!

The tree is big.
It is tall.

It is soft.

A little puppy.
It can run.

A little cub.
It is round and brown.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText:
A little calf.
It drinks milk.

A snail is slow.
It is not fast.

uses.title: Fast and Slow

A worm is slow.
It is not fast.

uses.title: Fast and Slow
uses.pageText:
A turtle is slow.
It does not rush.

A seed is little.
Put it in the dirt.

uses.pageText:
A bud forms.
It can bloom!

The moon is big.
It is round.

uses.title: Space

The sun is the biggest.
It is very hot.

uses.title: Space

Earth is our home.
It is blue and green.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText:
Mars is red.
It is a planet.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is summer. The sun is hot. It is a sunny day.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is winter. It is cold. Snow falls.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: This is a seed. It is tiny. Seeds come in many shapes.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Put the seed in soil. Pat it down gently.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Add some water. The seed drinks it up.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A green shoot comes up! It has two small leaves.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: The stem grows tall. More leaves grow. It needs sun and water.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is sunny! The sun is bright. It feels warm.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is sunny! The sun is bright. It feels warm.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is rainy. Drops fall from the clouds. Drip, drip, drip.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is windy. The wind blows hard. Leaves fly in the air.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is snowy. White flakes fall. Everything looks white.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is cloudy. Grey clouds fill the sky. Where is the sun?

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A sunflower is tall and yellow. The sun makes it grow.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A daisy is small and white. It grows in the grass.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A rose is red. It smells sweet. It has sharp thorns.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A rose is red. It smells sweet. It has sharp thorns.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean is big. It is full of animals. Let us look!

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A whale is huge! It is the biggest animal. Whales swim to the top to breathe.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: An octopus has eight arms. It can change colour. It hides in rocks.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: An octopus has eight arms. It can change colour. It hides in rocks.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A seahorse is tiny. It holds on to plants.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: An owl can see in the dark. It hunts at night. Twit-twoo!

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: A bat flies at night. It finds food in the dark. Bats eat insects.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: A hedgehog snuffles in the dark. It looks for slugs and bugs.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: A fox hunts at night. It has big ears. It moves quietly.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: A fox hunts at night. It has big ears. It moves quietly.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A ladybird is red with black spots. It eats tiny greenfly.

uses.title: Hot and Cold
uses.pageText: The sun is hot. It warms us up.

uses.title: Hot and Cold
uses.pageText: Fire is hot. Do not touch it!

uses.title: Hot and Cold
uses.pageText: Hot food can burn. Let it cool down first.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: Drop a duck in water. It floats on top!

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: Drop a stone in water. It sinks to the bottom.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: A boat floats on the water. It can carry things.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: Try it yourself! What floats? What sinks?

uses.title: Hello, Sun!
uses.pageText: The sun is a big, hot star. It is very far away.

uses.title: Hello, Sun!
uses.pageText: At midday, the sun is high. It is the hottest part of the day.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon shines at night. It gives us light in the dark.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon changes shape. Sometimes it looks like a banana.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: Sometimes it is a full circle. This is a full moon.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon goes around the Earth. It travels very slowly.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon is far away. But we can see it every night.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: My body is amazing! I look after it every day.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: My body is mine. I keep it safe and strong.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Go outside and find a rock! Look at it carefully.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: Water is precious. Let us look after it.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Deep underground, rock gets so hot that it melts. This melted rock is called magma. Magma is hotter than anything you can imagine.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Sometimes, magma pushes up through a crack in the Earth. When it bursts out at the surface, we call it a volcano! The melted rock that flows out is called lava.

uses.title: Volcanoes

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: The female emperor penguin lays one egg. The father balances it on his feet and covers it with a warm flap of skin. He keeps it safe from the freezing cold.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: When the egg hatches, a tiny chick comes out. The chick has thick grey fluffy feathers. It cuddles close to its parent to stay warm.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon does not make its own light. It has no fire or glow inside. The light we see is sunlight bouncing off the Moon's surface.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks different every night. Sometimes it is a full, bright circle. Sometimes it is a thin crescent. These different shapes are called the phases of the Moon.

uses.title: The Moon

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans. This causes the tides. When the tide comes in, the sea rises up the beach. When it goes out, it pulls back.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans. This causes the tides. When the tide comes in, the sea rises up the beach. When it goes out, it pulls back.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks small from Earth, but it is very large. It is about a quarter the size of our whole planet. If Earth were a basketball, the Moon would be a tennis ball.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A seed needs three things to start growing: water, warmth, and air. When it gets all three, it wakes up and begins to grow.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A seed needs three things to start growing: water, warmth, and air. When it gets all three, it wakes up and begins to grow.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: The shoot breaks through the soil. It opens its first leaves toward the sun. Now the plant can begin to make its own food.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Plants use sunlight, water, and air to make food. This is called photosynthesis. It also makes the oxygen we breathe. Plants feed us and give us air!

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: You can grow your own plant. Put a seed in some soil. Add water. Put it in a sunny spot. Then watch the cycle begin.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders have eight eyes, but many cannot see well. Instead, they feel vibrations through their legs. When something touches the web, the spider feels it instantly.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: When an insect is caught, the spider wraps it in silk. This keeps it still. Then the spider injects venom to begin digesting its meal.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean covers more than two thirds of our planet. It is the largest habitat on Earth. And most of it is still unexplored.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean covers more than two thirds of our planet. It is the largest habitat on Earth. And most of it is still unexplored.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean has different layers. Near the surface, there is plenty of sunlight and warmth. Further down, it grows colder and darker. Below 200 metres, no sunlight reaches at all.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Coral looks like rock or plant, but it is an animal. Each piece of coral is made of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps. Coral reefs take thousands of years to grow.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The deepest part of the ocean is called the Mariana Trench. It is nearly 11 kilometres deep. If you put the world's tallest mountain inside it, it would still be covered by water.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage two: the egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar's only job is to eat. It eats and eats and grows and grows. Some caterpillars eat their own eggshell first!

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Most caves form when rainwater seeps into limestone rock. The water is slightly acidic. It slowly dissolves the rock away. This takes thousands and thousands of years.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A female frog lays hundreds of eggs in water. The eggs are called frogspawn. Each egg is surrounded by clear jelly that protects it and keeps it safe.

uses.title: Frogs

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Slowly, the tadpole changes. Back legs appear first. Then front legs. The tail shrinks away. After about twelve weeks, it is a frog!

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: The young frog climbs out of the water. It can now breathe air through its lungs. It can also live on land. The whole world opens up.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: The young frog climbs out of the water. It can now breathe air through its lungs. It can also live on land. The whole world opens up.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

uses.title: Bob and Nan's First Day at School
uses.pageText: It is the big day.

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: It is Bob's big day!

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: Bob rips it! It is a red bat!

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: Bob rips it! It is a red bat!

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: It was the best day!

uses.title: Nan and Bob Learn to Read
uses.pageText: C - A - T. Cat! Bob can get it!

uses.title: Nan and Bob Learn to Read
uses.pageText: Bob can read it: 'The dog ran.'

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Anna grabbed her pen and drew the plan. "It needs big wings," she said, "and a pointed nose cone at the top."

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James got the red paint. Anna got the silver paint. They painted and painted until it shone!

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "It is the best rocket ever made!" said James. He and Anna stood back and grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They landed on the moon with a big BUMP! It was pale and still and very, very quiet.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: A small green alien ran to say hello. "My name is Zim!" it said. "Do you want to play?"

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Then Chips saw a big rose bush. He ran at it. CRUNCH! MUNCH! SNAP! The rose bush was gone.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips ate it all in a flash. He looked at the bowl. Then he looked at James. Then he looked at James's jumper.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: It was a bright autumn day. Mum had a long list. "I need help at the shop," she said. "Can you both come?"

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: The shop was big and bright. It smelled of fresh bread and ripe fruit.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Anna ran to find the bread. She picked the big round loaf with seeds on top. It smelled amazing!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James came out. "It did not hurt at all!" he said. "And the chair goes UP and DOWN!" Anna laughed.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: At the end of the garden stood a big old oak tree. James and Anna had been staring at it for days.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: "We should build a tree house!" said James. He got his notebook and drew the plan right away. It had a door, a window, a flag and a rope ladder.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Next came the floor — flat planks, all in a row. "Walk on it!" said Dad. They did. It held firm!

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Next came the floor — flat planks, all in a row. "Walk on it!" said Dad. They did. It held firm!

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna got to brush Bess's mane. James gave her a big red apple. Bess sniffed it — then snaffled the whole thing in one go!

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: That evening, Grandma made soup from the garden and fried the eggs James had found. It was the best meal they had ever tasted.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mrs. Green told the class: "We are putting on a school play! It is called 'The Lost Dragon'."

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James practised his dragon roar all week. It shook the windows. Mum wore earmuffs. Chips ran under the sofa.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James took a deep breath. He thought of his best roar. Then he let it out — the biggest, loudest roar he had ever done.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mum and Dad clapped the loudest. Mum had tears. Dad said it was just the bright lights. James and Anna did not believe him.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. They were absolutely sure it would be fine. They were wrong.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James tried again. Eyes forward. Pedal. Wobble. Wobble. Then — he was doing it! He was really, properly doing it!

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James tried again. Eyes forward. Pedal. Wobble. Wobble. Then — he was doing it! He was really, properly doing it!

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Then James tried riding with NO hands. He made it exactly three seconds before heading straight into the same bush.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The marshmallow on Chips's stick got too close to the fire. It caught light. Chips ate the whole thing — stick and all.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "What if it comes back?" said James. "Then we will scare it," said Anna. She picked up the air horn Dad had packed.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "What if it comes back?" said James. "Then we will scare it," said Anna. She picked up the air horn Dad had packed.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they said. But the sun was warm and breakfast was good and it had been a perfect camp.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Aiden spent the whole first morning at a rock pool near the headland. He found three kinds of crab, a sea anemone that closed when you touched it, and a tiny fish he thought might be a blenny. He wrote everything down in his field notebook in careful columns.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: It started with the waistcoat hook being empty.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They decided to grow crystals. It was Betty's original idea and Aiden's second choice, which Betty said made it the obvious answer. They ordered the kit and spent four days watching for the post.

uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.pageText: "Socks!" said Aiden and Betty. Socks examined the jar from every angle, turning it slowly. He handed it back eventually — and the crystals were, miraculously, completely intact.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Third place, with a commendation for experimental method, went to HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW? The commendation was on a proper certificate with a gold border. Betty read every word of it, twice.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Through the binoculars, Betty saw a kingfisher — a bright impossible dart of blue-orange above the water, there and then gone. She had to put the binoculars down and close her eyes for a moment. She had seen it. She wrote it in the log book.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Aiden had started a new notebook that evening — not the Socks field study, but a nature notebook. He had titled it with the date. Betty had started a matching one, without them discussing it. Both were already half a page in.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden didn't say anything. He went home and sat on his bed and stared at the ceiling. He wasn't crying, but he wasn't fine either. He didn't really want to talk about it — which Betty noticed immediately.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden wrote in his notebook: When something is unfair, you have two choices — pretend it isn't happening, or decide what to do. He starred the second option. He didn't quite know yet what doing something looked like.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: It was quiet. Nobody laughed. Marcus said something low, but nobody around him responded. Aiden walked on. His legs were slightly shaky — but he hadn't shown it, and he was extremely proud of himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: It was quiet. Nobody laughed. Marcus said something low, but nobody around him responded. Aiden walked on. His legs were slightly shaky — but he hadn't shown it, and he was extremely proud of himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: He wrote in his notebook that evening: Saying a true thing clearly is harder than it looks and better than it sounds. He underlined it twice.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor had noticed, in the way that good teachers always notice. She started a class discussion about what it means to be fair, and what you do when things aren't. Several children looked at the floor. Marcus looked at the window.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He told Betty. Betty got the torch and studied it with great interest. "It's definitely loose," she said. "It'll fall out and a permanent one will grow. That's much better, actually." Aiden was not entirely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He told Betty. Betty got the torch and studied it with great interest. "It's definitely loose," she said. "It'll fall out and a permanent one will grow. That's much better, actually." Aiden was not entirely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Mum said it was completely normal and that they had both lost teeth before when they were smaller — Aiden had even eaten one inside a peanut butter sandwich and not noticed for an hour. Aiden was not certain this was reassuring.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Aiden's tooth came out on a Thursday. Not dramatically — he was reading his book and he touched it and then it was just there in his fingers, which was very quick and very strange and did not hurt at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He held it up for a long time. It was tiny. It was the smallest thing that had ever felt significant. He put it in the small envelope Mum left for him, and when he placed it under his pillow it felt ceremonial.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Three weeks later, the new tooth began to come through. It was enormous relative to the gap — a proper square adult tooth in a mouth that had been full of small rounded baby ones. Aiden looked at himself in the mirror and felt extremely strange.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Socks was fascinated by both of them through this whole period. He kept trying to look in their mouths. He seemed to find it deeply interesting, which Aiden added to the field notebook under: Primate-specific dental curiosity — possible.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the armoury, there was a full suit of plate armour. It was smaller than Aiden expected. The guide told them that real knights were roughly the same size as Dad, which was very hard to imagine. Aiden tried on a gauntlet under supervision. His hand barely fit inside.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.
