uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: When an insect is caught, the spider wraps it in silk. This keeps it still. Then the spider injects venom to begin digesting its meal.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Slowly, the tadpole changes. Back legs appear first. Then front legs. The tail shrinks away. After about twelve weeks, it is a frog!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Then Chips saw a big rose bush. He ran at it. CRUNCH! MUNCH! SNAP! The rose bush was gone.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips ate it all in a flash. He looked at the bowl. Then he looked at James. Then he looked at James's jumper.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips ate it all in a flash. He looked at the bowl. Then he looked at James. Then he looked at James's jumper.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Then Anna spotted the cake stand! Big cakes, small cakes, jam tarts and iced buns — all in a long, shining row.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Then they made the walls and cut a little door. James helped saw a window hole with a small hand saw.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna got to brush Bess's mane. James gave her a big red apple. Bess sniffed it — then snaffled the whole thing in one go!

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Then Percy the pig got out. He ran in and out of the hen house and round and round the yard at top speed.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Chips had been quiet all morning. Then they found him — in the veggie patch, eating the bean plants.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Then the lights went up and James walked on stage. He could see the WHOLE school in the dark. His legs went very wobbly.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James took a deep breath. He thought of his best roar. Then he let it out — the biggest, loudest roar he had ever done.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mum brought out two bowls — water for Bella, chopped apple for Chips. Bella drank hers. Chips ate his. Then Chips ate Bella's water too.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James tried again. Eyes forward. Pedal. Wobble. Wobble. Then — he was doing it! He was really, properly doing it!

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Then James tried riding with NO hands. He made it exactly three seconds before heading straight into the same bush.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: James and Anna helped bang in the tent pegs and thread the poles through. Chips ate one peg. Then he tried to eat a second.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "What if it comes back?" said James. "Then we will scare it," said Anna. She picked up the air horn Dad had packed.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Through the binoculars, Betty saw a kingfisher — a bright impossible dart of blue-orange above the water, there and then gone. She had to put the binoculars down and close her eyes for a moment. She had seen it. She wrote it in the log book.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Aiden's tooth came out on a Thursday. Not dramatically — he was reading his book and he touched it and then it was just there in his fingers, which was very quick and very strange and did not hurt at all.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Then a thunderstorm came. Dozy woke up frightened. All the Dino Pals hid.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky laughed and laughed. But then Cheeky slipped on the same mud. SPLAT!

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Dozy hugged the pillow. Thank you, said Dozy. Both of you. Then Dozy fell asleep, right there, on the spot.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy woke up and tried to fly. Flappy got three wing-flaps up. Then landed in the mud.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Then Chompy fell into a ditch. HELP, said Chompy. It was not a deep ditch. But Chompy's arms were very tiny.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy ran three circuits of Sunny Hollow. Then four. Then five. Then kept going.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy ran three circuits of Sunny Hollow. Then four. Then five. Then kept going.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy ran three circuits of Sunny Hollow. Then four. Then five. Then kept going.

uses.title: Woolly Can't Sleep
uses.pageText: Then it was quiet.

uses.title: Bouncy Won't Stop
uses.pageText: Then Bouncy hopped again.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: Then a bug sat on Noisy.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: Then Noisy saw a worm.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText: Then Shy came out.

uses.title: Giggly Has the Hiccups
uses.pageText: Then Giggly stopped.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: Then Brave fell off.

uses.title: Sleepy's Big Dream
uses.pageText: Then Sleepy woke up.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Clucky had a bit. Then Clucky giggled too.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "The stone did that!" said Pip. He tucked it safely into his pocket. Then he walked toward the Fog Marsh.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: The plant stopped growing. The leaves curled gently inward. Then, slowly, it began to shrink.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They crossed back together. Stone did not look at the water. Stone looked at the far end of the bridge. One step, then another.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: She said the spell. There was a flash of bright blue light. Then it was quiet.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly. They always did.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: The fish was quiet for a while. It swam a small, slow circle. Then it came back. Because I am new here, said the fish. And I wanted to sound interesting.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow was digging a new tunnel. He dug down, and he dug sideways, and he dug carefully around the roots. Then his spade hit something hard and wooden.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Every fish in the stream turned purple. The water sang in a different key. One fish turned into a frog for a moment, and then turned back.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip and Stone were sitting outside the Hollow Oak.
Then a noise came from the Fog Marsh.
It was very, very loud.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
"The song comes from the source," said Dewdrop.
"We must follow the stream up."
Fern looked at the deep forest ahead.
"Then we go," said Fern.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
The water rushed over the singing stones.
And the Crystal Stream began to sing.
First very quietly.
Then louder.
Then loud enough to hear all the way to the Hollow Oak.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
The water rushed over the singing stones.
And the Crystal Stream began to sing.
First very quietly.
Then louder.
Then loud enough to hear all the way to the Hollow Oak.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
That afternoon, it was Glimmer's turn to teach.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer hovered for a moment.
Then landed.
"Like that," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Then his tunnel fell open.
He tumbled into a room.
It was large.
It was old.
It was not a tunnel.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna stood in the doorway.
She was very still.
Her eyes went wide.
Then soft.
"Oh," said Luna.
Very quietly.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then — a sound.
A shuffling.
A round shape moving through the clearing.
Pip and Glimmer looked at each other.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then Burrow sat down.
Against the big mushroom.
Pip and Glimmer were still behind it.
Burrow began to snore.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren poured the potion on the plants.
The plants stood very straight.
Then they leaned.
Then one of them took a step.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren poured the potion on the plants.
The plants stood very straight.
Then they leaned.
Then one of them took a step.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Then all the plants began to walk.
They were very polite about it.
They walked around Fern.
They walked around Wren.
They went for a stroll.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop found Stone at the Hollow Oak.
"I need your hands," she said.
"Just to reach in and move a rock."
Stone understood immediately.
Then Stone understood all of it.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
It was late in the Hollow Oak.
Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Pip, Wren, Burrow, and Fern went inside to search.
They searched every room.
They found nothing.
Then Burrow's nose twitched.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern looked around the room.
Then she looked at Twig.
The spectacles were on top of Twig's head.
They had been there all along.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone looked at the forest.
Then everyone looked at Glimmer.
Glimmer looked at the forest.
Glimmer looked at their own mouth.
"Oh," said Glimmer.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
It was the deepest part of the night.
Moonwood was very quiet.
Then there was a sound at the edge of the clearing.
Something small was there.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip knelt down.
He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
"Where is your home?" asked Burrow, gently.
The creature looked at its paws.
Then at the window.
"Deep," it said.
"Deep dark."

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The creature ran to its family.
The family gathered around it.
They looked at the Moonwood creatures.
Not afraid.
Just looking.
Then one of them blinked.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
A grape is small.
It is round.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText:
Space is very big!
We are small.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A green shoot comes up! It has two small leaves.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A daisy is small and white. It grows in the grass.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: Bugs are all around us. Big bugs. Small bugs. Look closely!

uses.title: Pets We Love
uses.pageText: A hamster is small and fluffy. Hamsters run on a wheel.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: This is small. A mouse is small.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: This is small. A mouse is small.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: A bus is big. A toy car is small.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: A tree is big. A flower is small.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: A whale is big. A fish is small.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: Big or small — all things are special! What is big? What is small?

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: Big or small — all things are special! What is big? What is small?

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Rocks are hard. Rocks can be big or small.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Pebbles are small, smooth rocks. Water makes them smooth.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: We can help bees by planting flowers. Bees love lavender, sunflowers, and daisies. Even a small garden or a pot of flowers can help.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: In 1969, astronauts travelled to the Moon. Neil Armstrong was the first human to walk on its surface. "That's one small step for man," he said.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks small from Earth, but it is very large. It is about a quarter the size of our whole planet. If Earth were a basketball, the Moon would be a tennis ball.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage one: the butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf. The eggs are very small — some are no bigger than a pinhead. The leaf is food for the caterpillar inside.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: A small green alien ran to say hello. "My name is Zim!" it said. "Do you want to play?"

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James and Anna had a pet goat. His name was Chips. He was small and white with big brown patches.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Then Anna spotted the cake stand! Big cakes, small cakes, jam tarts and iced buns — all in a long, shining row.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Then they made the walls and cut a little door. James helped saw a window hole with a small hand saw.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Dad made a small camp fire in a safe metal dish. They toasted marshmallows on long sticks over the warm flames.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The view from the top was unlike anything Aiden had seen. The whole coastline curved away in both directions — bays and headlands, a small fishing village far below, and the sea stretching to the horizon, catching the light like crinkled silver foil.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He held it up for a long time. It was tiny. It was the smallest thing that had ever felt significant. He put it in the small envelope Mum left for him, and when he placed it under his pillow it felt ceremonial.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Three weeks later, the new tooth began to come through. It was enormous relative to the gap — a proper square adult tooth in a mouth that had been full of small rounded baby ones. Aiden looked at himself in the mirror and felt extremely strange.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The dungeon was underground and smelled of cold stone and old air. Betty read every board by torchlight. Aiden stood still in the near-dark for a moment and thought about how this exact place had been here through everything — and felt briefly, appropriately small.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Every morning, the Dino Pals found a small gift on the Big Flat Rock. Nobody knew who left them.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Sunny saw two small eyes behind a rock. And two small pink paws placing a tiny woven grass bracelet on the rock.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Sunny saw two small eyes behind a rock. And two small pink paws placing a tiny woven grass bracelet on the rock.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried roaring like the other dinosaurs. A small squawk came out. Some feathers drifted down.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried stomping. Flappy's feet were quite small. Nobody noticed.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Grumpy has a strong tail, said Sunny. Grumpy swung the club tail at the rocks. CLONK. One small rock moved. There were fifty more.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy held the small winner's pebble and looked at it. Zippy, said Sunny, are you all right? I nearly lost, said Zippy.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny is small.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Very, very small.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Small is very, very good.

uses.title: Splashy Finds a Puddle
uses.pageText: It is a small puddle.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip was walking through Moonwood when his foot kicked something small. It was a tiny stone. It glowed with a soft gold light.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: Fern had one small seed. She planted it in the soft ground near the Hollow Oak.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She said a growing spell. Just a small one. Just to help it along.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By evening, it was a large, beautiful plant beside the Hollow Oak. Not too small. Not too large. Luna came out through the door.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the first day: a small puff of smoke. Just smoke. No fire at all.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: That evening, a Fog Marsh fox came creeping into Moonwood. It had found Fern's seed collection. The seeds were small and precious. Glimmer saw the fox.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Oh, said Wren. Her voice came out very small. Everything around her was enormous.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: The fish was quiet for a while. It swam a small, slow circle. Then it came back. Because I am new here, said the fish. And I wanted to sound interesting.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: After that, the fish told Dewdrop true things. Small things, mostly. Where the water was coldest. Where the most unusual pebbles were. These things were true.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow set down his spade. He felt around it very carefully. It was a door. A small, very old wooden door, deep underground.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: He polished his glasses and looked more closely. On the door was a small carving. A tree with roots going in every direction. It was very old.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They all came to look. The tunnel was small. Stone had to go sideways. Luna had to be helped around three corners.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Inside was a small round room. The walls were covered in tiny glowing drawings. Trees and streams. Creatures and old paths. Every living thing that had ever been in Moonwood.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow found a blank patch of wall. He picked up a small flat stone. Very carefully, he drew the Hollow Oak. Now we are in it too, he said.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: She opened the box. Inside were twelve small seeds. Each one glowed with a soft gold light. Oh, said Fern, very quietly.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
"Why were you shouting?" asked Pip.
The toadling blinked.
"I am lost," it said.
"I was calling for my family."
Its voice was very small now.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Back at the Hollow Oak, everyone asked:
"What was the loud thing?"
"Very small," said Pip.
"Very loud," said Stone.
They both smiled.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark put down his wand.
He put down his notes.
He stood very still.
He stopped thinking.
A small real flame came.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
The room had carvings on every wall.
It had small glowing stones in the ceiling.
It smelled of old wood and old magic.
Burrow had never seen it before.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants walked into the Hollow Oak.
Some walked toward the Crystal Stream.
A very small plant walked very slowly toward Burrow's tunnel.
They were not in a hurry.
They were just walking.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Fern stopped.
She knelt down.
There were small green shoots in the ground.
They glowed.
Just a little.
Just like the seeds.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The small things landed and bounced.
They bounced along the ground.
They made a sound like giggling.
They left gold trails where they bounced.
"What ARE they?" said Pip.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"What are you?" asked Pip.
The star spirit blinked its large gold eyes.
"Star," it said.
Its voice was very small.
"Fell," it added.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer breathed in.
Deeply.
Glimmer breathed out.
A jet of orange fire came out.
Small.
Perfect.
Real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
It was the deepest part of the night.
Moonwood was very quiet.
Then there was a sound at the edge of the clearing.
Something small was there.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip opened the door.
A small creature was at the edge of the clearing.
It had very large silver eyes.
It was frightened.
It did not run.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Beyond the roots, a small clearing.
Silver moss lit the ground.
It was warm.
Other creatures were there.
They looked up.
They had the same enormous silver eyes.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: I see with my eyes.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: I hear with my ears.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: I smell with my nose.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: I taste with my tongue.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: I touch with my hands.

uses.title: Healthy Habits
uses.pageText: I wash my hands with soap.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A ladybird is red with black spots. It eats tiny greenfly.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: The female emperor penguin lays one egg. The father balances it on his feet and covers it with a warm flap of skin. He keeps it safe from the freezing cold.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: The father does not eat for two months. He huddles with other fathers to stay warm. Meanwhile, the mother goes to the sea to find fish. She will bring food back when the egg hatches.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: You can see the Moon most nights. On a clear night with a telescope, you can see the craters clearly. Look up tonight — the Moon is always there.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They landed on the moon with a big BUMP! It was pale and still and very, very quiet.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James and Anna played with Zim all day. They jumped so high on the moon!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James and Anna had a pet goat. His name was Chips. He was small and white with big brown patches.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They got home just in time for lunch. James filled Chips's bowl with fresh grass and sliced apple.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Anna ran to find the bread. She picked the big round loaf with seeds on top. It smelled amazing!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: They found the cheese, the eggs and the juice. James was very careful with the eggs.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James chose a big slice of lemon cake with thick white icing. Anna chose a pink strawberry jam tart.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At the till, Mum let James put the shopping on the belt. He was VERY careful with the eggs.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Then they made the walls and cut a little door. James helped saw a window hole with a small hand saw.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Then James tried riding with NO hands. He made it exactly three seconds before heading straight into the same bush.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At home time, Mum was waiting at the gate. She crouched down with an expectant look. "Well?" she said. They both started talking at exactly the same moment and didn't stop for ten minutes.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie was Dad's younger brother, and he was a wildlife researcher who had spent the last two years living near a tropical rainforest, studying primates. He had, apparently, brought one with him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: It started with the waistcoat hook being empty.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The school hall was full of projects — a volcano that erupted three times, a model solar system, a survey about favourite foods with real graphs. Betty looked at all of them carefully and said nothing. Aiden chewed the inside of his cheek.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Third place, with a commendation for experimental method, went to HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW? The commendation was on a proper certificate with a gold border. Betty read every word of it, twice.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Third place, with a commendation for experimental method, went to HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW? The commendation was on a proper certificate with a gold border. Betty read every word of it, twice.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Aiden had started a new notebook that evening — not the Socks field study, but a nature notebook. He had titled it with the date. Betty had started a matching one, without them discussing it. Both were already half a page in.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He told Betty. Betty got the torch and studied it with great interest. "It's definitely loose," she said. "It'll fall out and a permanent one will grow. That's much better, actually." Aiden was not entirely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Betty had the guide map. She navigated with precise efficiency — Great Hall, Armoury, North Tower, King's Chamber, Dungeon — the best order for minimum backtracking. Aiden followed behind her, reading every information board they passed, completely at home in a world of facts.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The drive home was quiet in the way that follows something large. "What are you thinking about?" said Mum. Aiden and Betty both answered at the same time, with completely different answers. "That," said Mum, "is exactly right."

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a leafy fan for Dozy. This is perfect, said Dozy, already asleep with it.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: They were the best gifts we ever had, said Sunny. Will you come and sit with us? Shy came out. Just a little way. But it was something.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: But dinosaurs do not nest in trees, said Flappy. You do, said Grumpy. And birds do not live in Sunny Hollow with everyone else. You do, said Grumpy.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Sneezy, dabbing with the handkerchief. Every leaf had fallen off every tree. Do not apologise, said Grumpy. For once, Grumpy was actually smiling.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Chompy. Hmph, said Grumpy. They sat on the rock together. Less peaceful with Chompy. But not actually terrible.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Fancy held a Best Sail competition. Fancy was the only one with a sail. Fancy gave themselves first prize. This seems fair, said Fancy.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip was walking through Moonwood when his foot kicked something small. It was a tiny stone. It glowed with a soft gold light.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: One morning, a new fish appeared. It was silver with a bright blue stripe. Dewdrop had never seen a fish like it.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Can fish lie? Dewdrop asked Burrow. Some of them can, said Burrow. Which fish? The new one with the blue stripe, said Dewdrop. Burrow had not seen a new fish.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: You are interesting, said Dewdrop. You are the only fish in this stream with a blue stripe. The fish looked at its own stripe. That is true, it said.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: He polished his glasses and looked more closely. On the door was a small carving. A tree with roots going in every direction. It was very old.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: This was the problem with forgetting things. You couldn't always remember what you had forgotten. Luna knew it was important. She knew it was today.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it something to do with the Crystal Stream? asked Dewdrop. Luna stopped walking. She looked at the stream for a moment. Wait, said Luna.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: She opened the box. Inside were twelve small seeds. Each one glowed with a soft gold light. Oh, said Fern, very quietly.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it with water.
She pushed as hard as she could.
The boulder did not move.
"I am not strong enough," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern tried to push with her hands.
The boulder did not move.
Fern stepped back and thought.
"We need each other," said Fern.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow went up to find Luna.
"Come with me," he said.
"Bring a light."
Luna said nothing.
She came.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Burrow bumped the bench.
It fell over.
Burrow kept walking.
He found Pip's door.
He moved the boots with his paws.
He did not wake up.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern's garden was her favourite place.
One morning, Wren arrived with a cauldron.
"I have a potion," said Wren.
"It will help your plants."

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip noticed it on a Tuesday.
The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Moonwood blazed with gold.
Every mushroom.
Every lamp.
Every glowing stone.
The forest was more beautiful than anyone had ever seen it.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip brought it inside.
Everyone woke up.
Stone brought a piece of acorn biscuit.
The creature ate it very carefully.
It watched everyone with its large silver eyes.

uses.title: Farm Animals
uses.pageText:
This is a pig.
Oink, oink!

uses.title: Farm Animals
uses.pageText:
This is a hen.
Cluck, cluck!

uses.title: Farm Animals
uses.pageText:
This is a big cow.
Moo, moo!

uses.title: Farm Animals
uses.pageText:
This is a dog.
Woof, woof!

uses.title: Farm Animals
uses.pageText:
This is a duck.
Quack, quack!

uses.title: Farm Animals
uses.pageText:
This is a cat.
Meow!

uses.title: Farm Animals
uses.pageText:
This is a farm!
So many animals.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is spring. Flowers pop up. Birds sing.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is summer. The sun is hot. It is a sunny day.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is autumn. Leaves go red and gold. Leaves fall down.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is winter. It is cold. Snow falls.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: This is a seed. It is tiny. Seeds come in many shapes.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: This is big. An elephant is big.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: This is small. A mouse is small.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: Sometimes it is a full circle. This is a full moon.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: This is called pollination. Without bees, many plants could not make seeds. No seeds means no fruits or vegetables. We need bees very much.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Deep underground, rock gets so hot that it melts. This melted rock is called magma. Magma is hotter than anything you can imagine.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can seem frightening. But they have helped shape our planet. They make new land, rich soil and even new islands. They have been doing this for billions of years.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans. This causes the tides. When the tide comes in, the sea rises up the beach. When it goes out, it pulls back.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Plants use sunlight, water, and air to make food. This is called photosynthesis. It also makes the oxygen we breathe. Plants feed us and give us air!

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: When an insect is caught, the spider wraps it in silk. This keeps it still. Then the spider injects venom to begin digesting its meal.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: In the deepest, darkest water, some creatures make their own light. This is called bioluminescence. The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure to attract prey.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: A butterfly's life has four stages. This is called a lifecycle. Each stage looks completely different from the one before.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage three: the caterpillar makes a hard shell around itself. This is called a chrysalis. Inside, an extraordinary change is about to happen.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Most caves form when rainwater seeps into limestone rock. The water is slightly acidic. It slowly dissolves the rock away. This takes thousands and thousands of years.

uses.title: Bob and Nan
uses.pageText: This is Bob.

uses.title: Bob and Nan
uses.pageText: This is Nan.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: James and Anna climbed up and sat at the little window. "This is the best thing we have ever made," said Anna.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He loves shiny objects," Uncle Eddie explained at dinner. "He adores warm spots — the airing cupboard is a particular risk. And if he gets bored, he will find a way to become interesting." Everyone filed this information away carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Mum said it was completely normal and that they had both lost teeth before when they were smaller — Aiden had even eaten one inside a peanut butter sandwich and not noticed for an hour. Aiden was not certain this was reassuring.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Socks was fascinated by both of them through this whole period. He kept trying to look in their mouths. He seemed to find it deeply interesting, which Aiden added to the field notebook under: Primate-specific dental curiosity — possible.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The dungeon was underground and smelled of cold stone and old air. Betty read every board by torchlight. Aiden stood still in the near-dark for a moment and thought about how this exact place had been here through everything — and felt briefly, appropriately small.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: Hmph, said Grumpy. This is... not terrible.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Oh, said Zippy. This is... nice. Zippy sat down. Zippy had never sat down before.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a leafy fan for Dozy. This is perfect, said Dozy, already asleep with it.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: I cannot leave the cave, said Fancy. Not like this. Fancy sat very still and stared at the cave wall.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Honky offered to shout at it until it moved. Everyone agreed this would make things much worse.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Has anyone seen my pillow? said Dozy. Dozy had been looking for it all morning. This was serious.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried nesting in a tree. This part actually worked quite well. Flappy was surprised.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried eating leaves. Fine. Flappy tried catching insects mid-air. Remarkably good at this. Flappy was more surprised.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: This will take all day, said Grumpy. Hmph. Everyone sat down feeling stuck.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: This is a leaf, said Grumpy. I know, said Chompy. It is a good leaf.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: This is a pebble, said Grumpy. I am not eating the pebble, said Chompy. Glad to hear it, said Grumpy.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: This is a good rock, said Chompy. Yes, said Grumpy. Is there anything to eat near it? said Chompy. Grumpy pointed at the berry patch. Chompy went happily.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Fancy held a Best Sail competition. Fancy was the only one with a sail. Fancy gave themselves first prize. This seems fair, said Fancy.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Chompy was there, but all the food was made of more clouds. This is disappointing, said Dream Chompy.
