They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: At the very end, everyone stood and clapped. James and Anna walked to the front of the stage and bowed together.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He loves shiny objects," Uncle Eddie explained at dinner. "He adores warm spots — the airing cupboard is a particular risk. And if he gets bored, he will find a way to become interesting." Everyone filed this information away carefully.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: It was morning in Sunny Hollow. Everyone was up. Everyone except Dozy.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: It was morning in Sunny Hollow. Everyone was up. Everyone except Dozy.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Everyone got to work. Chompy ate the berries. Chompy! said Bossy.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Honky offered to shout at it until it moved. Everyone agreed this would make things much worse.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Everyone searched. Bouncy bounced into every corner. Zippy ran everywhere twice. Cheeky looked in all the hiding spots. Nothing.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Not from where I am standing, said Clumsy. Everyone looked up.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: How did it get there? said Grumpy. Everyone looked at Bouncy. I bounced past it, said Bouncy. SORRY.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: But dinosaurs do not nest in trees, said Flappy. You do, said Grumpy. And birds do not live in Sunny Hollow with everyone else. You do, said Grumpy.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: We need to move those rocks, said Bossy. Everyone tried pushing. The rocks did not move at all.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: This will take all day, said Grumpy. Hmph. Everyone sat down feeling stuck.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Everyone move back, said Grumpy. They moved back.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: I have an announcement! called Bossy, megaphone raised. We are having the First Sunny Hollow Games. Tomorrow. Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dream Bouncy bounced so high that Bouncy went above the clouds and kept going. Everyone watched. Nobody was surprised.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Storm coming, said Grumpy. Big one. Grumpy was almost always right about weather. Everyone believed Grumpy.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose could smell the rain from far away. Twenty minutes, said Sneezy. Maybe fifteen. Everyone moved faster.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Wiggly's long tail swept the Big Flat Rock clear in seconds. Food, supplies, anything that could blow away. Sorry, said Wiggly, sweeping everything. This time everyone was grateful.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Shy, who knew every hidden corner of the Fernwood, led everyone to the deepest part of Cozy Cave. Shy knew exactly where it was warmest.

uses.title: Bouncy Won't Stop
uses.pageText:
"Stop!" said everyone.
Hop. Hop. Hop.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: "SURPRISE!" said everyone.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "Shh!" said everyone.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "Shh!" said everyone.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "SHH!" said everyone.

uses.title: Noisy Wakes Everyone Up
uses.pageText: It is dark. Everyone is asleep.

uses.title: Noisy Wakes Everyone Up
uses.pageText: "NOISY!" said everyone.

uses.title: Grumpy's Secret
uses.pageText: Tiny told everyone.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Everyone is at the party.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Everyone is happy.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By afternoon, the plant had grown through the roof. It was still growing. Everyone stood back and watched.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: There was a rope bridge over the Crystal Stream. Everyone crossed it without thinking. Everyone except Stone.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: There was a rope bridge over the Crystal Stream. Everyone crossed it without thinking. Everyone except Stone.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint pinned the first map up inside the Hollow Oak. It was very beautiful. Everyone agreed it was the best wrong map they had ever seen.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: I have found something, Burrow told everyone. They gathered at the Hollow Oak. A door, said Burrow, underground. Very old. I don't know what is inside.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow opened the door. A warm golden light came from inside. Everyone leaned forward.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark breathed in carefully. I think, he said, I might need to sneeze again. Everyone took a large step back.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Everyone helped. They checked the Hollow Oak from top to bottom. They walked the paths. They looked in the Whispering Meadow. Nothing triggered the memory.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Back at the Hollow Oak, everyone asked:
"What was the loud thing?"
"Very small," said Pip.
"Very loud," said Stone.
They both smiled.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the Hollow Oak, everyone heard it.
"The stream is singing again!" said Pip.
"We just moved a stone," said Fern.
"And asked the water nicely," said Dewdrop.
"It did the rest."

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
The next night, it happened again.
More things had moved.
"Was it you?" asked Stone.
"No," said Pip.
"Was it you?" asked Pip.
"No," said everyone.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna called everyone together.
"The seeds keep Moonwood glowing," she said.
"Without them, the forest will grow dark."
Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna called everyone together.
"The seeds keep Moonwood glowing," she said.
"Without them, the forest will grow dark."
Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
It was late in the Hollow Oak.
Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Halfway through, everyone was somewhere different.
Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
They marked the boundary at the Hollow Oak.
Everyone placed a stone.
"The marsh is the marsh," said Luna.
"Moonwood is Moonwood."
"And we leave space for both."

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
There was a sign on the Hollow Oak door.
GLIMMER'S FIRE PERFORMANCE — TODAY.
Everyone came.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone looked at the forest.
Then everyone looked at Glimmer.
Glimmer looked at the forest.
Glimmer looked at their own mouth.
"Oh," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone looked at the forest.
Then everyone looked at Glimmer.
Glimmer looked at the forest.
Glimmer looked at their own mouth.
"Oh," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip brought it inside.
Everyone woke up.
Stone brought a piece of acorn biscuit.
The creature ate it very carefully.
It watched everyone with its large silver eyes.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip brought it inside.
Everyone woke up.
Stone brought a piece of acorn biscuit.
The creature ate it very carefully.
It watched everyone with its large silver eyes.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
"We'll take you home," said Pip.
"But the Deep Dark—" said Wren.
"We'll go together," said Pip.
Everyone looked at each other.
"Together," said Stone.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is rainy. Drops fall from the clouds. Drip, drip, drip.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: Rain falls from the clouds. Drip, drip, drip.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: The female emperor penguin lays one egg. The father balances it on his feet and covers it with a warm flap of skin. He keeps it safe from the freezing cold.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks small from Earth, but it is very large. It is about a quarter the size of our whole planet. If Earth were a basketball, the Moon would be a tennis ball.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Seeds travel away from the parent plant. Some fly on the wind. Some stick to animals' fur. Some are eaten by birds and fall far away. Some float on water.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean makes more than half the oxygen we breathe. Tiny plants called phytoplankton float near the surface. They use sunlight to make oxygen. Every other breath you take came from the ocean.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: A butterfly's life has four stages. This is called a lifecycle. Each stage looks completely different from the one before.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Some butterflies migrate thousands of kilometres. The monarch butterfly flies from Canada to Mexico every year — a journey of 4,000 kilometres. They always find the same trees.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are home to many animals. Bats sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings by day. At dusk, thousands of bats fly out together to feed on insects in the night air.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips had a blue bell on his collar. JINGLE! JINGLE! JINGLE! You could hear him coming from far away!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James made Chips a lead from a long piece of rope. Now Chips could come on walks!

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Mum sent up a tray of juice and biscuits on a rope. Dad waved from below. Chips jangled at the base of the tree, trying to reach the biscuits.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna found the duck pond. Three white ducks swam in slow circles. One waddled right up and ate seeds from Anna's hand.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: That evening, Grandma made soup from the garden and fried the eggs James had found. It was the best meal they had ever tasted.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "Next year," said James, "we camp in a real field." "Next year," said Mum from the doorway, "Chips stays home." Chips ate the tent door zip.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They had set up a lemonade stand beside the sale table — Betty's idea, planned the previous Thursday. Aiden poured from a glass jug. Betty collected the money and kept the queue moving. By one o'clock they had sold every cup and run entirely out of lemons.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The view from the top was unlike anything Aiden had seen. The whole coastline curved away in both directions — bays and headlands, a small fishing village far below, and the sea stretching to the horizon, catching the light like crinkled silver foil.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "Socks!" said Aiden and Betty. Socks examined the jar from every angle, turning it slowly. He handed it back eventually — and the crystals were, miraculously, completely intact.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Shy! said Sunny, softly. The gifts are from you, aren't they? Shy nodded, going very pink.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Clumsy looked in from a great height. It looks fine to me, said Clumsy. You cannot even see your own feet, said Fancy.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly fetched water from the waterfall very carefully. The tail only knocked over two things. Sorry, said Wiggly.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Not from where I am standing, said Clumsy. Everyone looked up.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy had been very quiet. Sneezy could feel something building. High up. In the pollen from the ferns.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: I can see everything from here, said Dream Dozy. We can always see everything, said Dream Sunny. You just need to be up high enough. Dozy thought about this.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Clumsy stood tall and looked out over the whole Hollow. The storm is coming from the east, said Clumsy. The tall ferns are already bending. That gives us time.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose could smell the rain from far away. Twenty minutes, said Sneezy. Maybe fifteen. Everyone moved faster.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: When it passed, Sunny Hollow sparkled. We did that, said Sunny. All of us. Not bad, said Grumpy. From Grumpy, that meant wonderful.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Burrow appeared from a nearby tunnel. "That is a Bravery Stone," said Burrow. "Whoever holds it will feel brave."

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow opened the door. A warm golden light came from inside. Everyone leaned forward.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Everyone helped. They checked the Hollow Oak from top to bottom. They walked the paths. They looked in the Whispering Meadow. Nothing triggered the memory.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: They planted the seeds in a ring around the Hollow Oak. One from each of them. In the golden afternoon light.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip and Stone were sitting outside the Hollow Oak.
Then a noise came from the Fog Marsh.
It was very, very loud.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Stone stood up and called out across the marsh.
It was the loudest sound Pip had ever heard.
Louder than the toadling.
Much louder.
Something answered from the far side of the marsh.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
"The song comes from the source," said Dewdrop.
"We must follow the stream up."
Fern looked at the deep forest ahead.
"Then we go," said Fern.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern went to the middle of the clearing.
She closed her eyes.
She sang.
Very softly.
The same song from long ago.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Pip reached the Crystal Stream.
He leaped from stone to stone.
One stone was slippery.
Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A snail has a shell on its back. A snail moves very slowly.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: The father does not eat for two months. He huddles with other fathers to stay warm. Meanwhile, the mother goes to the sea to find fish. She will bring food back when the egg hatches.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans. This causes the tides. When the tide comes in, the sea rises up the beach. When it goes out, it pulls back.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The astronauts brought Moon rocks back to Earth. Scientists are still studying them today. Moon rocks help us understand how the Solar System was formed.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Slowly, the tadpole changes. Back legs appear first. Then front legs. The tail shrinks away. After about twelve weeks, it is a frog!

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs are expert hunters. They have long, sticky tongues. A frog can flip its tongue out and back in less time than a blink to catch an insect.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "It is the best rocket ever made!" said James. He and Anna stood back and grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Time to go home," said Anna. "Come back soon!" called Zim, and he waved and waved.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: BUMP! They were back in the garden. Mum had made cake. "Best trip EVER!" they said.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna set off nice and slowly. She did not wobble. She did not crash. She rode all the way to the end of the path and back.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: By lunchtime, they could both ride all the way down the long lane and back without stopping once.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Dad put up a big green tent in the back garden. "We are going camping!" he said. "Just for one night."

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "What if it comes back?" said James. "Then we will scare it," said Anna. She picked up the air horn Dad had packed.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "Socks!" said Aiden and Betty. Socks examined the jar from every angle, turning it slowly. He handed it back eventually — and the crystals were, miraculously, completely intact.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The far bank was different — thicker trees, softer ground, a field of tall meadow grass beyond the treeline. Socks bounded ahead, turning back every few steps to make sure they were following.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: The sun came back out. See? said Sunny. Every day is a good day!

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy ran to the waterfall. Zippy ran back. Zippy ran to the meadow. Zippy ran back.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy ran to the waterfall. Zippy ran back. Zippy ran to the meadow. Zippy ran back.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked off. BOING! Wiggly bounced back. My tail is stuck! HEE HEE HEE! said Cheeky.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Dozy offered a pillow. It needs weight, not softness, said Fancy. Dozy went back to sleep.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy went back to the tree. Got three wing-flaps up. Landed neatly on a branch. Sat very high up and looked at all of Sunny Hollow below. Oh, said Flappy quietly. That is quite good actually.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Everyone move back, said Grumpy. They moved back.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Everyone move back, said Grumpy. They moved back.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: AAAAAAACHOOOOOO! The sneeze hit the rocks like a wave. Rocks scattered in every direction. The stream burst free. The waterfall roared back. A rainbow appeared.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Back in the meadow, Dozy's eyes opened. All the Dino Pals were sitting in a circle, waiting. What was it like? said Sunny.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Zippy ran back and forth collecting everything needed before anyone could finish asking. Twelve trips in four minutes. Done, said Zippy.

uses.title: Sleepy Can't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Sleepy went back to bed.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: They went back home.

uses.title: Sleepy's Big Dream
uses.pageText: Sleepy went back to sleep.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat at the back.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By afternoon, the plant had grown through the roof. It was still growing. Everyone stood back and watched.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They crossed back together. Stone did not look at the water. Stone looked at the far end of the bridge. One step, then another.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: There was another flash of blue. Wren was back to her normal size. She brushed off her robe. She straightened her hat.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop went back to the Crystal Stream. Why do you say things that are not true? she asked. She said it kindly. She just wanted to know.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: The fish was quiet for a while. It swam a small, slow circle. Then it came back. Because I am new here, said the fish. And I wanted to sound interesting.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: What is the fish called? asked Pip. I... said Dewdrop. She stopped. She had forgotten to ask. She turned back toward the water.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Every fish in the stream turned purple. The water sang in a different key. One fish turned into a frog for a moment, and then turned back.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: The remedy worked. Spark's cold was gone. The flowers slowly turned back to their usual colours. The fish returned to normal.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark breathed in carefully. I think, he said, I might need to sneeze again. Everyone took a large step back.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip walked toward the Fog Marsh.
He looked back.
Stone had not moved.
Stone had moved one foot.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Back at the Hollow Oak, everyone asked:
"What was the loud thing?"
"Very small," said Pip.
"Very loud," said Stone.
They both smiled.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern tried to push with her hands.
The boulder did not move.
Fern stepped back and thought.
"We need each other," said Fern.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"Why didn't we try that first?" asked Flint.
"I don't know," said Wren.
She looked back at the mushroom trail.
"They seemed happy about it though."
The last mushroom blinked once and went out.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants slowed.
The far ones turned.
They walked back.
Slowly.
Like sleepy creatures going home.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Everything was back.
"I'm sorry," said Wren.
"Did you learn something?" asked Fern.
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
That evening, the fog stayed at the line.
The mushrooms began to come back on.
One by one.
Pip watched them light up.
The marsh was where it should be.
The forest was where it should be.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: The sun goes down.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText:
The tree has roots.
They go down.

uses.title: A Seed Grows
uses.pageText: A root grows down in the soil.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText:
The sun goes down.
The sky turns red.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is autumn. Leaves go red and gold. Leaves fall down.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Put the seed in soil. Pat it down gently.

uses.title: Hot and Cold
uses.pageText: Hot food can burn. Let it cool down first.

uses.title: Hello, Sun!
uses.pageText: In the evening, the sun goes down. Goodnight, sun!

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: After a volcano, the cooled lava becomes new rock. Volcanic rock breaks down into rich, dark soil. Many plants and crops grow very well in volcanic soil.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean has different layers. Near the surface, there is plenty of sunlight and warmth. Further down, it grows colder and darker. Below 200 metres, no sunlight reaches at all.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Further down, in the deep and dark, strange creatures live. Many have enormous eyes to see in the dim light. Some are found nowhere else on Earth.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are home to many animals. Bats sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings by day. At dusk, thousands of bats fly out together to feed on insects in the night air.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They set off down the lane. Chips trotted along and stopped to munch the long grass at the sides.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: Anna found a book about sharks on the shelf. She sat down and read and read. She forgot to feel scared.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "James!" called the dentist. He stood up. He walked in. The big chair went up and down like a ride!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James came out. "It did not hurt at all!" he said. "And the chair goes UP and DOWN!" Anna laughed.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the day of try-outs, James roared so loud that Mrs. Green's glasses slid right down her nose. He got the part!

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mrs. Chen stood at the garden gate and laughed so hard that she had to sit down on the grass.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: At last, both Chips and Bella lay down on the lawn side by side, panting. Chips licked Bella's ear. Bella licked Chips's nose.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: By lunchtime, they could both ride all the way down the long lane and back without stopping once.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Dad got his old bike out and the three of them went for a long ride down to the duck pond.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At home time, Mum was waiting at the gate. She crouched down with an expectant look. "Well?" she said. They both started talking at exactly the same moment and didn't stop for ten minutes.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Aiden spent the whole first morning at a rock pool near the headland. He found three kinds of crab, a sea anemone that closed when you touched it, and a tiny fish he thought might be a blenny. He wrote everything down in his field notebook in careful columns.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Through the binoculars, Betty saw a kingfisher — a bright impossible dart of blue-orange above the water, there and then gone. She had to put the binoculars down and close her eyes for a moment. She had seen it. She wrote it in the log book.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Oh, said Zippy. This is... nice. Zippy sat down. Zippy had never sat down before.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Oh, said Zippy. This is... nice. Zippy sat down. Zippy had never sat down before.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Next: Cheeky put mud on Fancy's favourite rock. Fancy sat down. OH! cried Fancy.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried roaring like the other dinosaurs. A small squawk came out. Some feathers drifted down.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: This will take all day, said Grumpy. Hmph. Everyone sat down feeling stuck.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText: Cuddly sat down by the barn.

uses.title: Speedy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Speedy sits down.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: Cuddly sat down.

uses.title: Muddy and Splashy Make a Mess
uses.pageText: The mud went down.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat down. Woolly sat down.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat down. Woolly sat down.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: Fern sat down and thought. Spells had made it grow. But a growing thing needed something different.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone reached the other side. Stone reached down and picked up Burrow very carefully. "Oh, thank you," said Burrow. "I was going in circles."

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer sat down. "I will never breathe fire," said Glimmer. "I have tried every day and it is never fire."

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint sat down on a mossy rock. He looked at the map for a long time. It was very beautiful. It was also completely wrong.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow was digging a new tunnel. He dug down, and he dug sideways, and he dug carefully around the roots. Then his spade hit something hard and wooden.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow set down his spade. He felt around it very carefully. It was a door. A small, very old wooden door, deep underground.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna flew to the Crystal Stream. She landed on a stepping stone. She looked down into the water.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Stone knelt down carefully.
"We will help," said Stone.
The toadling looked at Stone.
"You are very large," said the toadling.
"Yes," said Stone. "But I am gentle."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer tried.
Smoke came out.
Just smoke.
"Interesting," said Spark, and wrote things down.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark put down his wand.
He put down his notes.
He stood very still.
He stopped thinking.
A small real flame came.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark put down his wand.
He put down his notes.
He stood very still.
He stopped thinking.
A small real flame came.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Flint opened his satchel.
Seven maps fell out.
One was of the coast.
One was upside down.
None of them were quite right.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They sat down under a large mushroom.
They were tired.
They were lost.
The mushroom glowed cheerfully.
Wren looked at it.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then Burrow sat down.
Against the big mushroom.
Pip and Glimmer were still behind it.
Burrow began to snore.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
"Just your arm," said Dewdrop.
"Just the one arm."
"Just for a moment."
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the water.
Stone sat down on the bank.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Fern stopped.
She knelt down.
There were small green shoots in the ground.
They glowed.
Just a little.
Just like the seeds.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip knelt down.
He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: Five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. I use them every day!

uses.title: Staying Healthy
uses.pageText: Brush your teeth. Brush them twice a day.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Pebbles are small, smooth rocks. Water makes them smooth.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Most volcanoes are quiet for a very long time. Scientists called volcanologists watch them carefully. They use special equipment to spot the signs of an eruption.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The astronauts brought Moon rocks back to Earth. Scientists are still studying them today. Moon rocks help us understand how the Solar System was formed.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James ran to see the hens. "They have laid five eggs!" he said. He put them one by one — very, very carefully — into a basket.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Dad got his old bike out and the three of them went for a long ride down to the duck pond.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The school hall was full of projects — a volcano that erupted three times, a model solar system, a survey about favourite foods with real graphs. Betty looked at all of them carefully and said nothing. Aiden chewed the inside of his cheek.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Aiden had started a new notebook that evening — not the Socks field study, but a nature notebook. He had titled it with the date. Betty had started a matching one, without them discussing it. Both were already half a page in.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Socks was fascinated by both of them through this whole period. He kept trying to look in their mouths. He seemed to find it deeply interesting, which Aiden added to the field notebook under: Primate-specific dental curiosity — possible.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the armoury, there was a full suit of plate armour. It was smaller than Aiden expected. The guide told them that real knights were roughly the same size as Dad, which was very hard to imagine. Aiden tried on a gauntlet under supervision. His hand barely fit inside.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky had an idea. Cheeky always had ideas. Most of them were pranks.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Every morning, the Dino Pals found a small gift on the Big Flat Rock. Nobody knew who left them.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a pile of extra berries for Chompy. Someone knows me very well, said Chompy, already eating them.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: The tidiest corner prize went to Shy. Shy had arranged twelve perfect pebbles behind a rock where nobody could see them. It counts, said Bossy carefully.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dream Grumpy was grumpy about the clouds. They are too soft. I cannot sit on them properly. Dream Grumpy was exactly the same as real Grumpy.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: It was exactly like this, said Dozy, looking at all of them, but cloudier. Dozy's eyes closed again. Wake me for supper.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Both of them are happy.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop knew every fish in the Crystal Stream. She talked to them every morning. They told her things: where the water was cold, where the best pebbles were.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Can fish lie? Dewdrop asked Burrow. Some of them can, said Burrow. Which fish? The new one with the blue stripe, said Dewdrop. Burrow had not seen a new fish.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Spark. The flowers looked at him. He looked at them. His nose twitched again.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Spark. This was his third sorry. He meant all three of them very much.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna gave one to each creature. One for each of them. The seeds glowed gently in their hands. Plant them this afternoon, said Luna.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna gave one to each creature. One for each of them. The seeds glowed gently in their hands. Plant them this afternoon, said Luna.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: They planted the seeds in a ring around the Hollow Oak. One from each of them. In the golden afternoon light.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
The toadling stopped when it saw them.
Everything was suddenly very quiet.
"Oh," said Pip.
"Oh," said Stone.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the first day, Spark explained fire.
He drew many diagrams.
The diagrams were very complicated.
Glimmer did not understand any of them.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the third day, the diagrams had multiplied.
There were charts about heat.
Charts about breathing.
Charts about dragon anatomy.
Glimmer stared at them all.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Flint opened his satchel.
Seven maps fell out.
One was of the coast.
One was upside down.
None of them were quite right.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"This is the Memory Room," said Luna.
"This is where Moonwood keeps its oldest stories."
Burrow looked at the carvings.
"All of them?" he asked.
"All of them," said Luna.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"This is the Memory Room," said Luna.
"This is where Moonwood keeps its oldest stories."
Burrow looked at the carvings.
"All of them?" he asked.
"All of them," said Luna.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
One morning, things had moved in the night.
Pip's boots were not where he had left them.
A bench was tipped over.
Someone had been in the clearing.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren poured the potion on the plants.
The plants stood very straight.
Then they leaned.
Then one of them took a step.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
The magic seeds were gone.
The box that held them was open and empty.
Luna looked at the box for a long time.
"This is not good," she said.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna called everyone together.
"The seeds keep Moonwood glowing," she said.
"Without them, the forest will grow dark."
Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They gathered the star spirits.
There were many of them.
Stone held several.
Wren had two in her hat.
They kept bouncing.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
It was late in the Hollow Oak.
Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Inside the marsh, it was colder.
The trees drooped.
The water did not move.
Dewdrop led them through the fog.
She could feel the water.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
That evening, the fog stayed at the line.
The mushrooms began to come back on.
One by one.
Pip watched them light up.
The marsh was where it should be.
The forest was where it should be.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The creature ran to its family.
The family gathered around it.
They looked at the Moonwood creatures.
Not afraid.
Just looking.
Then one of them blinked.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two eyes.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two ears.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have one nose.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have one mouth.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two hands.

uses.title: Reptiles
uses.pageText: Reptiles have dry skin.

uses.title: Reptiles
uses.pageText: Turtles have a hard shell.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have two eyes.
I can see.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have two ears.
I can hear.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have a nose.
I can smell.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have a mouth.
I can eat.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have two hands.
I can clap!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have two feet.
I can run!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have a body!
I love my body.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Trees have roots under the soil. Roots hold the tree up.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A fish has fins. Fins help fish swim. Fish have scales.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A butterfly has four wings. Its wings have bright patterns.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: People have been to the moon! They wore big white suits.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: The Earth spins around. That is why we have day and night.

uses.title: My Five Senses
