uses.pageText: I have five senses. They help me know the world.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have a head. I have a face. I can smile!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have a head. I have a face. I can smile!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two arms. I have two hands. I can clap!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two arms. I have two hands. I can clap!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have a tummy. Food goes into my tummy. Rumble!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two legs. I have two feet. I can kick and run!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two legs. I have two feet. I can kick and run!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have eyes to see. I have ears to hear. I have a nose to smell.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have eyes to see. I have ears to hear. I have a nose to smell.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have eyes to see. I have ears to hear. I have a nose to smell.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Famous volcanoes can be found all around the world. Iceland, Hawaii and Italy all have active volcanoes. Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can seem frightening. But they have helped shape our planet. They make new land, rich soil and even new islands. They have been doing this for billions of years.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can seem frightening. But they have helped shape our planet. They make new land, rich soil and even new islands. They have been doing this for billions of years.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins live in large groups called colonies. Some colonies have hundreds of thousands of penguins! Each penguin recognises its partner and its chick by their call.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders are not insects. Insects have six legs. Spiders have eight legs. They belong to a group called arachnids.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders are not insects. Insects have six legs. Spiders have eight legs. They belong to a group called arachnids.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Some spiders do not use webs at all. Jumping spiders leap onto their food. They have big eyes that face forward to judge distance. A jumping spider can leap 20 times its own body length!

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders have eight eyes, but many cannot see well. Instead, they feel vibrations through their legs. When something touches the web, the spider feels it instantly.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Further down, in the deep and dark, strange creatures live. Many have enormous eyes to see in the dim light. Some are found nowhere else on Earth.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies are insects. Like all insects, they have six legs, four wings, and a body in three parts. They also have two long antennae.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies are insects. Like all insects, they have six legs, four wings, and a body in three parts. They also have two long antennae.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: After a few weeks, tadpoles wriggle out of the eggs. Tadpoles have tails and no legs. They breathe underwater using gills, like fish.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs are expert hunters. They have long, sticky tongues. A frog can flip its tongue out and back in less time than a blink to catch an insect.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: James and Anna climbed up and sat at the little window. "This is the best thing we have ever made," said Anna.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James ran to see the hens. "They have laid five eggs!" he said. He put them one by one — very, very carefully — into a basket.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James put his hand straight up. "I want to be the dragon!" Six other children put their hands up too. They would all have to try out.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden wrote in his notebook: When something is unfair, you have two choices — pretend it isn't happening, or decide what to do. He starred the second option. He didn't quite know yet what doing something looked like.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: We have a problem, said Bossy. We need Dozy for the picnic!

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Listen up! called Bossy. I have a plan!

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Honky, said Bossy, you need an inside voice. What is an inside voice? A quiet one. I do not have one of those.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: I should be able to fly, said Flappy. I have wings. You are also a dinosaur, said Grumpy. Dinosaurs do not fly.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: I have an announcement! called Bossy, megaphone raised. We are having the First Sunny Hollow Games. Tomorrow. Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: There would be a running race, a jumping contest, a loudness competition, and a prize for the tidiest corner of the Hollow. More events to be decided, said Bossy. I have a clipboard.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer sat down. "I will never breathe fire," said Glimmer. "I have tried every day and it is never fire."

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: I have been here longer than the Hollow Oak, said the fish. Dewdrop looked carefully. The fish was, if anything, quite new-looking. I know all the secrets of the Deep Dark, the fish added.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: I have found something, Burrow told everyone. They gathered at the Hollow Oak. A door, said Burrow, underground. Very old. I don't know what is inside.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They arrived at the Whispering Meadow.
It was exactly where they had been going.
Flint wrote something on his map.
"Mushroom trail," he said.
"I should have had that already."

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"Have you been here before?" asked Burrow.
"Yes," said Luna.
She looked around the room.
"A very long time ago."
"What is it?" asked Burrow.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern's garden was her favourite place.
One morning, Wren arrived with a cauldron.
"I have a potion," said Wren.
"It will help your plants."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"Hello," said Fern.
The tiny creature looked up.
"Have you seen my spectacles?" she said.
"I've been looking for three days."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"I am Twig," said the tiny creature.
"I live here."
"I have always lived here."
She seemed perfectly happy about this.

uses.title: Bob and Nan
uses.pageText: Bob and Nan sat.

uses.title: Bob, Nan and Fluff
uses.pageText: Bob and Nan sat in the sun.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: Anna found a book about sharks on the shelf. She sat down and read and read. She forgot to feel scared.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: James and Anna climbed up and sat at the little window. "This is the best thing we have ever made," said Anna.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: The summer holidays were over at last. Aiden sat on his bed and stared at his new school bag. Grade 1. The words sounded bigger than they looked.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden added a new page to his field notebook: WHAT MAKES A GOOD EXPERIMENT. He had six points. Socks sat on the desk and watched him write, which Aiden had never seen him do before.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden didn't say anything. He went home and sat on his bed and stared at the ceiling. He wasn't crying, but he wasn't fine either. He didn't really want to talk about it — which Betty noticed immediately.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly sat very, very still. The tail still knocked over three berries and a leaf.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Oh, said Zippy. This is... nice. Zippy sat down. Zippy had never sat down before.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Oh, said Zippy. This is... nice. Zippy sat down. Zippy had never sat down before.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Next: Cheeky put mud on Fancy's favourite rock. Fancy sat down. OH! cried Fancy.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: I cannot leave the cave, said Fancy. Not like this. Fancy sat very still and stared at the cave wall.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy went back to the tree. Got three wing-flaps up. Landed neatly on a branch. Sat very high up and looked at all of Sunny Hollow below. Oh, said Flappy quietly. That is quite good actually.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: This will take all day, said Grumpy. Hmph. Everyone sat down feeling stuck.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: They reached the meadow. Grumpy found the flat rock and sat on it. Chompy found a berry patch immediately.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat. It was the right temperature. The right shape. Grumpy almost smiled.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Chompy. Hmph, said Grumpy. They sat on the rock together. Less peaceful with Chompy. But not actually terrible.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: Woolly Can't Sleep
uses.pageText: Woolly sat up.

uses.title: Woolly Can't Sleep
uses.pageText: Woolly sat up.

uses.title: Woolly Can't Sleep
uses.pageText: Woolly sat up.

uses.title: Clucky Lays an Egg
uses.pageText:
She sat in the nest.
"Not yet," said Clucky.

uses.title: Clucky Lays an Egg
uses.pageText:
She sat on the log.
"Not yet," said Clucky.

uses.title: Clucky Lays an Egg
uses.pageText:
She sat in the box.
"Not yet," said Clucky.

uses.title: Clucky Lays an Egg
uses.pageText:
She sat on the hat.
"Not yet!" said Clucky.

uses.title: Clucky Lays an Egg
uses.pageText: She sat in the mud.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: Then a bug sat on Noisy.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText: Cuddly sat down by the barn.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText: Shy sat next to Cuddly.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: Cuddly sat down.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: They sat in the big tree.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat down. Woolly sat down.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat down. Woolly sat down.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat at the back.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: That evening, Pip sat by the Crystal Stream. He looked at the stone. The gold glow had gone out.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: Fern sat down and thought. Spells had made it grow. But a growing thing needed something different.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer sat down. "I will never breathe fire," said Glimmer. "I have tried every day and it is never fire."

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint sat down on a mossy rock. He looked at the map for a long time. It was very beautiful. It was also completely wrong.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna woke up knowing she had forgotten something important. She sat on her branch. She thought very hard. She could not remember what it was.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They sat down under a large mushroom.
They were tired.
They were lost.
The mushroom glowed cheerfully.
Wren looked at it.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow sat very still and listened.
The room grew warmer.
The carvings lit up one by one.
Luna's voice was quiet and certain.
She had always known these stories.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then Burrow sat down.
Against the big mushroom.
Pip and Glimmer were still behind it.
Burrow began to snore.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
"Just your arm," said Dewdrop.
"Just the one arm."
"Just for a moment."
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the water.
Stone sat down on the bank.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Stone sat and dripped.
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the rest of Stone.
"The fish is free," said Stone.
"Yes," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
They sat by the stream together.
Stone dripped for a long time.
The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.
And meant it.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
At the centre of the marsh, they found it.
A figure made of grey mist.
It sat against a dead tree.
It was very still.
It looked very sad.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
They all sat in the clearing.
Glimmer stood at the front.
It was very quiet.
"Ready," said Glimmer.
It did not quite feel true.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText:
Stars are far away.
There are so many.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: There are thousands of kinds of bees. The honeybee is one of the most helpful bees in the world.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: There are 18 species of penguin. Not all live in cold places. Little blue penguins live in Australia. African penguins live on warm, sunny beaches. Every kind of penguin is remarkable.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: You can see the Moon most nights. On a clear night with a telescope, you can see the craters clearly. Look up tonight — the Moon is always there.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean has different layers. Near the surface, there is plenty of sunlight and warmth. Further down, it grows colder and darker. Below 200 metres, no sunlight reaches at all.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored. We know more about the surface of the Moon than we do about the deep ocean. There is so much left to discover.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James was not so sure. He made his most worried face all the way there. Anna held his hand.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: At the dentist, there was a big fish tank in the waiting room! Bright fish darted in and out of rocks and weeds.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma's farm was big and sunny. There were hens in the yard, ducks by the pond and a very fat pig called Percy.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: At midnight, a fox barked in the lane. Chips went very still. James shone the torch outside. Nothing was there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Through the binoculars, Betty saw a kingfisher — a bright impossible dart of blue-orange above the water, there and then gone. She had to put the binoculars down and close her eyes for a moment. She had seen it. She wrote it in the log book.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Aiden's tooth came out on a Thursday. Not dramatically — he was reading his book and he touched it and then it was just there in his fingers, which was very quick and very strange and did not hurt at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the armoury, there was a full suit of plate armour. It was smaller than Aiden expected. The guide told them that real knights were roughly the same size as Dad, which was very hard to imagine. Aiden tried on a gauntlet under supervision. His hand barely fit inside.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: It was very quiet. Zippy looked around. There were flowers. There was a big blue sky.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: It was very quiet. Zippy looked around. There were flowers. There was a big blue sky.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Can you see the pillow? said Dozy. There was a long pause. Oh, said Clumsy. Yes. It is in the waterfall.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: How did it get there? said Grumpy. Everyone looked at Bouncy. I bounced past it, said Bouncy. SORRY.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Dozy hugged the pillow. Thank you, said Dozy. Both of you. Then Dozy fell asleep, right there, on the spot.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Grumpy has a strong tail, said Sunny. Grumpy swung the club tail at the rocks. CLONK. One small rock moved. There were fifty more.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: I am going to the Long Meadow, said Grumpy. There is a good flat rock there. Peaceful. No one around. Chompy appeared. Can I come? said Chompy. Grumpy closed their eyes. Fine.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: I am going to the Long Meadow, said Grumpy. There is a good flat rock there. Peaceful. No one around. Chompy appeared. Can I come? said Chompy. Grumpy closed their eyes. Fine.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: This is a good rock, said Chompy. Yes, said Grumpy. Is there anything to eat near it? said Chompy. Grumpy pointed at the berry patch. Chompy went happily.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: There would be a running race, a jumping contest, a loudness competition, and a prize for the tidiest corner of the Hollow. More events to be decided, said Bossy. I have a clipboard.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Chompy was there, but all the food was made of more clouds. This is disappointing, said Dream Chompy.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: There was a rope bridge over the Crystal Stream. Everyone crossed it without thinking. Everyone except Stone.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone would not cross the bridge. "There is a troll under the bridge," said Stone. "I do not want to meet it."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: "You crossed the bridge," said Pip. "Yes," said Stone. "But there might still be a troll under it." Stone looked at the bridge. "I should probably check."

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: She said the spell. There was a flash of bright blue light. Then it was quiet.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: There was another flash of blue. Wren was back to her normal size. She brushed off her robe. She straightened her hat.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: On the fourth day, Flint held up his finished map. "There," he said. "Every path in Moonwood. All of it."

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They walked along the walls slowly. There were drawings of things no one had seen in hundreds of years. What is this place? asked Fern.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Yes, said Luna. I remember now. She picked it up. I put it there to keep it safe. For today.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the third day, the diagrams had multiplied.
There were charts about heat.
Charts about breathing.
Charts about dragon anatomy.
Glimmer stared at them all.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
It was very late when Burrow noticed.
"Will you tell me the rest?" he asked.
"Yes," said Luna.
"There is quite a lot."
They both settled in.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
In the morning, Burrow woke up.
He looked around.
Pip and Glimmer were standing in front of him.
"Good morning," said Burrow.
There was a long pause.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
The fish was wedged between two rocks.
It had been there since morning.
Its tail kept flicking.
It could not get free.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Wren and Spark tried search spells.
The spells pointed at each other.
Stone looked under every log.
Gently.
There were no seeds under the logs.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Fern stopped.
She knelt down.
There were small green shoots in the ground.
They glowed.
Just a little.
Just like the seeds.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They gathered the star spirits.
There were many of them.
Stone held several.
Wren had two in her hat.
They kept bouncing.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern looked around the room.
Then she looked at Twig.
The spectacles were on top of Twig's head.
They had been there all along.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
There was a sign on the Hollow Oak door.
GLIMMER'S FIRE PERFORMANCE — TODAY.
Everyone came.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
It was the deepest part of the night.
Moonwood was very quiet.
Then there was a sound at the edge of the clearing.
Something small was there.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
It was the deepest part of the night.
Moonwood was very quiet.
Then there was a sound at the edge of the clearing.
Something small was there.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Beyond the roots, a small clearing.
Silver moss lit the ground.
It was warm.
Other creatures were there.
They looked up.
They had the same enormous silver eyes.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James came out. "It did not hurt at all!" he said. "And the chair goes UP and DOWN!" Anna laughed.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Dad did the tricky high bits — the tall planks and the big nails. James and Anna passed the tools and held the wood still.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Next came the floor — flat planks, all in a row. "Walk on it!" said Dad. They did. It held firm!

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna did not want to be the dragon. She wanted to paint the big backdrop — the scenery behind the stage.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mum and Dad clapped the loudest. Mum had tears. Dad said it was just the bright lights. James and Anna did not believe him.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna set off nice and slowly. She did not wobble. She did not crash. She rode all the way to the end of the path and back.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna set off nice and slowly. She did not wobble. She did not crash. She rode all the way to the end of the path and back.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: "How did you DO that?" said James. "I kept my eyes on where I wanted to go," said Anna. "Don't look at the ground."

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Aiden's tooth came out on a Thursday. Not dramatically — he was reading his book and he touched it and then it was just there in his fingers, which was very quick and very strange and did not hurt at all.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Wake up, Dozy! called Bouncy. Dozy did not wake up.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Wake up, Dozy! called Zippy. Dozy did not wake up.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: WAKE UP, DOZY! called Honky. Dozy did not wake up.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: How did it get there? said Grumpy. Everyone looked at Bouncy. I bounced past it, said Bouncy. SORRY.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Bossy flies, said Flappy. Bossy is a Pterodactyl. You are an Archaeopteryx. That is different. How is it different? said Flappy. Grumpy did not actually know.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: We need to move those rocks, said Bossy. Everyone tried pushing. The rocks did not move at all.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Dozy slept through most of the events and woke up in time for the picnic. Did I win anything? said Dozy. Most restful competitor, said Bossy. Deserved, said Dozy, and fell asleep again.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: When it passed, Sunny Hollow sparkled. We did that, said Sunny. All of us. Not bad, said Grumpy. From Grumpy, that meant wonderful.

uses.title: Sleepy Can't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Sleepy did not get up.

uses.title: Sleepy Can't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Sleepy did not get up.

uses.title: Sleepy Can't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Sleepy did not get up.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText: Cuddly did not go away.

uses.title: Bouncy and Speedy Have a Race
uses.pageText: They did not stop.

uses.title: Noisy Wakes Everyone Up
uses.pageText: Sleepy did not wake up.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: "Pull!" said Grumpy. The wool did not come off.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Clucky did not giggle.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Bouncy blew up the balloons. She did not stop.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: His legs felt wobbly. The ground was a long way below. But he did not stop. He reached the top.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "The stone did that!" said Pip. He tucked it safely into his pocket. Then he walked toward the Fog Marsh.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "Did it run out of brave?" asked Pip.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She did not use a spell. She sang to it, very softly. She sang the song her mother had taught her about seeds.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: "How did you make it stop?" asked Pip. "I didn't make it do anything," said Fern. "I asked it nicely."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They crossed back together. Stone did not look at the water. Stone looked at the far end of the bridge. One step, then another.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "That is not fire," said Glimmer. "No," agreed Pip. "But it smells nice." Glimmer did not look convinced.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer did not think. Glimmer just ran toward the fox. Glimmer breathed in as hard as possible.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: "Did it work?" asked Pip. "No," said Wren. "I am exactly the same height."

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He walked for three days. He did not stop. His map grew longer and longer. It was full of detail.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly. They always did.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it with water.
She pushed as hard as she could.
The boulder did not move.
"I am not strong enough," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern tried to push with her hands.
The boulder did not move.
Fern stepped back and thought.
"We need each other," said Fern.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the Hollow Oak, everyone heard it.
"The stream is singing again!" said Pip.
"We just moved a stone," said Fern.
"And asked the water nicely," said Dewdrop.
"It did the rest."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the first day, Spark explained fire.
He drew many diagrams.
The diagrams were very complicated.
Glimmer did not understand any of them.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"Did we succeed?" asked Spark.
"I don't know," said Glimmer.
"Let's try again tomorrow."
"Yes," said Spark.
They both smiled.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna was very large for a tunnel.
She came anyway.
She did not say anything about this.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Burrow bumped the bench.
It fell over.
Burrow kept walking.
He found Pip's door.
He moved the boots with his paws.
He did not wake up.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren stirred the potion.
It was meant to be green.
It was more purple.
Wren did not notice this.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Everything was back.
"I'm sorry," said Wren.
"Did you learn something?" asked Fern.
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it loose.
She sent the water flowing hard against the rocks.
The fish did not move.
"I need help," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Burrow went underground.
He searched every tunnel.
He found three interesting things.
He did not find any seeds.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
It was late in the Hollow Oak.
Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Inside the marsh, it was colder.
The trees drooped.
The water did not move.
Dewdrop led them through the fog.
She could feel the water.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
They all sat in the clearing.
Glimmer stood at the front.
It was very quiet.
"Ready," said Glimmer.
It did not quite feel true.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer did it again.
Longer.
The fire was steady.
It was warm.
Glimmer's scales caught the light.
Glimmer had never looked so much like a dragon.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip opened the door.
A small creature was at the edge of the clearing.
It had very large silver eyes.
It was frightened.
It did not run.

uses.title: Bob and Nan's First Day at School
uses.pageText: Nan has her bag.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Anna grabbed her pen and drew the plan. "It needs big wings," she said, "and a pointed nose cone at the top."

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "Oh, Chips!" said Anna. But she gave him a big hug. Chips licked her right on the nose.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma had a big brown horse called Bess. She was huge and gentle. Her nose was the softest thing James had ever felt.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna got to brush Bess's mane. James gave her a big red apple. Bess sniffed it — then snaffled the whole thing in one go!

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James chased Percy one way. Anna chased Percy the other way. Grandma just stood and laughed until her eyes watered.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the day of try-outs, James roared so loud that Mrs. Green's glasses slid right down her nose. He got the part!

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Through the binoculars, Betty saw a kingfisher — a bright impossible dart of blue-orange above the water, there and then gone. She had to put the binoculars down and close her eyes for a moment. She had seen it. She wrote it in the log book.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Betty had the guide map. She navigated with precise efficiency — Great Hall, Armoury, North Tower, King's Chamber, Dungeon — the best order for minimum backtracking. Aiden followed behind her, reading every information board they passed, completely at home in a world of facts.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: Sunny shared her lunch. Here you go, Chompy! said Sunny.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She did not use a spell. She sang to it, very softly. She sang the song her mother had taught her about seeds.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She did not use a spell. She sang to it, very softly. She sang the song her mother had taught her about seeds.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren wanted to be taller. She had found a spell in her book. A growing spell, she was sure. She read it very carefully.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren looked at her hands. Her hands were a very long way away. She was not taller. She was one inch tall.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren looked at her hands. Her hands were a very long way away. She was not taller. She was one inch tall.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Oh, said Wren. Her voice came out very small. Everything around her was enormous.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Oh, said Wren. Her voice came out very small. Everything around her was enormous.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren found her spell book. It was enormous now. She climbed up onto it and looked at the spell. She had read it backwards.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: "Fixing it," said tiny Wren. She raised her tiny hands. She said the spell again. Forwards, this time.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: There was another flash of blue. Wren was back to her normal size. She brushed off her robe. She straightened her hat.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: There was another flash of blue. Wren was back to her normal size. She brushed off her robe. She straightened her hat.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: There was another flash of blue. Wren was back to her normal size. She brushed off her robe. She straightened her hat.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren picked up her spell book. She turned to the next spell. "But I am going to find a better one," she said. She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop knew every fish in the Crystal Stream. She talked to them every morning. They told her things: where the water was cold, where the best pebbles were.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Hello, said Dewdrop. I am the oldest fish in Moonwood, said the fish. Dewdrop tilted her head. The fish was not very large.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Wren found a cold remedy in her spell book. She read it very, very carefully. Forwards? said Spark. Forwards, said Wren.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna woke up knowing she had forgotten something important. She sat on her branch. She thought very hard. She could not remember what it was.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern tried to push with her hands.
The boulder did not move.
Fern stepped back and thought.
"We need each other," said Fern.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"I wonder," said Wren.
She closed her spell book.
She spoke to the mushroom.
Very quietly.
She asked it the way.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna stood in the doorway.
She was very still.
Her eyes went wide.
Then soft.
"Oh," said Luna.
Very quietly.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna settled on a ledge.
She folded her wings.
She looked at the carvings for a moment.
"The first story of Moonwood," she began,
"is this."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern's garden was her favourite place.
One morning, Wren arrived with a cauldron.
"I have a potion," said Wren.
"It will help your plants."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Oh," said Wren.
"Oh no," said Fern.
"The plants are walking."
Wren checked her book.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern went to the middle of the clearing.
She closed her eyes.
She sang.
Very softly.
The same song from long ago.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They gathered the star spirits.
There were many of them.
Stone held several.
Wren had two in her hat.
They kept bouncing.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire faded slowly.
Moonwood kept its glow.
Luna looked at Glimmer over her glasses.
"Quite controlled," said Luna.
"Thank you," said Glimmer.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James and Anna were in the garden. They had lots of big, flat boxes.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Let us make a rocket!" said James. "We can fly all the way into space!"

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James got the red paint. Anna got the silver paint. They painted and painted until it shone!

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "It is the best rocket ever made!" said James. He and Anna stood back and grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They climbed inside. James held up five fingers. "Five... four... three... two... one... BLAST OFF!"

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James and Anna played with Zim all day. They jumped so high on the moon!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James and Anna had a pet goat. His name was Chips. He was small and white with big brown patches.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James made Chips a lead from a long piece of rope. Now Chips could come on walks!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They got home just in time for lunch. James filled Chips's bowl with fresh grass and sliced apple.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips ate it all in a flash. He looked at the bowl. Then he looked at James. Then he looked at James's jumper.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. James grabbed the list. Anna grabbed the bags. Off they went!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. James grabbed the list. Anna grabbed the bags. Off they went!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "We need bread, grapes, cheese, eggs and orange juice," said James, reading the list carefully.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James found the grapes. Red ones or green ones? He put both bunches in the basket — just to be safe.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: They found the cheese, the eggs and the juice. James was very careful with the eggs.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "Can we get a cake each?" asked James. Mum smiled. "One each," she said.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James chose a big slice of lemon cake with thick white icing. Anna chose a pink strawberry jam tart.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At the till, Mum let James put the shopping on the belt. He was VERY careful with the eggs.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James was not so sure. He made his most worried face all the way there. Anna held his hand.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James pressed his nose flat to the glass. "That one looks just like a tiny striped rocket!" he said.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "James!" called the dentist. He stood up. He walked in. The big chair went up and down like a ride!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James came out. "It did not hurt at all!" he said. "And the chair goes UP and DOWN!" Anna laughed.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Well done, both of you," said Mum. "You were so brave today." They each got a sticker — James got a rocket, Anna got a star.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: At the end of the garden stood a big old oak tree. James and Anna had been staring at it for days.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: "We should build a tree house!" said James. He got his notebook and drew the plan right away. It had a door, a window, a flag and a rope ladder.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Dad did the tricky high bits — the tall planks and the big nails. James and Anna passed the tools and held the wood still.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Then they made the walls and cut a little door. James helped saw a window hole with a small hand saw.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Now for the best bit — the paint! James chose blue for the walls. Anna chose yellow for the door. Chips chewed the lid off the paint tin.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: James and Anna climbed up and sat at the little window. "This is the best thing we have ever made," said Anna.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James and Anna were going to stay at Grandma's farm for the week. They packed their bags — and Chips got in the car too.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James ran to see the hens. "They have laid five eggs!" he said. He put them one by one — very, very carefully — into a basket.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma had a big brown horse called Bess. She was huge and gentle. Her nose was the softest thing James had ever felt.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna got to brush Bess's mane. James gave her a big red apple. Bess sniffed it — then snaffled the whole thing in one go!

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James chased Percy one way. Anna chased Percy the other way. Grandma just stood and laughed until her eyes watered.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna together. Grandma came and looked. "He fits in very well here," she said.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: That evening, Grandma made soup from the garden and fried the eggs James had found. It was the best meal they had ever tasted.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James put his hand straight up. "I want to be the dragon!" Six other children put their hands up too. They would all have to try out.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James practised his dragon roar all week. It shook the windows. Mum wore earmuffs. Chips ran under the sofa.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the day of try-outs, James roared so loud that Mrs. Green's glasses slid right down her nose. He got the part!

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the night of the play, James wore a green scale costume and a red dragon mask. He looked completely brilliant.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Then the lights went up and James walked on stage. He could see the WHOLE school in the dark. His legs went very wobbly.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James took a deep breath. He thought of his best roar. Then he let it out — the biggest, loudest roar he had ever done.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: The play went brilliantly after that. James roared and stomped and the little ones in the front row screamed and giggled.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: At the very end, everyone stood and clapped. James and Anna walked to the front of the stage and bowed together.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mum and Dad clapped the loudest. Mum had tears. Dad said it was just the bright lights. James and Anna did not believe him.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. They were absolutely sure it would be fine. They were wrong.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: James brought Chips into the garden. Anna opened the gate. Bella bounded in like a very large, very furry rocket.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella crashed into the paddling pool. Water exploded in every direction. James and Anna were completely soaked.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "I think they like each other," said Anna. "They are just as bad as each other," said James.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: For their birthdays, James and Anna each got a new bike. James's was red. Anna's was purple.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They put on their helmets and walked the bikes outside. James could not wait. Anna checked the brakes first.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: "How did you DO that?" said James. "I kept my eyes on where I wanted to go," said Anna. "Don't look at the ground."

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James tried again. Eyes forward. Pedal. Wobble. Wobble. Then — he was doing it! He was really, properly doing it!

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Then James tried riding with NO hands. He made it exactly three seconds before heading straight into the same bush.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: On the way home, James and Anna raced. They crossed the gate post at exactly the same time. A perfect tie.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: That night their legs ached. But they were both smiling. "Same time tomorrow?" said James. Anna was already asleep.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: James and Anna helped bang in the tent pegs and thread the poles through. Chips ate one peg. Then he tried to eat a second.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: At midnight, a fox barked in the lane. Chips went very still. James shone the torch outside. Nothing was there.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
