uses.pageText: "What if it comes back?" said James. "Then we will scare it," said Anna. She picked up the air horn Dad had packed.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They tried to sleep. Chips leaned on James. James leaned on Anna. Anna leaned on the tent wall. Nobody was quite comfortable.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They tried to sleep. Chips leaned on James. James leaned on Anna. Anna leaned on the tent wall. Nobody was quite comfortable.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "Next year," said James, "we camp in a real field." "Next year," said Mum from the doorway, "Chips stays home." Chips ate the tent door zip.

uses.title: Seasons
uses.pageText: I like all four seasons!

uses.title: Fast and Slow
uses.pageText:
Fast or slow?
Which do you like?

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: Four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Which do you like best?

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: An oval is like a stretched circle. An egg is an oval. A leaf is an oval.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon changes shape. Sometimes it looks like a banana.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: Which sense do you like best?

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Lava can be as hot as 1,000 degrees. Some volcanoes are calm and slow. Their lava oozes out like very thick, very hot syrup.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Not all webs look the same. Sheet webs are flat like a hammock. Cobwebs are messy tangles. Every type of spider makes its own kind of web.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The top layer is full of life. Coral reefs grow in warm, shallow water. They are home to thousands of kinds of fish and animal. A coral reef is like an underwater city.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Coral looks like rock or plant, but it is an animal. Each piece of coral is made of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps. Coral reefs take thousands of years to grow.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies are insects. Like all insects, they have six legs, four wings, and a body in three parts. They also have two long antennae.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: After a few weeks, tadpoles wriggle out of the eggs. Tadpoles have tails and no legs. They breathe underwater using gills, like fish.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James pressed his nose flat to the glass. "That one looks just like a tiny striped rocket!" he said.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "James!" called the dentist. He stood up. He walked in. The big chair went up and down like a ride!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Their neighbour Mrs. Chen had a big, bouncy dog called Bella. "Would Chips like a play date?" Mrs. Chen asked one morning.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: James brought Chips into the garden. Anna opened the gate. Bella bounded in like a very large, very furry rocket.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "I think they like each other," said Anna. "They are just as bad as each other," said James.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The view from the top was unlike anything Aiden had seen. The whole coastline curved away in both directions — bays and headlands, a small fishing village far below, and the sea stretching to the horizon, catching the light like crinkled silver foil.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden wrote in his notebook: When something is unfair, you have two choices — pretend it isn't happening, or decide what to do. He starred the second option. He didn't quite know yet what doing something looked like.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: I like your tail, said Dozy sleepily. It fans me while I nap. The Dino Pals all agreed.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a smooth pebble for Grumpy. Someone knows I like pebbles, said Grumpy, suspicious but pleased.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: I cannot leave the cave, said Fancy. Not like this. Fancy sat very still and stared at the cave wall.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried roaring like the other dinosaurs. A small squawk came out. Some feathers drifted down.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: AAAAAAACHOOOOOO! The sneeze hit the rocks like a wave. Rocks scattered in every direction. The stream burst free. The waterfall roared back. A rainbow appeared.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Back in the meadow, Dozy's eyes opened. All the Dino Pals were sitting in a circle, waiting. What was it like? said Sunny.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: It was exactly like this, said Dozy, looking at all of them, but cloudier. Dozy's eyes closed again. Wake me for supper.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: But you didn't, said Sunny. Zippy ran four more circuits of Sunny Hollow. I know, said Zippy, on the third lap. I just like to make sure.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: "I do not like birthdays," said Grumpy.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: "I do not like cake," said Grumpy.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: "I do not like hats," said Grumpy.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: "I do not like surprises," said Grumpy.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: "I like cake," said Grumpy.

uses.title: Muddy and Splashy Make a Mess
uses.pageText: "I do not like mud!" said Grumpy.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: "I do not like this," said Grumpy. "I do not like this," said Woolly.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: "I do not like this," said Grumpy. "I do not like this," said Woolly.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: "I like parties," said Grumpy.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone thought about this for a long time. "Yes," said Stone. "But I still don't like the bridge."

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: One morning, a new fish appeared. It was silver with a bright blue stripe. Dewdrop had never seen a fish like it.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
That afternoon, it was Glimmer's turn to teach.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer hovered for a moment.
Then landed.
"Like that," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"What does flying feel like?" asked Spark.
Glimmer thought.
"Like falling upward," said Glimmer.
Spark nodded slowly.
"I think I understand."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"What does flying feel like?" asked Spark.
Glimmer thought.
"Like falling upward," said Glimmer.
Spark nodded slowly.
"I think I understand."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants slowed.
The far ones turned.
They walked back.
Slowly.
Like sleepy creatures going home.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Stone stood at the edge of the Crystal Stream.
The water sparkled.
Stone's feet stayed on the bank.
"I don't like getting wet," said Stone.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Fern stopped.
She knelt down.
There were small green shoots in the ground.
They glowed.
Just a little.
Just like the seeds.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The small things landed and bounced.
They bounced along the ground.
They made a sound like giggling.
They left gold trails where they bounced.
"What ARE they?" said Pip.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer did it again.
Longer.
The fire was steady.
It was warm.
Glimmer's scales caught the light.
Glimmer had never looked so much like a dragon.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: Our Earth
uses.pageText: Earth has land and water.

uses.title: Our Earth
uses.pageText: Earth has tall mountains.

uses.title: Our Earth
uses.pageText: Earth has deep oceans.

uses.title: Our Earth
uses.pageText: Earth has green forests.

uses.title: Magnets
uses.pageText: A magnet has two poles.

uses.title: My Pet
uses.pageText:
My dog has a bed.
It is soft.

uses.title: My Pet
uses.pageText:
My cat has a mat.
It is warm.

uses.title: My Pet
uses.pageText:
My fish has a tank.
It is wet.

uses.title: My Pet
uses.pageText:
My bird has a cage.
It can sing.

uses.title: My Pet
uses.pageText:
My rabbit has fur.
It is soft.

uses.title: My Pet
uses.pageText:
My pet has a name.
I love my pet.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText:
The tree has roots.
They go down.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText: The tree has a thick trunk.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText:
The tree has branches.
They reach up.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText: The tree has green leaves.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText:
The tree has red apples.
I can pick one.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText:
Saturn has rings.
The rings are big.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A green shoot comes up! It has two small leaves.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A flower blooms! The seed has grown into a plant.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A flower has petals. A flower has a stem. A flower has roots.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A flower has petals. A flower has a stem. A flower has roots.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A flower has petals. A flower has a stem. A flower has roots.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A rose is red. It smells sweet. It has sharp thorns.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText: A baby sheep is a lamb. A lamb has soft wool.

uses.title: Animals on the Farm
uses.pageText: A sheep has thick wool. Wool keeps us warm.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A fish has fins. Fins help fish swim. Fish have scales.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: An octopus has eight arms. It can change colour. It hides in rocks.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A crab has a hard shell. A crab walks sideways.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: A fox hunts at night. It has big ears. It moves quietly.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A butterfly has four wings. Its wings have bright patterns.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A snail has a shell on its back. A snail moves very slowly.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A square has four equal sides. A window is a square. A cracker is a square.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A triangle has three sides. A pizza slice is a triangle. A roof is a triangle.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A rectangle has four sides. Two sides are long, two are short. A door is a rectangle. A book is a rectangle.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A star has five points. We see stars in the night sky.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Famous volcanoes can be found all around the world. Iceland, Hawaii and Italy all have active volcanoes. Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: When the egg hatches, a tiny chick comes out. The chick has thick grey fluffy feathers. It cuddles close to its parent to stay warm.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon does not make its own light. It has no fire or glow inside. The light we see is sunlight bouncing off the Moon's surface.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean has different layers. Near the surface, there is plenty of sunlight and warmth. Further down, it grows colder and darker. Below 200 metres, no sunlight reaches at all.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored. We know more about the surface of the Moon than we do about the deep ocean. There is so much left to discover.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: A butterfly's life has four stages. This is called a lifecycle. Each stage looks completely different from the one before.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Over time, tunnels and chambers form underground. Some cave systems stretch for hundreds of kilometres. The Mammoth Cave system in America has more than 650 kilometres of passages.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs sing to find a mate. Each species has its own call. The ribbit of a tree frog, the deep croak of a bullfrog — their calls fill warm evenings around the world.

uses.pageText: Nan has a big gift for Bob.

uses.pageText: Nan has a nap. Fluff has a nap too.

uses.pageText: Mum has a hot cup for Nan and Bob.

uses.pageText: Fluff has a sore leg.

uses.pageText: The vet has a jab for Fluff.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly felt sad. My tail has a mind of its own, said Wiggly.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Has anyone seen my pillow? said Dozy. Dozy had been looking for it all morning. This was serious.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Grumpy has a strong tail, said Sunny. Grumpy swung the club tail at the rocks. CLONK. One small rock moved. There were fifty more.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy has been asleep for three hours, said Bossy. Should we be worried? said Bossy. Dozy looks very peaceful, said Sunny. They watched Dozy sleeping. Dozy was definitely very peaceful.

uses.title: Clucky Lays an Egg
uses.pageText: Clucky has to lay an egg.

uses.title: Giggly Has the Hiccups
uses.pageText: Giggly has the hiccups.

uses.pageText: Muddy has some mud.

uses.pageText: Splashy has some water.

uses.pageText: Tiny has lost a hat.

uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon is far away. But we can see it every night.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can seem frightening. But they have helped shape our planet. They make new land, rich soil and even new islands. They have been doing this for billions of years.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are birds — but they cannot fly. Instead, they use their wings as flippers. They are brilliant swimmers.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks small from Earth, but it is very large. It is about a quarter the size of our whole planet. If Earth were a basketball, the Moon would be a tennis ball.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders have eight eyes, but many cannot see well. Instead, they feel vibrations through their legs. When something touches the web, the spider feels it instantly.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Coral looks like rock or plant, but it is an animal. Each piece of coral is made of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps. Coral reefs take thousands of years to grow.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "Oh, Chips!" said Anna. But she gave him a big hug. Chips licked her right on the nose.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they both said. But they could not stop smiling. Chips was naughty and cheeky and silly — and they loved him so much.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At home, Mum made lunch. After, they had their cakes. Chips ate the paper bag. "CHIPS!" they said. But they were laughing too hard to be cross.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: "I can help," said Dad, "but you two are in charge. You tell me the plan."

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: That night their legs ached. But they were both smiling. "Same time tomorrow?" said James. Anna was already asleep.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they said. But the sun was warm and breakfast was good and it had been a perfect camp.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Aiden had started a new notebook that evening — not the Socks field study, but a nature notebook. He had titled it with the date. Betty had started a matching one, without them discussing it. Both were already half a page in.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden didn't say anything. He went home and sat on his bed and stared at the ceiling. He wasn't crying, but he wasn't fine either. He didn't really want to talk about it — which Betty noticed immediately.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: It was quiet. Nobody laughed. Marcus said something low, but nobody around him responded. Aiden walked on. His legs were slightly shaky — but he hadn't shown it, and he was extremely proud of himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: It was quiet. Nobody laughed. Marcus said something low, but nobody around him responded. Aiden walked on. His legs were slightly shaky — but he hadn't shown it, and he was extremely proud of himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Grumpy. Not that I needed it. But Grumpy was smiling. Just a little.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky laughed and laughed. But then Cheeky slipped on the same mud. SPLAT!

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a smooth pebble for Grumpy. Someone knows I like pebbles, said Grumpy, suspicious but pleased.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: They were the best gifts we ever had, said Sunny. Will you come and sit with us? Shy came out. Just a little way. But it was something.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy asked Sunny. You are wonderful just as you are! said Sunny. But what AM I? said Flappy. Wonderful! said Sunny. Flappy went away still confused.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: But dinosaurs do not nest in trees, said Flappy. You do, said Grumpy. And birds do not live in Sunny Hollow with everyone else. You do, said Grumpy.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Then Chompy fell into a ditch. HELP, said Chompy. It was not a deep ditch. But Chompy's arms were very tiny.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Chompy. Hmph, said Grumpy. They sat on the rock together. Less peaceful with Chompy. But not actually terrible.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Chompy was there, but all the food was made of more clouds. This is disappointing, said Dream Chompy.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy floated on a cloud past the Rainbow Waterfall. But in the dream, the waterfall was made of warm golden light. Oh, said Dozy. This is very nice.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: It was exactly like this, said Dozy, looking at all of them, but cloudier. Dozy's eyes closed again. Wake me for supper.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: BANG. They were off. Zippy was first. Of course. But the very fast runner was close. Very close.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: But you didn't, said Sunny. Zippy ran four more circuits of Sunny Hollow. I know, said Zippy, on the third lap. I just like to make sure.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.pageText: But Tiny can fit in the pot.

uses.title: Grumpy's Secret

uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone. "But I don't feel brave," he said. "I feel the same as always."

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: His legs felt wobbly. The ground was a long way below. But he did not stop. He reached the top.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: Fern sat down and thought. Spells had made it grow. But a growing thing needed something different.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone thought about this for a long time. "Yes," said Stone. "But I still don't like the bridge."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: "You crossed the bridge," said Pip. "Yes," said Stone. "But there might still be a troll under it." Stone looked at the bridge. "I should probably check."

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "That is not fire," said Glimmer. "No," agreed Pip. "But it smells nice." Glimmer did not look convinced.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren picked up her spell book. She turned to the next spell. "But I am going to find a better one," she said. She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Stone knelt down carefully.
"We will help," said Stone.
The toadling looked at Stone.
"You are very large," said the toadling.
"Yes," said Stone. "But I am gentle."

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
"It flows," said Fern.
"But it does not sing," said Dewdrop.
"Something is wrong at the source."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
"We'll take you home," said Pip.
"But the Deep Dark—" said Wren.
"We'll go together," said Pip.
Everyone looked at each other.
"Together," said Stone.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: Sun, rain, wind, snow. Weather changes every day. What is the weather today?

uses.pageText: Baby animals grow. One day they will be big.

uses.title: Animals on the Farm
uses.pageText: A cow gives us milk. We drink milk every day.

uses.title: Animals at Night

uses.pageText: At midday, the sun is high. It is the hottest part of the day.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: In the day, we wake up. We play, learn, and eat.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: The Earth spins around. That is why we have day and night.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: Five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. I use them every day!

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I learned to run and jump. I grew more every day.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I will keep on growing. One day I will be tall!

uses.title: Staying Healthy
uses.pageText: Brush your teeth. Brush them twice a day.

uses.title: Staying Healthy
uses.pageText: Stay healthy every day! Eat, move, sleep, and smile!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: My body is amazing! I look after it every day.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: We drink water every day. Water keeps us healthy.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees work hard every day. They help flowers grow. They make our world sweeter. Bees are amazing.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are home to many animals. Bats sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings by day. At dusk, thousands of bats fly out together to feed on insects in the night air.

uses.title: Bob and Nan go to the Park
uses.pageText: What a fun day!

uses.title: Bob and Nan's First Day at School
uses.pageText: It is the big day.

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: It is Bob's big day!

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: It was the best day!

uses.title: Nan and Bob Learn to Read
uses.pageText: Nan and Bob read all day.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James and Anna played with Zim all day. They jumped so high on the moon!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips liked to eat. He ate the long green grass. He ate sticks and bits of bark. One day, he ate Dad's best hat!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: It was a bright autumn day. Mum had a long list. "I need help at the shop," she said. "Can you both come?"

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the day of try-outs, James roared so loud that Mrs. Green's glasses slid right down her nose. He got the part!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The last day of the summer term was also the loudest day of the school year. Aiden and Betty burst through the front door and both shouted "HOLIDAY!" at exactly the same moment, which echoed all the way up the stairs and made the dog next door bark.

uses.pageText: The last day of the summer term was also the loudest day of the school year. Aiden and Betty burst through the front door and both shouted "HOLIDAY!" at exactly the same moment, which echoed all the way up the stairs and made the dog next door bark.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: The sun came back out. See? said Sunny. Every day is a good day!

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: The sun came back out. See? said Sunny. Every day is a good day!

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a smooth pebble for Grumpy. Someone knows I like pebbles, said Grumpy, suspicious but pleased.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a pile of extra berries for Chompy. Someone knows me very well, said Chompy, already eating them.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a leafy fan for Dozy. This is perfect, said Dozy, already asleep with it.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: This will take all day, said Grumpy. Hmph. Everyone sat down feeling stuck.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: The race day came. The runners lined up. They were all fast. One was very fast indeed.

uses.title: Grumpy's Secret
uses.pageText: Every day, Grumpy goes off.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: It is party day!

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: One day, Burrow got stuck on the other side of the stream. "Help!" called Burrow. "I cannot find the tunnel. Everything looks the same to me!"

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the first day: a small puff of smoke. Just smoke. No fire at all.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the fifth day, Glimmer breathed in as deeply as possible. A warm puff came out. It smelled of cinnamon. "That's something," said Pip.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the tenth day, Glimmer went to the Crystal Stream alone. Again and again. Smoke. Sparks. Warm cinnamon breath. Still no fire.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer sat down. "I will never breathe fire," said Glimmer. "I have tried every day and it is never fire."

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: On the fourth day, Flint held up his finished map. "There," he said. "Every path in Moonwood. All of it."

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the first day, Spark explained fire.
He drew many diagrams.
The diagrams were very complicated.
Glimmer did not understand any of them.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the third day, the diagrams had multiplied.
There were charts about heat.
Charts about breathing.
Charts about dragon anatomy.
Glimmer stared at them all.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Reptiles
uses.pageText: Snakes are long reptiles.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A rectangle has four sides. Two sides are long, two are short. A door is a rectangle. A book is a rectangle.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Most volcanoes are quiet for a very long time. Scientists called volcanologists watch them carefully. They use special equipment to spot the signs of an eruption.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's surface is covered in craters. Craters are bowl-shaped holes made by space rocks crashing into the Moon long ago. Some craters are bigger than cities.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies are insects. Like all insects, they have six legs, four wings, and a body in three parts. They also have two long antennae.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs are expert hunters. They have long, sticky tongues. A frog can flip its tongue out and back in less time than a blink to catch an insect.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They cut and snipped and stuck and taped. They worked all morning long.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips liked to eat. He ate the long green grass. He ate sticks and bits of bark. One day, he ate Dad's best hat!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James made Chips a lead from a long piece of rope. Now Chips could come on walks!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They set off down the lane. Chips trotted along and stopped to munch the long grass at the sides.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: It was a bright autumn day. Mum had a long list. "I need help at the shop," she said. "Can you both come?"

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Then Anna spotted the cake stand! Big cakes, small cakes, jam tarts and iced buns — all in a long, shining row.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: By lunchtime, they could both ride all the way down the long lane and back without stopping once.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Dad got his old bike out and the three of them went for a long ride down to the duck pond.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Dad made a small camp fire in a safe metal dish. They toasted marshmallows on long sticks over the warm flames.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He held it up for a long time. It was tiny. It was the smallest thing that had ever felt significant. He put it in the small envelope Mum left for him, and when he placed it under his pillow it felt ceremonial.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Clumsy could see over all the ferns, past the waterfall, all the way to the Long Meadow and beyond.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Can you see the pillow? said Dozy. There was a long pause. Oh, said Clumsy. Yes. It is in the waterfall.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Grumpy, said Flappy. Am I a dinosaur or a bird? Grumpy thought for a very long time. You are Flappy, said Grumpy. That is enough.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: I am going to the Long Meadow, said Grumpy. There is a good flat rock there. Peaceful. No one around. Chompy appeared. Can I come? said Chompy. Grumpy closed their eyes. Fine.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Sneezy entered the farthest-blast competition. Sneezy's sneeze sent the test leaf all the way to the Long Meadow. The judge had to run to collect the result. Zippy collected it. Obviously.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Wiggly's long tail swept the Big Flat Rock clear in seconds. Food, supplies, anything that could blow away. Sorry, said Wiggly, sweeping everything. This time everyone was grateful.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: His legs felt wobbly. The ground was a long way below. But he did not stop. He reached the top.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone for a long time. "I'll keep it," he said. "To remember."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone thought about this for a long time. "Yes," said Stone. "But I still don't like the bridge."

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren looked at her hands. Her hands were a very long way away. She was not taller. She was one inch tall.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint sat down on a mossy rock. He looked at the map for a long time. It was very beautiful. It was also completely wrong.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They stayed for a long time. No one wanted to leave. The room was very quiet and very warm.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"Spark," said Glimmer.
"You are trying too hard."
"Fire is not thinking."
"It is feeling."
Spark looked at Glimmer for a long time.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"Have you been here before?" asked Burrow.
"Yes," said Luna.
She looked around the room.
"A very long time ago."
"What is it?" asked Burrow.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
In the morning, Burrow woke up.
He looked around.
Pip and Glimmer were standing in front of him.
"Good morning," said Burrow.
There was a long pause.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern went to the middle of the clearing.
She closed her eyes.
She sang.
Very softly.
The same song from long ago.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
They sat by the stream together.
Stone dripped for a long time.
The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.
And meant it.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
The magic seeds were gone.
The box that held them was open and empty.
Luna looked at the box for a long time.
"This is not good," she said.

uses.title: How Things Grow
uses.pageText: All living things need food.

uses.title: How Things Grow
uses.pageText: All living things need water.

uses.title: Animals on the Farm
uses.pageText: A horse is strong. Horses can pull and carry things.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: Big or small — all things are special! What is big? What is small?

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: A boat floats on the water. It can carry things.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: A big rock is heavy. Heavy things often sink.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: Some things float. Some things sink. Science is fun!

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: Some things float. Some things sink. Science is fun!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: A push moves things away. Push!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: A pull brings things closer. Pull!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: Push and pull are forces. Forces make things move.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can smell. My nose lets me smell nice things.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can touch. My hands can feel if things are rough or smooth, hot or cold.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: Now I am bigger. I can do so many things!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: My body can do so many things! I can hop, skip, and spin.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: We use rocks to build things. Walls and roads are made of rock.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A seed needs three things to start growing: water, warmth, and air. When it gets all three, it wakes up and begins to grow.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor had noticed, in the way that good teachers always notice. She started a class discussion about what it means to be fair, and what you do when things aren't. Several children looked at the floor. Marcus looked at the window.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Chompy: get berries. Sunny: get leaves. Wiggly: carry things. Dozy: try to stay awake.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Honky offered to shout at it until it moved. Everyone agreed this would make things much worse.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly fetched water from the waterfall very carefully. The tail only knocked over two things. Sorry, said Wiggly.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Bouncy bounced up to reach the high branches and secure anything at risk. Only bumped into three things. A new record, said Bouncy.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop knew every fish in the Crystal Stream. She talked to them every morning. They told her things: where the water was cold, where the best pebbles were.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop went back to the Crystal Stream. Why do you say things that are not true? she asked. She said it kindly. She just wanted to know.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: After that, the fish told Dewdrop true things. Small things, mostly. Where the water was coldest. Where the most unusual pebbles were. These things were true.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: After that, the fish told Dewdrop true things. Small things, mostly. Where the water was coldest. Where the most unusual pebbles were. These things were true.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: After that, the fish told Dewdrop true things. Small things, mostly. Where the water was coldest. Where the most unusual pebbles were. These things were true.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: What is inside? said Pip. Luna was quiet. Good things, I think, she said finally. I cannot quite remember what kind.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They walked along the walls slowly. There were drawings of things no one had seen in hundreds of years. What is this place? asked Fern.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: This was the problem with forgetting things. You couldn't always remember what you had forgotten. Luna knew it was important. She knew it was today.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer tried.
Smoke came out.
Just smoke.
"Interesting," said Spark, and wrote things down.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
One morning, things had moved in the night.
Pip's boots were not where he had left them.
A bench was tipped over.
Someone had been in the clearing.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
The next night, it happened again.
More things had moved.
"Was it you?" asked Stone.
"No," said Pip.
"Was it you?" asked Pip.
"No," said everyone.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Pip searched the Fog Marsh.
He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Burrow went underground.
He searched every tunnel.
He found three interesting things.
He did not find any seeds.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The small things landed and bounced.
They bounced along the ground.
They made a sound like giggling.
They left gold trails where they bounced.
"What ARE they?" said Pip.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"This way," said Flint.
He was right.
The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.
"I always find things," said Flint.
"Eventually."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They had set up a lemonade stand beside the sale table — Betty's idea, planned the previous Thursday. Aiden poured from a glass jug. Betty collected the money and kept the queue moving. By one o'clock they had sold every cup and run entirely out of lemons.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The last day of the summer term was also the loudest day of the school year. Aiden and Betty burst through the front door and both shouted "HOLIDAY!" at exactly the same moment, which echoed all the way up the stairs and made the dog next door bark.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They decided to grow crystals. It was Betty's original idea and Aiden's second choice, which Betty said made it the obvious answer. They ordered the kit and spent four days watching for the post.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "Socks!" said Aiden and Betty. Socks examined the jar from every angle, turning it slowly. He handed it back eventually — and the crystals were, miraculously, completely intact.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The school hall was full of projects — a volcano that erupted three times, a model solar system, a survey about favourite foods with real graphs. Betty looked at all of them carefully and said nothing. Aiden chewed the inside of his cheek.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Third place, with a commendation for experimental method, went to HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW? The commendation was on a proper certificate with a gold border. Betty read every word of it, twice.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Through the binoculars, Betty saw a kingfisher — a bright impossible dart of blue-orange above the water, there and then gone. She had to put the binoculars down and close her eyes for a moment. She had seen it. She wrote it in the log book.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Aiden had started a new notebook that evening — not the Socks field study, but a nature notebook. He had titled it with the date. Betty had started a matching one, without them discussing it. Both were already half a page in.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden didn't say anything. He went home and sat on his bed and stared at the ceiling. He wasn't crying, but he wasn't fine either. He didn't really want to talk about it — which Betty noticed immediately.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
