uses.pageText: He told Betty. Betty got the torch and studied it with great interest. "It's definitely loose," she said. "It'll fall out and a permanent one will grow. That's much better, actually." Aiden was not entirely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He told Betty. Betty got the torch and studied it with great interest. "It's definitely loose," she said. "It'll fall out and a permanent one will grow. That's much better, actually." Aiden was not entirely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Betty had the guide map. She navigated with precise efficiency — Great Hall, Armoury, North Tower, King's Chamber, Dungeon — the best order for minimum backtracking. Aiden followed behind her, reading every information board they passed, completely at home in a world of facts.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The dungeon was underground and smelled of cold stone and old air. Betty read every board by torchlight. Aiden stood still in the near-dark for a moment and thought about how this exact place had been here through everything — and felt briefly, appropriately small.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The drive home was quiet in the way that follows something large. "What are you thinking about?" said Mum. Aiden and Betty both answered at the same time, with completely different answers. "That," said Mum, "is exactly right."

uses.title: How Things Grow
uses.pageText: Growing takes time and care!

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Most volcanoes are quiet for a very long time. Scientists called volcanologists watch them carefully. They use special equipment to spot the signs of an eruption.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Over time, tunnels and chambers form underground. Some cave systems stretch for hundreds of kilometres. The Mammoth Cave system in America has more than 650 kilometres of passages.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs are expert hunters. They have long, sticky tongues. A frog can flip its tongue out and back in less time than a blink to catch an insect.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Time to go home," said Anna. "Come back soon!" called Zim, and he waved and waved.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They got home just in time for lunch. James filled Chips's bowl with fresh grass and sliced apple.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: On the way home, James and Anna raced. They crossed the gate post at exactly the same time. A perfect tie.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: That night their legs ached. But they were both smiling. "Same time tomorrow?" said James. Anna was already asleep.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Chips was coming too. He had his own little blanket and his bell, which jingled every single time he moved.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At home time, Mum was waiting at the gate. She crouched down with an expectant look. "Well?" she said. They both started talking at exactly the same moment and didn't stop for ten minutes.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He held it up for a long time. It was tiny. It was the smallest thing that had ever felt significant. He put it in the small envelope Mum left for him, and when he placed it under his pillow it felt ceremonial.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The drive home was quiet in the way that follows something large. "What are you thinking about?" said Mum. Aiden and Betty both answered at the same time, with completely different answers. "That," said Mum, "is exactly right."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Grumpy, said Flappy. Am I a dinosaur or a bird? Grumpy thought for a very long time. You are Flappy, said Grumpy. That is enough.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Dozy slept through most of the events and woke up in time for the picnic. Did I win anything? said Dozy. Most restful competitor, said Bossy. Deserved, said Dozy, and fell asleep again.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: One afternoon, Dozy fell asleep in the Long Meadow. This was not unusual. But this time, Dozy did not wake up for a very, very long time.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: The second runner came over. Good race, they said. You too, said Zippy, breathing hard for the first time ever.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Clumsy stood tall and looked out over the whole Hollow. The storm is coming from the east, said Clumsy. The tall ferns are already bending. That gives us time.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Wiggly's long tail swept the Big Flat Rock clear in seconds. Food, supplies, anything that could blow away. Sorry, said Wiggly, sweeping everything. This time everyone was grateful.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone for a long time. "I'll keep it," he said. "To remember."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone thought about this for a long time. "Yes," said Stone. "But I still don't like the bridge."

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Right, said Wren. She walked to the beginning of the spell. She read it again. This time, she read it forwards.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: "Fixing it," said tiny Wren. She raised her tiny hands. She said the spell again. Forwards, this time.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint sat down on a mossy rock. He looked at the map for a long time. It was very beautiful. It was also completely wrong.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They stayed for a long time. No one wanted to leave. The room was very quiet and very warm.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"Spark," said Glimmer.
"You are trying too hard."
"Fire is not thinking."
"It is feeling."
Spark looked at Glimmer for a long time.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"Have you been here before?" asked Burrow.
"Yes," said Luna.
She looked around the room.
"A very long time ago."
"What is it?" asked Burrow.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
They sat by the stream together.
Stone dripped for a long time.
The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.
And meant it.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
The magic seeds were gone.
The box that held them was open and empty.
Luna looked at the box for a long time.
"This is not good," she said.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James and Anna were in the garden. They had lots of big, flat boxes.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Anna grabbed her pen and drew the plan. "It needs big wings," she said, "and a pointed nose cone at the top."

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James got the red paint. Anna got the silver paint. They painted and painted until it shone!

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "It is the best rocket ever made!" said James. He and Anna stood back and grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: James and Anna played with Zim all day. They jumped so high on the moon!

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Time to go home," said Anna. "Come back soon!" called Zim, and he waved and waved.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James and Anna had a pet goat. His name was Chips. He was small and white with big brown patches.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "Oh, Chips!" said Anna. But she gave him a big hug. Chips licked her right on the nose.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. James grabbed the list. Anna grabbed the bags. Off they went!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. James grabbed the list. Anna grabbed the bags. Off they went!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Anna ran to find the bread. She picked the big round loaf with seeds on top. It smelled amazing!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Then Anna spotted the cake stand! Big cakes, small cakes, jam tarts and iced buns — all in a long, shining row.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James chose a big slice of lemon cake with thick white icing. Anna chose a pink strawberry jam tart.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James was not so sure. He made his most worried face all the way there. Anna held his hand.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: Anna found a book about sharks on the shelf. She sat down and read and read. She forgot to feel scared.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James came out. "It did not hurt at all!" he said. "And the chair goes UP and DOWN!" Anna laughed.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Well done, both of you," said Mum. "You were so brave today." They each got a sticker — James got a rocket, Anna got a star.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: At the end of the garden stood a big old oak tree. James and Anna had been staring at it for days.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Anna made a list. "We will need planks of wood, nails, rope, hinges and paint," she said. "And a flag."

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Dad did the tricky high bits — the tall planks and the big nails. James and Anna passed the tools and held the wood still.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Now for the best bit — the paint! James chose blue for the walls. Anna chose yellow for the door. Chips chewed the lid off the paint tin.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: James and Anna climbed up and sat at the little window. "This is the best thing we have ever made," said Anna.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: James and Anna climbed up and sat at the little window. "This is the best thing we have ever made," said Anna.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James and Anna were going to stay at Grandma's farm for the week. They packed their bags — and Chips got in the car too.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna found the duck pond. Three white ducks swam in slow circles. One waddled right up and ate seeds from Anna's hand.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna got to brush Bess's mane. James gave her a big red apple. Bess sniffed it — then snaffled the whole thing in one go!

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James chased Percy one way. Anna chased Percy the other way. Grandma just stood and laughed until her eyes watered.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna together. Grandma came and looked. "He fits in very well here," she said.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna did not want to be the dragon. She wanted to paint the big backdrop — the scenery behind the stage.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: At the very end, everyone stood and clapped. James and Anna walked to the front of the stage and bowed together.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mum and Dad clapped the loudest. Mum had tears. Dad said it was just the bright lights. James and Anna did not believe him.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. They were absolutely sure it would be fine. They were wrong.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: James brought Chips into the garden. Anna opened the gate. Bella bounded in like a very large, very furry rocket.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella crashed into the paddling pool. Water exploded in every direction. James and Anna were completely soaked.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "I think they like each other," said Anna. "They are just as bad as each other," said James.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: For their birthdays, James and Anna each got a new bike. James's was red. Anna's was purple.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They put on their helmets and walked the bikes outside. James could not wait. Anna checked the brakes first.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna set off nice and slowly. She did not wobble. She did not crash. She rode all the way to the end of the path and back.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: "How did you DO that?" said James. "I kept my eyes on where I wanted to go," said Anna. "Don't look at the ground."

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: On the way home, James and Anna raced. They crossed the gate post at exactly the same time. A perfect tie.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: That night their legs ached. But they were both smiling. "Same time tomorrow?" said James. Anna was already asleep.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: James and Anna helped bang in the tent pegs and thread the poles through. Chips ate one peg. Then he tried to eat a second.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "What if it comes back?" said James. "Then we will scare it," said Anna. She picked up the air horn Dad had packed.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They tried to sleep. Chips leaned on James. James leaned on Anna. Anna leaned on the tent wall. Nobody was quite comfortable.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They tried to sleep. Chips leaned on James. James leaned on Anna. Anna leaned on the tent wall. Nobody was quite comfortable.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Some trees lose their leaves in autumn. In winter, the branches are bare.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Some trees keep their leaves all year. They are called evergreen trees.

uses.title: Pets We Love
uses.pageText: A rabbit is a pet. Rabbits are soft and fluffy. They twitch their noses.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Lava can be as hot as 1,000 degrees. Some volcanoes are calm and slow. Their lava oozes out like very thick, very hot syrup.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are birds — but they cannot fly. Instead, they use their wings as flippers. They are brilliant swimmers.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins live in large groups called colonies. Some colonies have hundreds of thousands of penguins! Each penguin recognises its partner and its chick by their call.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Some spiders do not use webs at all. Jumping spiders leap onto their food. They have big eyes that face forward to judge distance. A jumping spider can leap 20 times its own body length!

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders have eight eyes, but many cannot see well. Instead, they feel vibrations through their legs. When something touches the web, the spider feels it instantly.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: In the deepest, darkest water, some creatures make their own light. This is called bioluminescence. The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure to attract prey.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage two: the egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar's only job is to eat. It eats and eats and grows and grows. Some caterpillars eat their own eggshell first!

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs are amphibians. Amphibians can live in water and on land. Frogs begin their life in water and later move onto land.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A frog's skin is always damp. Frogs can breathe through their skin as well as through their lungs. They must never dry out.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A frog's skin is always damp. Frogs can breathe through their skin as well as through their lungs. They must never dry out.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs sing to find a mate. Each species has its own call. The ribbit of a tree frog, the deep croak of a bullfrog — their calls fill warm evenings around the world.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At home, Mum made lunch. After, they had their cakes. Chips ate the paper bag. "CHIPS!" they said. But they were laughing too hard to be cross.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James and Anna were going to stay at Grandma's farm for the week. They packed their bags — and Chips got in the car too.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James put his hand straight up. "I want to be the dragon!" Six other children put their hands up too. They would all have to try out.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Their neighbour Mrs. Chen had a big, bouncy dog called Bella. "Would Chips like a play date?" Mrs. Chen asked one morning.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: For their birthdays, James and Anna each got a new bike. James's was red. Anna's was purple.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They put on their helmets and walked the bikes outside. James could not wait. Anna checked the brakes first.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They ate their sandwiches by the duck pond. Chips waited at home. Chips and bikes were definitely not a good idea.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: That night their legs ached. But they were both smiling. "Same time tomorrow?" said James. Anna was already asleep.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They packed their sleeping bags, a torch, a pack of cards, two books and lots of snacks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They made their display board on a rainy Saturday — a bright blue background, a photograph of each day's crystal growth, Betty's data chart, and a title in Aiden's best six-colour lettering: HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW?

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Socks was fascinated by both of them through this whole period. He kept trying to look in their mouths. He seemed to find it deeply interesting, which Aiden added to the field notebook under: Primate-specific dental curiosity — possible.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: I am going to the Long Meadow, said Grumpy. There is a good flat rock there. Peaceful. No one around. Chompy appeared. Can I come? said Chompy. Grumpy closed their eyes. Fine.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer stared at their own mouth. "Oh," said Glimmer. The fire had been inside all along. "I just needed to really mean it."

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: The remedy worked. Spark's cold was gone. The flowers slowly turned back to their usual colours. The fish returned to normal.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna gave one to each creature. One for each of them. The seeds glowed gently in their hands. Plant them this afternoon, said Luna.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
He found the acorn biscuits.
He put some in his pocket.
He was still asleep.
Glimmer covered their mouth.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Stone raised their hands high.
Pip and Spark added a little push.
The star spirits lifted.
Up.
And up.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone looked at the forest.
Then everyone looked at Glimmer.
Glimmer looked at the forest.
Glimmer looked at their own mouth.
"Oh," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Some trees keep their leaves all year. They are called evergreen trees.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: This is called pollination. Without bees, many plants could not make seeds. No seeds means no fruits or vegetables. We need bees very much.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Deep underground, rock gets so hot that it melts. This melted rock is called magma. Magma is hotter than anything you can imagine.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Sometimes, magma pushes up through a crack in the Earth. When it bursts out at the surface, we call it a volcano! The melted rock that flows out is called lava.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Most volcanoes are quiet for a very long time. Scientists called volcanologists watch them carefully. They use special equipment to spot the signs of an eruption.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins live in large groups called colonies. Some colonies have hundreds of thousands of penguins! Each penguin recognises its partner and its chick by their call.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks different every night. Sometimes it is a full, bright circle. Sometimes it is a thin crescent. These different shapes are called the phases of the Moon.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Plants use sunlight, water, and air to make food. This is called photosynthesis. It also makes the oxygen we breathe. Plants feed us and give us air!

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders are not insects. Insects have six legs. Spiders have eight legs. They belong to a group called arachnids.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Most spiders can make silk. The silk comes out of tiny organs called spinnerets. Spider silk is incredibly strong — stronger than steel wire of the same thickness!

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Coral looks like rock or plant, but it is an animal. Each piece of coral is made of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps. Coral reefs take thousands of years to grow.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: In the deepest, darkest water, some creatures make their own light. This is called bioluminescence. The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure to attract prey.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The deepest part of the ocean is called the Mariana Trench. It is nearly 11 kilometres deep. If you put the world's tallest mountain inside it, it would still be covered by water.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean makes more than half the oxygen we breathe. Tiny plants called phytoplankton float near the surface. They use sunlight to make oxygen. Every other breath you take came from the ocean.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: A butterfly's life has four stages. This is called a lifecycle. Each stage looks completely different from the one before.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage three: the caterpillar makes a hard shell around itself. This is called a chrysalis. Inside, an extraordinary change is about to happen.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A female frog lays hundreds of eggs in water. The eggs are called frogspawn. Each egg is surrounded by clear jelly that protects it and keeps it safe.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Time to go home," said Anna. "Come back soon!" called Zim, and he waved and waved.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "James!" called the dentist. He stood up. He walked in. The big chair went up and down like a ride!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma's farm was big and sunny. There were hens in the yard, ducks by the pond and a very fat pig called Percy.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma had a big brown horse called Bess. She was huge and gentle. Her nose was the softest thing James had ever felt.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mrs. Green told the class: "We are putting on a school play! It is called 'The Lost Dragon'."

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Their neighbour Mrs. Chen had a big, bouncy dog called Bella. "Would Chips like a play date?" Mrs. Chen asked one morning.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: Come in! called Sunny. It is lovely!

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Wake up, Dozy! called Bouncy. Dozy did not wake up.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Wake up, Dozy! called Zippy. Dozy did not wake up.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: WAKE UP, DOZY! called Honky. Dozy did not wake up.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Listen up! called Bossy. I have a plan!

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: MY SAIL! cried Fancy. Sorry! called Bouncy, already bouncing away.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy! called Sunny. Where are you going? I DON'T KNOW! called Zippy, already gone.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy! called Sunny. Where are you going? I DON'T KNOW! called Zippy, already gone.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: GOOD MORNING SUNNY HOLLOW! called Honky. Every leaf fell off every tree.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: IT IS OKAY! called Honky. Honky's voice was louder than the thunder. Dozy stopped shaking.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Bouncy thought it was a ghost. Zippy ran everywhere looking, very fast. Honky called out asking. Every leaf fell off.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: I have an announcement! called Bossy, megaphone raised. We are having the First Sunny Hollow Games. Tomorrow. Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: One day, Burrow got stuck on the other side of the stream. "Help!" called Burrow. "I cannot find the tunnel. Everything looks the same to me!"

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: What is the fish called? asked Pip. I... said Dewdrop. She stopped. She had forgotten to ask. She turned back toward the water.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: The memory room, said Luna. That is what it was called. She touched the wall very gently. I remember now.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Stone stood up and called out across the marsh.
It was the loudest sound Pip had ever heard.
Louder than the toadling.
Much louder.
Something answered from the far side of the marsh.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna called everyone together.
"The seeds keep Moonwood glowing," she said.
"Without them, the forest will grow dark."
Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James and Anna had a pet goat. His name was Chips. He was small and white with big brown patches.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips had a blue bell on his collar. JINGLE! JINGLE! JINGLE! You could hear him coming from far away!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips liked to eat. He ate the long green grass. He ate sticks and bits of bark. One day, he ate Dad's best hat!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said Dad. Chips blinked. He chewed. He looked the other way.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said Dad. Chips blinked. He chewed. He looked the other way.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James made Chips a lead from a long piece of rope. Now Chips could come on walks!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James made Chips a lead from a long piece of rope. Now Chips could come on walks!

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They set off down the lane. Chips trotted along and stopped to munch the long grass at the sides.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Then Chips saw a big rose bush. He ran at it. CRUNCH! MUNCH! SNAP! The rose bush was gone.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "Oh, Chips!" said Anna. But she gave him a big hug. Chips licked her right on the nose.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "Oh, Chips!" said Anna. But she gave him a big hug. Chips licked her right on the nose.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips ate it all in a flash. He looked at the bowl. Then he looked at James. Then he looked at James's jumper.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they both said. But they could not stop smiling. Chips was naughty and cheeky and silly — and they loved him so much.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they both said. But they could not stop smiling. Chips was naughty and cheeky and silly — and they loved him so much.

uses.pageText: At home, Mum made lunch. After, they had their cakes. Chips ate the paper bag. "CHIPS!" they said. But they were laughing too hard to be cross.

uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Now for the best bit — the paint! James chose blue for the walls. Anna chose yellow for the door. Chips chewed the lid off the paint tin.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Mum sent up a tray of juice and biscuits on a rope. Dad waved from below. Chips jangled at the base of the tree, trying to reach the biscuits.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James and Anna were going to stay at Grandma's farm for the week. They packed their bags — and Chips got in the car too.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Chips had been quiet all morning. Then they found him — in the veggie patch, eating the bean plants.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna together. Grandma came and looked. "He fits in very well here," she said.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James practised his dragon roar all week. It shook the windows. Mum wore earmuffs. Chips ran under the sofa.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Their neighbour Mrs. Chen had a big, bouncy dog called Bella. "Would Chips like a play date?" Mrs. Chen asked one morning.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: James brought Chips into the garden. Anna opened the gate. Bella bounded in like a very large, very furry rocket.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella chased Chips. Chips chased Bella. They ran round and round the garden at an absolutely ridiculous speed.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella chased Chips. Chips chased Bella. They ran round and round the garden at an absolutely ridiculous speed.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Chips jumped over the flower bed. Bella jumped after him. Daisies and petals flew in all directions.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: At last, both Chips and Bella lay down on the lawn side by side, panting. Chips licked Bella's ear. Bella licked Chips's nose.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: At last, both Chips and Bella lay down on the lawn side by side, panting. Chips licked Bella's ear. Bella licked Chips's nose.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mum brought out two bowls — water for Bella, chopped apple for Chips. Bella drank hers. Chips ate his. Then Chips ate Bella's water too.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mum brought out two bowls — water for Bella, chopped apple for Chips. Bella drank hers. Chips ate his. Then Chips ate Bella's water too.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mum brought out two bowls — water for Bella, chopped apple for Chips. Bella drank hers. Chips ate his. Then Chips ate Bella's water too.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They ate their sandwiches by the duck pond. Chips waited at home. Chips and bikes were definitely not a good idea.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They ate their sandwiches by the duck pond. Chips waited at home. Chips and bikes were definitely not a good idea.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: James and Anna helped bang in the tent pegs and thread the poles through. Chips ate one peg. Then he tried to eat a second.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Chips was coming too. He had his own little blanket and his bell, which jingled every single time he moved.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The marshmallow on Chips's stick got too close to the fire. It caught light. Chips ate the whole thing — stick and all.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They played cards in the tent by torchlight. Chips ate two cards before they noticed. The game got harder after that.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: At midnight, a fox barked in the lane. Chips went very still. James shone the torch outside. Nothing was there.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They tried to sleep. Chips leaned on James. James leaned on Anna. Anna leaned on the tent wall. Nobody was quite comfortable.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: In the morning, dew was on the grass and the birds sang. Chips had eaten a corner of the tent in the night.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they said. But the sun was warm and breakfast was good and it had been a perfect camp.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "Next year," said James, "we camp in a real field." "Next year," said Mum from the doorway, "Chips stays home." Chips ate the tent door zip.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "Next year," said James, "we camp in a real field." "Next year," said Mum from the doorway, "Chips stays home." Chips ate the tent door zip.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can be found on land and under the sea. When an underwater volcano keeps erupting, the lava builds up and can make a brand new island!

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Famous volcanoes can be found all around the world. Iceland, Hawaii and Italy all have active volcanoes. Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Further down, in the deep and dark, strange creatures live. Many have enormous eyes to see in the dim light. Some are found nowhere else on Earth.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James found the grapes. Red ones or green ones? He put both bunches in the basket — just to be safe.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: They found the cheese, the eggs and the juice. James was very careful with the eggs.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: Anna found a book about sharks on the shelf. She sat down and read and read. She forgot to feel scared.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna found the duck pond. Three white ducks swam in slow circles. One waddled right up and ate seeds from Anna's hand.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Chips had been quiet all morning. Then they found him — in the veggie patch, eating the bean plants.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: That evening, Grandma made soup from the garden and fried the eggs James had found. It was the best meal they had ever tasted.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Aiden spent the whole first morning at a rock pool near the headland. He found three kinds of crab, a sea anemone that closed when you touched it, and a tiny fish he thought might be a blenny. He wrote everything down in his field notebook in careful columns.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: Chompy found some leaves. I am still hungry, said Chompy.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Chompy had an idea. Chompy found the biggest, yummiest lunch in Sunny Hollow.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Sunny found Zippy. I was looking at a flower, said Zippy. I went past it twelve times first.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Every morning, the Dino Pals found a small gift on the Big Flat Rock. Nobody knew who left them.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Fancy woke up and found something terrible. Fancy's sail was bent. Not a little bent. Very bent.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: They reached the meadow. Grumpy found the flat rock and sat on it. Chompy found a berry patch immediately.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: They reached the meadow. Grumpy found the flat rock and sat on it. Chompy found a berry patch immediately.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "Try something scary," said Burrow. So Pip walked to the Tumblerock Cliffs. He found the high ledge and began to climb.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They reached the other side. Burrow found his glasses. Stone stood up straight.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: That evening, a Fog Marsh fox came creeping into Moonwood. It had found Fern's seed collection. The seeds were small and precious. Glimmer saw the fox.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren wanted to be taller. She had found a spell in her book. A growing spell, she was sure. She read it very carefully.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren found her spell book. It was enormous now. She climbed up onto it and looked at the spell. She had read it backwards.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: I have found something, Burrow told everyone. They gathered at the Hollow Oak. A door, said Burrow, underground. Very old. I don't know what is inside.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow found a blank patch of wall. He picked up a small flat stone. Very carefully, he drew the Hollow Oak. Now we are in it too, he said.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Wren found a cold remedy in her spell book. She read it very, very carefully. Forwards? said Spark. Forwards, said Wren.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the source, they found it.
A great boulder had fallen.
It lay across the singing stones.
The stones could not sing.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Burrow bumped the bench.
It fell over.
Burrow kept walking.
He found Pip's door.
He moved the boots with his paws.
He did not wake up.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
He found the acorn biscuits.
He put some in his pocket.
He was still asleep.
Glimmer covered their mouth.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren found the problem.
She had used the wrong book.
"This is the motion recipe," she said.
"Not the growing recipe."
She showed Fern.
They were both quiet for a moment.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop found Stone at the Hollow Oak.
"I need your hands," she said.
"Just to reach in and move a rock."
Stone understood immediately.
Then Stone understood all of it.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Stone's hand went into the stream.
It found the rock.
It gripped it.
Stone's face: very unhappy about this.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Pip searched the Fog Marsh.
He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Pip searched the Fog Marsh.
He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

He found three new things to map.
