He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Burrow went underground.
He searched every tunnel.
He found three interesting things.
He did not find any seeds.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"This way," said Flint.
He was right.
The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.
"I always find things," said Flint.
"Eventually."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Pip, Wren, Burrow, and Fern went inside to search.
They searched every room.
They found nothing.
Then Burrow's nose twitched.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
At the centre of the marsh, they found it.
A figure made of grey mist.
It sat against a dead tree.
It was very still.
It looked very sad.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Burrow found the underground path.
He could smell the way.
The creature stepped forward.
It knew this place.
"Here," it said.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They got home just in time for lunch. James filled Chips's bowl with fresh grass and sliced apple.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James found the grapes. Red ones or green ones? He put both bunches in the basket — just to be safe.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "The dentist is very kind," said Mum. "She just takes a little look inside your mouth. That is all."

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James pressed his nose flat to the glass. "That one looks just like a tiny striped rocket!" he said.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James chased Percy one way. Anna chased Percy the other way. Grandma just stood and laughed until her eyes watered.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mum and Dad clapped the loudest. Mum had tears. Dad said it was just the bright lights. James and Anna did not believe him.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "I think they like each other," said Anna. "They are just as bad as each other," said James.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Dad put up a big green tent in the back garden. "We are going camping!" he said. "Just for one night."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Aiden's tooth came out on a Thursday. Not dramatically — he was reading his book and he touched it and then it was just there in his fingers, which was very quick and very strange and did not hurt at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Dozy was up! I was just resting my eyes, said Dozy. Dozy's eyes were already closing again.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Grumpy. Not that I needed it. But Grumpy was smiling. Just a little.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Honky felt sad. I am just too loud, said Honky. Sorry. TOOT.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky helped clean Fancy's rock. Will you do any more pranks? asked Fancy. Maybe just one more, said Cheeky. And winked.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: They were the best gifts we ever had, said Sunny. Will you come and sit with us? Shy came out. Just a little way. But it was something.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy asked Sunny. You are wonderful just as you are! said Sunny. But what AM I? said Flappy. Wonderful! said Sunny. Flappy went away still confused.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: I can see everything from here, said Dream Dozy. We can always see everything, said Dream Sunny. You just need to be up high enough. Dozy thought about this.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy crossed the line first. Just. The second runner arrived a heartbeat later.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: But you didn't, said Sunny. Zippy ran four more circuits of Sunny Hollow. I know, said Zippy, on the third lap. I just like to make sure.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She said a growing spell. Just a small one. Just to help it along.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She said a growing spell. Just a small one. Just to help it along.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the first day: a small puff of smoke. Just smoke. No fire at all.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer did not think. Glimmer just ran toward the fox. Glimmer breathed in as hard as possible.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer stared at their own mouth. "Oh," said Glimmer. The fire had been inside all along. "I just needed to really mean it."

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop went back to the Crystal Stream. Why do you say things that are not true? she asked. She said it kindly. She just wanted to know.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the Hollow Oak, everyone heard it.
"The stream is singing again!" said Pip.
"We just moved a stone," said Fern.
"And asked the water nicely," said Dewdrop.
"It did the rest."

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer tried.
Smoke came out.
Just smoke.
"Interesting," said Spark, and wrote things down.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants walked into the Hollow Oak.
Some walked toward the Crystal Stream.
A very small plant walked very slowly toward Burrow's tunnel.
They were not in a hurry.
They were just walking.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop found Stone at the Hollow Oak.
"I need your hands," she said.
"Just to reach in and move a rock."
Stone understood immediately.
Then Stone understood all of it.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
"Just your arm," said Dewdrop.
"Just the one arm."
"Just for a moment."
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the water.
Stone sat down on the bank.

uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden added a new page to his field notebook: WHAT MAKES A GOOD EXPERIMENT. He had six points. Socks sat on the desk and watched him write, which Aiden had never seen him do before.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden wrote in his notebook: When something is unfair, you have two choices — pretend it isn't happening, or decide what to do. He starred the second option. He didn't quite know yet what doing something looked like.

uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The drive home was quiet in the way that follows something large. "What are you thinking about?" said Mum. Aiden and Betty both answered at the same time, with completely different answers. "That," said Mum, "is exactly right."

uses.pageText: Luna woke up knowing she had forgotten something important. She sat on her branch. She thought very hard. She could not remember what it was.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: This was the problem with forgetting things. You couldn't always remember what you had forgotten. Luna knew it was important. She knew it was today.

uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark put down his wand.
He put down his notes.
He stood very still.
He stopped thinking.
A small real flame came.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow went up to find Luna.
"Come with me," he said.
"Bring a light."
Luna said nothing.
She came.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna was very large for a tunnel.
She came anyway.
She did not say anything about this.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Pip reached the Crystal Stream.
He leaped from stone to stone.
One stone was slippery.
Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip told Luna.
Luna listened carefully.
"Something is wrong at the marsh," she said.
"We must go in."
Pip, Fern, and Dewdrop came too.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
There was a sign on the Hollow Oak door.
GLIMMER'S FIRE PERFORMANCE — TODAY.
Everyone came.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer breathed in.
Deeply.
Glimmer breathed out.
A jet of orange fire came out.
Small.
Perfect.
Real.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip knelt down.
He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: The stem grows tall. More leaves grow. It needs sun and water.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I learned to run and jump. I grew more every day.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Famous volcanoes can be found all around the world. Iceland, Hawaii and Italy all have active volcanoes. Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean covers more than two thirds of our planet. It is the largest habitat on Earth. And most of it is still unexplored.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean makes more than half the oxygen we breathe. Tiny plants called phytoplankton float near the surface. They use sunlight to make oxygen. Every other breath you take came from the ocean.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored. We know more about the surface of the Moon than we do about the deep ocean. There is so much left to discover.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored. We know more about the surface of the Moon than we do about the deep ocean. There is so much left to discover.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Over time, tunnels and chambers form underground. Some cave systems stretch for hundreds of kilometres. The Mammoth Cave system in America has more than 650 kilometres of passages.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: Chompy ate some berries. More, please! said Chompy.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: Chompy ate and ate. More, please! said Chompy.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: Oh YES! said Sunny. More puddles!

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Shh! said Grumpy. SORRY! said Honky. More leaves fell.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky helped clean Fancy's rock. Will you do any more pranks? asked Fancy. Maybe just one more, said Cheeky. And winked.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky helped clean Fancy's rock. Will you do any more pranks? asked Fancy. Maybe just one more, said Cheeky. And winked.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried eating leaves. Fine. Flappy tried catching insects mid-air. Remarkably good at this. Flappy was more surprised.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Grumpy has a strong tail, said Sunny. Grumpy swung the club tail at the rocks. CLONK. One small rock moved. There were fifty more.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: There would be a running race, a jumping contest, a loudness competition, and a prize for the tidiest corner of the Hollow. More events to be decided, said Bossy. I have a clipboard.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Chompy was there, but all the food was made of more clouds. This is disappointing, said Dream Chompy.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: But you didn't, said Sunny. Zippy ran four more circuits of Sunny Hollow. I know, said Zippy, on the third lap. I just like to make sure.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: Grumpy had some more cake.

uses.title: Hungry Eats Everything
uses.pageText: Hungry ate one more bit of grass.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: "More hugs!" said Cuddly.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: "No more hugs," said Woolly.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "Maybe you need to try harder," said Spark. Spark's own magic crackled around his ears. Glimmer tried harder. More smoke came out. Still no fire.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Luna flew in through the window. She looked at the desk. She looked more closely. "Wren?" said Luna.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: He polished his glasses and looked more closely. On the door was a small carving. A tree with roots going in every direction. It was very old.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark tried.
Sparkles shot everywhere.
His hat fell off.
His feet stayed on the ground.
"I think I need more practice," said Spark.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer ran.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer jumped.
Glimmer glided five whole steps.
"That's more," said Spark.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
The next night, it happened again.
More things had moved.
"Was it you?" asked Stone.
"No," said Pip.
"Was it you?" asked Pip.
"No," said everyone.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren stirred the potion.
It was meant to be green.
It was more purple.
Wren did not notice this.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Everything was back.
"I'm sorry," said Wren.
"Did you learn something?" asked Fern.
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
When the edge was clear, the spirit stood.
Its shape was clearer now.
"Thank you," said the spirit.
It was not mist anymore.
It was something more solid.
Something more itself.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
When the edge was clear, the spirit stood.
Its shape was clearer now.
"Thank you," said the spirit.
It was not mist anymore.
It was something more solid.
Something more itself.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Moonwood blazed with gold.
Every mushroom.
Every lamp.
Every glowing stone.
The forest was more beautiful than anyone had ever seen it.

uses.title: The Sun
uses.pageText: The sun helps us see.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText: I see all the colors!

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: I see with my eyes.

uses.title: Our Five Senses
uses.pageText: We use our eyes to see.

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
A bug can hide.
Can you see it?

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText:
I see shapes!
Shapes are all around.

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText: I see a big red barn.

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see a fat pig.
Oink!

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see a little chick.
Peep!

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see a big cow.
Moo!

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see green grass.
I see hay.

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see green grass.
I see hay.

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see a big dog.
It runs fast.

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I love the farm!
I can see so much.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have two eyes.
I can see.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Colours are all around us! What colour can you see?

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: An owl can see in the dark. It hunts at night. Twit-twoo!

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A star has five points. We see stars in the night sky.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: Look up at night. You can see the moon! The moon is big and round.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon is far away. But we can see it every night.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can see. My eyes let me see colours and shapes.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can see. My eyes let me see colours and shapes.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: Five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. I use them every day!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have eyes to see. I have ears to hear. I have a nose to smell.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon does not make its own light. It has no fire or glow inside. The light we see is sunlight bouncing off the Moon's surface.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: You can see the Moon most nights. On a clear night with a telescope, you can see the craters clearly. Look up tonight — the Moon is always there.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: You can see the Moon most nights. On a clear night with a telescope, you can see the craters clearly. Look up tonight — the Moon is always there.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders have eight eyes, but many cannot see well. Instead, they feel vibrations through their legs. When something touches the web, the spider feels it instantly.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Further down, in the deep and dark, strange creatures live. Many have enormous eyes to see in the dim light. Some are found nowhere else on Earth.

uses.title: Nan and Bob go to the Zoo
uses.pageText: Nan and Bob see the big fish.

uses.title: Nan and Bob go to the Zoo
uses.pageText: Bob and Nan see the big ape.

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: Bob can see six big candles.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James ran to see the hens. "They have laid five eggs!" he said. He put them one by one — very, very carefully — into a basket.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Then the lights went up and James walked on stage. He could see the WHOLE school in the dark. His legs went very wobbly.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: The sun came back out. See? said Sunny. Every day is a good day!

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Clumsy looked in from a great height. It looks fine to me, said Clumsy. You cannot even see your own feet, said Fancy.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Clumsy could see over all the ferns, past the waterfall, all the way to the Long Meadow and beyond.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can see the mud puddle, said Clumsy. I can see the berry bushes. I can see Chompy at the berry bushes, which is not a surprise.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can see the mud puddle, said Clumsy. I can see the berry bushes. I can see Chompy at the berry bushes, which is not a surprise.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can see the mud puddle, said Clumsy. I can see the berry bushes. I can see Chompy at the berry bushes, which is not a surprise.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Can you see the pillow? said Dozy. There was a long pause. Oh, said Clumsy. Yes. It is in the waterfall.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: The pool was too deep to reach in. I cannot see my feet, said Clumsy. I certainly cannot reach the bottom.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: We make a good team, said Clumsy. You see the problem. I reach the problem. Exactly, said Clumsy, and accidentally knocked off Wiggly's hat. Sorry.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: The tidiest corner prize went to Shy. Shy had arranged twelve perfect pebbles behind a rock where nobody could see them. It counts, said Bossy carefully.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: I can see everything from here, said Dream Dozy. We can always see everything, said Dream Sunny. You just need to be up high enough. Dozy thought about this.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: I can see everything from here, said Dream Dozy. We can always see everything, said Dream Sunny. You just need to be up high enough. Dozy thought about this.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Burrow smiled. "The stone doesn't do anything," he said. "I wanted to see what you would do. And you were brave."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: This is a seed. It is tiny. Seeds come in many shapes.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A seahorse is tiny. It holds on to plants.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A ladybird is red with black spots. It eats tiny greenfly.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: An ant is tiny. Ants work together. Ants carry food.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: When I was a baby, I was tiny. I could not walk or talk.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: When the egg hatches, a tiny chick comes out. The chick has thick grey fluffy feathers. It cuddles close to its parent to stay warm.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Almost every plant starts as a tiny seed. Seeds come in hundreds of different shapes and sizes. Each one holds everything a plant needs to begin life.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Most spiders can make silk. The silk comes out of tiny organs called spinnerets. Spider silk is incredibly strong — stronger than steel wire of the same thickness!

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Female spiders lay eggs in a silk sac. The sac protects the eggs. When they hatch, tiny spiderlings emerge. Some mothers carry the sac everywhere.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: Coral looks like rock or plant, but it is an animal. Each piece of coral is made of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps. Coral reefs take thousands of years to grow.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean makes more than half the oxygen we breathe. Tiny plants called phytoplankton float near the surface. They use sunlight to make oxygen. Every other breath you take came from the ocean.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage one: the butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf. The eggs are very small — some are no bigger than a pinhead. The leaf is food for the caterpillar inside.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James pressed his nose flat to the glass. "That one looks just like a tiny striped rocket!" he said.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Aiden spent the whole first morning at a rock pool near the headland. He found three kinds of crab, a sea anemone that closed when you touched it, and a tiny fish he thought might be a blenny. He wrote everything down in his field notebook in careful columns.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He held it up for a long time. It was tiny. It was the smallest thing that had ever felt significant. He put it in the small envelope Mum left for him, and when he placed it under his pillow it felt ceremonial.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Sunny saw two small eyes behind a rock. And two small pink paws placing a tiny woven grass bracelet on the rock.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Then Chompy fell into a ditch. HELP, said Chompy. It was not a deep ditch. But Chompy's arms were very tiny.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny is small.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny cannot reach the top.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny cannot open the big door.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny cannot jump the gap.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: But Tiny can fit in the pot.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny can fit in the bag.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny can fit in the log.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText:
Tiny went past.
"Come and play!"
Shy hid.

uses.title: Hungry Eats Everything
uses.pageText:
Hungry ate the map.
"My map!" said Tiny.

uses.title: Speedy Slows Down
uses.pageText: "Over here!" said Tiny.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: Tiny has lost a hat.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: The hat was on Tiny.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: "Oh," said Tiny.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: Tiny got the wool off.

uses.title: Grumpy's Secret
uses.pageText: Tiny went to look.

uses.title: Grumpy's Secret
uses.pageText: Tiny told everyone.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Tiny hung up the flags.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip was walking through Moonwood when his foot kicked something small. It was a tiny stone. It glowed with a soft gold light.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: "Fixing it," said tiny Wren. She raised her tiny hands. She said the spell again. Forwards, this time.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: "Fixing it," said tiny Wren. She raised her tiny hands. She said the spell again. Forwards, this time.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Inside was a small round room. The walls were covered in tiny glowing drawings. Trees and streams. Creatures and old paths. Every living thing that had ever been in Moonwood.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
It was late in the Hollow Oak.
Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"Hello," said Fern.
The tiny creature looked up.
"Have you seen my spectacles?" she said.
"I've been looking for three days."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"I am Twig," said the tiny creature.
"I live here."
"I have always lived here."
She seemed perfectly happy about this.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Let us make a rocket!" said James. "We can fly all the way into space!"

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said Dad. Chips blinked. He chewed. He looked the other way.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James was not so sure. He made his most worried face all the way there. Anna held his hand.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: The tree house was done! Blue walls, a yellow door, a red star flag and a rope ladder all the way to the ground.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James chased Percy one way. Anna chased Percy the other way. Grandma just stood and laughed until her eyes watered.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James chased Percy one way. Anna chased Percy the other way. Grandma just stood and laughed until her eyes watered.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna set off nice and slowly. She did not wobble. She did not crash. She rode all the way to the end of the path and back.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: By lunchtime, they could both ride all the way down the long lane and back without stopping once.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: On the way home, James and Anna raced. They crossed the gate post at exactly the same time. A perfect tie.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The last day of the summer term was also the loudest day of the school year. Aiden and Betty burst through the front door and both shouted "HOLIDAY!" at exactly the same moment, which echoed all the way up the stairs and made the dog next door bark.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He loves shiny objects," Uncle Eddie explained at dinner. "He adores warm spots — the airing cupboard is a particular risk. And if he gets bored, he will find a way to become interesting." Everyone filed this information away carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor had noticed, in the way that good teachers always notice. She started a class discussion about what it means to be fair, and what you do when things aren't. Several children looked at the floor. Marcus looked at the window.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The drive home was quiet in the way that follows something large. "What are you thinking about?" said Mum. Aiden and Betty both answered at the same time, with completely different answers. "That," said Mum, "is exactly right."

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Bossy, said Sunny, can we try YOUR way AND our way? They worked together. It worked!

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Bossy, said Sunny, can we try YOUR way AND our way? They worked together. It worked!

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: They were the best gifts we ever had, said Sunny. Will you come and sit with us? Shy came out. Just a little way. But it was something.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Clumsy could see over all the ferns, past the waterfall, all the way to the Long Meadow and beyond.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Sneezy entered the farthest-blast competition. Sneezy's sneeze sent the test leaf all the way to the Long Meadow. The judge had to run to collect the result. Zippy collected it. Obviously.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: Grumpy ran. Woolly ran. Not the same way.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: His legs felt wobbly. The ground was a long way below. But he did not stop. He reached the top.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren looked at her hands. Her hands were a very long way away. She was not taller. She was one inch tall.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He drew as he walked. He mapped the Crystal Stream path. He mapped the way to Tumblerock Cliffs. He drew everything carefully.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
The water rushed over the singing stones.
And the Crystal Stream began to sing.
First very quietly.
Then louder.
Then loud enough to hear all the way to the Hollow Oak.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"I wonder," said Wren.
She closed her spell book.
She spoke to the mushroom.
Very quietly.
She asked it the way.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
The mushroom's glow changed.
It pulsed once — pointing.
Another mushroom far away pulsed the same way.
And another.
A trail of glowing mushrooms lit up through the trees.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"This way," said Flint.
He was right.
The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.
"I always find things," said Flint.
"Eventually."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop crossed the finish line.
She had glided the whole way.
She was not wet.
She was not ruffled.
"Finished," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The Deep Dark was very dark.
The trees had no glow.
The light went only a little way ahead.
They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Burrow found the underground path.
He could smell the way.
The creature stepped forward.
It knew this place.
"Here," it said.

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText: Shapes are all around!

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText: Earth moves around the sun.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText: The moon moves around Earth.

uses.title: Water
uses.pageText:
Water is all around!
We need water.

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
Bugs are all around!
They are little.

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText:
I see shapes!
Shapes are all around.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Colours are all around us! What colour can you see?

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: Bugs are all around us. Big bugs. Small bugs. Look closely!

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon goes around the Earth. It travels very slowly.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: The Earth spins around. That is why we have day and night.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: Water is all around us. Oceans, rivers, and rain.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Famous volcanoes can be found all around the world. Iceland, Hawaii and Italy all have active volcanoes. Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage three: the caterpillar makes a hard shell around itself. This is called a chrysalis. Inside, an extraordinary change is about to happen.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs sing to find a mate. Each species has its own call. The ribbit of a tree frog, the deep croak of a bullfrog — their calls fill warm evenings around the world.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: It was quiet. Nobody laughed. Marcus said something low, but nobody around him responded. Aiden walked on. His legs were slightly shaky — but he hadn't shown it, and he was extremely proud of himself.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: It was very quiet. Zippy looked around. There were flowers. There was a big blue sky.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: I am going to the Long Meadow, said Grumpy. There is a good flat rock there. Peaceful. No one around. Chompy appeared. Can I come? said Chompy. Grumpy closed their eyes. Fine.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "Maybe you need to try harder," said Spark. Spark's own magic crackled around his ears. Glimmer tried harder. More smoke came out. Still no fire.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Oh, said Wren. Her voice came out very small. Everything around her was enormous.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He looked around to show someone. He was alone. The forest around him looked very different to the forest on his map.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He looked around to show someone. He was alone. The forest around him looked very different to the forest on his map.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow was digging a new tunnel. He dug down, and he dug sideways, and he dug carefully around the roots. Then his spade hit something hard and wooden.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow set down his spade. He felt around it very carefully. It was a door. A small, very old wooden door, deep underground.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They all came to look. The tunnel was small. Stone had to go sideways. Luna had to be helped around three corners.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark tried to hold the sneeze in. His eyes went watery. His magic began to build and build. The sparkles around him grew very bright.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: They planted the seeds in a ring around the Hollow Oak. One from each of them. In the golden afternoon light.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.
"Ready?" said Fern.
"Ready," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"We are here," said Flint.
He pointed at the map.
Wren looked around.
Grey fog was appearing between the trees.
"That is the Fog Marsh," said Wren.
"We are not near the meadow."

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna walked slowly around the room.
She touched the carvings.
They lit up where she touched.
Blue and gold.
She had been here before.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"Have you been here before?" asked Burrow.
"Yes," said Luna.
She looked around the room.
"A very long time ago."
"What is it?" asked Burrow.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
In the morning, Burrow woke up.
He looked around.
Pip and Glimmer were standing in front of him.
"Good morning," said Burrow.
There was a long pause.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Then all the plants began to walk.
They were very polite about it.
They walked around Fern.
They walked around Wren.
They went for a stroll.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Then all the plants began to walk.
They were very polite about it.
They walked around Fern.
They walked around Wren.
They went for a stroll.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop searched the stream.
Fern walked slowly around the clearing.
She was not searching.
She was listening.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern looked around the room.
Then she looked at Twig.
The spectacles were on top of Twig's head.
They had been there all along.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The creature ran to its family.
The family gathered around it.
They looked at the Moonwood creatures.
Not afraid.
Just looking.
Then one of them blinked.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: We can help bees by planting flowers. Bees love lavender, sunflowers, and daisies. Even a small garden or a pot of flowers can help.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins live in large groups called colonies. Some colonies have hundreds of thousands of penguins! Each penguin recognises its partner and its chick by their call.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's surface is covered in craters. Craters are bowl-shaped holes made by space rocks crashing into the Moon long ago. Some craters are bigger than cities.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: After pollination, the flower makes seeds. The seeds grow inside the plant protected by a pod, a fruit, or a shell.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Seeds travel away from the parent plant. Some fly on the wind. Some stick to animals' fur. Some are eaten by birds and fall far away. Some float on water.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The deepest part of the ocean is called the Mariana Trench. It is nearly 11 kilometres deep. If you put the world's tallest mountain inside it, it would still be covered by water.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are hollow spaces underground or inside cliffs. They form in many different ways. Some are made by water, some by sea waves, and some by ancient flowing lava.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are hollow spaces underground or inside cliffs. They form in many different ways. Some are made by water, some by sea waves, and some by ancient flowing lava.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are hollow spaces underground or inside cliffs. They form in many different ways. Some are made by water, some by sea waves, and some by ancient flowing lava.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are home to many animals. Bats sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings by day. At dusk, thousands of bats fly out together to feed on insects in the night air.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A female frog lays hundreds of eggs in water. The eggs are called frogspawn. Each egg is surrounded by clear jelly that protects it and keeps it safe.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: BANG! BANG! BANG! went the hammer. WHIRR! went the drill. The frame went up bit by bit.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma's farm was big and sunny. There were hens in the yard, ducks by the pond and a very fat pig called Percy.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James ran to see the hens. "They have laid five eggs!" he said. He put them one by one — very, very carefully — into a basket.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: At last, both Chips and Bella lay down on the lawn side by side, panting. Chips licked Bella's ear. Bella licked Chips's nose.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: By lunchtime, they could both ride all the way down the long lane and back without stopping once.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They ate their sandwiches by the duck pond. Chips waited at home. Chips and bikes were definitely not a good idea.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They played cards in the tent by torchlight. Chips ate two cards before they noticed. The game got harder after that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They had set up a lemonade stand beside the sale table — Betty's idea, planned the previous Thursday. Aiden poured from a glass jug. Betty collected the money and kept the queue moving. By one o'clock they had sold every cup and run entirely out of lemons.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Socks was fascinated by both of them through this whole period. He kept trying to look in their mouths. He seemed to find it deeply interesting, which Aiden added to the field notebook under: Primate-specific dental curiosity — possible.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The dungeon was underground and smelled of cold stone and old air. Betty read every board by torchlight. Aiden stood still in the near-dark for a moment and thought about how this exact place had been here through everything — and felt briefly, appropriately small.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: One by one, the Dino Pals joined in.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText: Cuddly sat down by the barn.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: That evening, Pip sat by the Crystal Stream. He looked at the stone. The gold glow had gone out.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By afternoon, the plant had grown through the roof. It was still growing. Everyone stood back and watched.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By evening, it was a large, beautiful plant beside the Hollow Oak. Not too small. Not too large. Luna came out through the door.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop was not sure any of this was true. She knew the Deep Dark secrets. They were kept by a very old badger, not a fish.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow sat very still and listened.
The room grew warmer.
The carvings lit up one by one.
Luna's voice was quiet and certain.
She had always known these stories.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
"It was you," said Pip gently. "You sleep-dig."
"I am very sorry," said Burrow.
He put his boot by the door.
"Will that stop you?" asked Glimmer.
"I don't know," said Burrow.
"I am asleep."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
They sat by the stream together.
Stone dripped for a long time.
The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.
And meant it.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
By the end of the week, the fog had crept closer.
The mushrooms at the edge were going out.
One by one.
The fog was not stopping.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
By the end of the week, the fog had crept closer.
The mushrooms at the edge were going out.
One by one.
The fog was not stopping.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
That evening, the fog stayed at the line.
The mushrooms began to come back on.
One by one.
Pip watched them light up.
The marsh was where it should be.
The forest was where it should be.

uses.title: How Things Grow
uses.pageText: A seed grows into a plant.

uses.title: How Things Grow
uses.pageText: A tadpole turns into a frog.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A flower blooms! The seed has grown into a plant.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have a tummy. Food goes into my tummy. Rumble!

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Other volcanoes are very explosive. They blast ash, smoke and rocks high into the sky. The blast can be heard hundreds of kilometres away.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: After a volcano, the cooled lava becomes new rock. Volcanic rock breaks down into rich, dark soil. Many plants and crops grow very well in volcanic soil.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's surface is covered in craters. Craters are bowl-shaped holes made by space rocks crashing into the Moon long ago. Some craters are bigger than cities.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage two: the egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar's only job is to eat. It eats and eats and grows and grows. Some caterpillars eat their own eggshell first!

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Most caves form when rainwater seeps into limestone rock. The water is slightly acidic. It slowly dissolves the rock away. This takes thousands and thousands of years.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Let us make a rocket!" said James. "We can fly all the way into space!"

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Up, up, up went the rocket! They shot past the white clouds and into the deep, dark sky.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Then James tried riding with NO hands. He made it exactly three seconds before heading straight into the same bush.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Lava can be as hot as 1,000 degrees. Some volcanoes are calm and slow. Their lava oozes out like very thick, very hot syrup.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins live in large groups called colonies. Some colonies have hundreds of thousands of penguins! Each penguin recognises its partner and its chick by their call.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's surface is covered in craters. Craters are bowl-shaped holes made by space rocks crashing into the Moon long ago. Some craters are bigger than cities.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Seeds travel away from the parent plant. Some fly on the wind. Some stick to animals' fur. Some are eaten by birds and fall far away. Some float on water.
