uses.pageText: Can WE help? said all the Dino Pals. NO! said Grumpy.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Oh, fine, said Grumpy quietly. All the Dino Pals helped together. POP!

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: All the Dino Pals looked at Bouncy. Sorry, said Bouncy, smiling.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: I like your tail, said Dozy sleepily. It fans me while I nap. The Dino Pals all agreed.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Then a thunderstorm came. Dozy woke up frightened. All the Dino Pals hid.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Now Cheeky was muddy. The Dino Pals looked at Cheeky. Cheeky looked at the Dino Pals.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Now Cheeky was muddy. The Dino Pals looked at Cheeky. Cheeky looked at the Dino Pals.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Every morning, the Dino Pals found a small gift on the Big Flat Rock. Nobody knew who left them.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: The Dino Pals went to look. A huge pile of rocks had fallen in the night and blocked the stream above.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose began to twitch. The Dino Pals turned to look. Oh no, said Bossy. Oh yes, said Wiggly.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Back in the meadow, Dozy's eyes opened. All the Dino Pals were sitting in a circle, waiting. What was it like? said Sunny.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: The Dino Pals cheered. Honky cheered loudest. Every leaf fell off every tree in the whole valley.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie was Dad's younger brother, and he was a wildlife researcher who had spent the last two years living near a tropical rainforest, studying primates. He had, apparently, brought one with him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He loves shiny objects," Uncle Eddie explained at dinner. "He adores warm spots — the airing cupboard is a particular risk. And if he gets bored, he will find a way to become interesting." Everyone filed this information away carefully.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is spring. Flowers pop up. Birds sing.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Flowers and trees are plants. They need sun, soil, and water.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: We can help bees by planting flowers. Bees love lavender, sunflowers, and daisies. Even a small garden or a pot of flowers can help.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: We can help bees by planting flowers. Bees love lavender, sunflowers, and daisies. Even a small garden or a pot of flowers can help.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees work hard every day. They help flowers grow. They make our world sweeter. Bees are amazing.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Back in the meadow, Dozy's eyes opened. All the Dino Pals were sitting in a circle, waiting. What was it like? said Sunny.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: The Dino Pals cheered. Honky cheered loudest. Every leaf fell off every tree in the whole valley.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText:
A ball is round.
It is a circle.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
An orange is round.
It is bright.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
A grape is small.
It is round.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText:
A little cub.
It is round and brown.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText:
The moon is big.
It is round.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A circle is round. The sun is a circle. A wheel is a circle.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: Look up at night. You can see the moon! The moon is big and round.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They flew past big round planets. Some had red spots. Some had wide, shining rings!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Anna ran to find the bread. She picked the big round loaf with seeds on top. It smelled amazing!

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Then Percy the pig got out. He ran in and out of the hen house and round and round the yard at top speed.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Then Percy the pig got out. He ran in and out of the hen house and round and round the yard at top speed.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella chased Chips. Chips chased Bella. They ran round and round the garden at an absolutely ridiculous speed.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella chased Chips. Chips chased Bella. They ran round and round the garden at an absolutely ridiculous speed.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Inside was a small round room. The walls were covered in tiny glowing drawings. Trees and streams. Creatures and old paths. Every living thing that had ever been in Moonwood.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then — a sound.
A shuffling.
A round shape moving through the clearing.
Pip and Glimmer looked at each other.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText: The sun is a big star.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A star has five points. We see stars in the night sky.

uses.title: Hello, Sun!
uses.pageText: The sun is a big, hot star. It is very far away.

uses.title: Hello, Sun!
uses.pageText: The sun is our nearest star. Thank you, sun!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Well done, both of you," said Mum. "You were so brave today." They each got a sticker — James got a rocket, Anna got a star.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: The tree house was done! Blue walls, a yellow door, a red star flag and a rope ladder all the way to the ground.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"What are you?" asked Pip.
The star spirit blinked its large gold eyes.
"Star," it said.
Its voice was very small.
"Fell," it added.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"What are you?" asked Pip.
The star spirit blinked its large gold eyes.
"Star," it said.
Its voice was very small.
"Fell," it added.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They gathered the star spirits.
There were many of them.
Stone held several.
Wren had two in her hat.
They kept bouncing.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Stone raised their hands high.
Pip and Spark added a little push.
The star spirits lifted.
Up.
And up.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They set off down the lane. Chips trotted along and stopped to munch the long grass at the sides.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy stopped. Where was Sunny Hollow? Zippy had never stopped before.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy stopped. Where was Sunny Hollow? Zippy had never stopped before.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: IT IS OKAY! called Honky. Honky's voice was louder than the thunder. Dozy stopped shaking.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: One morning, Rainbow Waterfall was not making rainbows. It was not making anything at all. The waterfall had stopped.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: They set off. Grumpy walked steadily. Chompy stopped to eat something every thirty steps.

uses.title: Bouncy Won't Stop
uses.pageText: Bouncy stopped.

uses.title: Giggly Has the Hiccups
uses.pageText: Then Giggly stopped.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: The plant stopped growing. The leaves curled gently inward. Then, slowly, it began to shrink.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: What is the fish called? asked Pip. I... said Dewdrop. She stopped. She had forgotten to ask. She turned back toward the water.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it something to do with the Crystal Stream? asked Dewdrop. Luna stopped walking. She looked at the stream for a moment. Wait, said Luna.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
The toadling stopped when it saw them.
Everything was suddenly very quiet.
"Oh," said Pip.
"Oh," said Stone.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark put down his wand.
He put down his notes.
He stood very still.
He stopped thinking.
A small real flame came.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Fern stopped.
She knelt down.
There were small green shoots in the ground.
They glowed.
Just a little.
Just like the seeds.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I got stronger. I took my first steps!

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James took a deep breath. He thought of his best roar. Then he let it out — the biggest, loudest roar he had ever done.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy bumped into Sneezy. Sneezy took a HUGE breath in...

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy walked home. Slowly. It took ages. Zippy loved it.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy took a breath in. The biggest breath anyone in Sunny Hollow had ever taken. The ferns bent backwards.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint took out a new piece of parchment. "I'll make another one," he said. He was not upset about this. He had always known the paths would move.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark breathed in carefully. I think, he said, I might need to sneeze again. Everyone took a large step back.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren poured the potion on the plants.
The plants stood very straight.
Then they leaned.
Then one of them took a step.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
They split into groups.
Each group took a different path.
Each path led somewhere different.
"Find the seeds," said Luna.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Trees have roots under the soil. Roots hold the tree up.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Some trees lose their leaves in autumn. In winter, the branches are bare.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Some trees keep their leaves all year. They are called evergreen trees.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Some trees keep their leaves all year. They are called evergreen trees.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Flowers and trees are plants. They need sun, soil, and water.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Some butterflies migrate thousands of kilometres. The monarch butterfly flies from Canada to Mexico every year — a journey of 4,000 kilometres. They always find the same trees.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The far bank was different — thicker trees, softer ground, a field of tall meadow grass beyond the treeline. Socks bounded ahead, turning back every few steps to make sure they were following.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: But dinosaurs do not nest in trees, said Flappy. You do, said Grumpy. And birds do not live in Sunny Hollow with everyone else. You do, said Grumpy.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Inside was a small round room. The walls were covered in tiny glowing drawings. Trees and streams. Creatures and old paths. Every living thing that had ever been in Moonwood.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
They stood at the edge together.
The fog was thick and grey-green.
The noise bounced off the twisted trees.
"Together," said Stone.
Pip nodded.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
An hour later, nothing looked right.
The trees were wrong.
The paths had gone.
"Where are we?" asked Wren.
Flint checked his map.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"We are here," said Flint.
He pointed at the map.
Wren looked around.
Grey fog was appearing between the trees.
"That is the Fog Marsh," said Wren.
"We are not near the meadow."

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
The mushroom's glow changed.
It pulsed once — pointing.
Another mushroom far away pulsed the same way.
And another.
A trail of glowing mushrooms lit up through the trees.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Inside the marsh, it was colder.
The trees drooped.
The water did not move.
Dewdrop led them through the fog.
She could feel the water.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The Deep Dark was very dark.
The trees had no glow.
The light went only a little way ahead.
They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText: The cloud is white.

uses.title: The Sky
uses.pageText:
A cloud is up.
It is white.

uses.title: Hot and Cold
uses.pageText:
Snow is cold.
It is white.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText:
A little lamb.
It is white.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is snowy. White flakes fall. Everything looks white.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is snowy. White flakes fall. Everything looks white.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A daisy is small and white. It grows in the grass.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: People have been to the moon! They wore big white suits.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Rocks can be many colours. Grey, brown, red, and white.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Up, up, up went the rocket! They shot past the white clouds and into the deep, dark sky.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James and Anna had a pet goat. His name was Chips. He was small and white with big brown patches.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James chose a big slice of lemon cake with thick white icing. Anna chose a pink strawberry jam tart.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna found the duck pond. Three white ducks swam in slow circles. One waddled right up and ate seeds from Anna's hand.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText: The sun is yellow.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
A big sun.
It is yellow.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
Red and blue.
Yellow and green.
So many colors!

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
A bee is yellow.
It can sting.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
A banana is yellow.
It is soft.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
It is red! It is yellow!
I love fruit!

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText:
A little chick.
It is yellow.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Yellow. A yellow sun. A yellow duck.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Yellow. A yellow sun. A yellow duck.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Yellow. A yellow sun. A yellow duck.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: After rain, look up! A rainbow! Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A sunflower is tall and yellow. The sun makes it grow.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText: A baby hen is a chick. A chick is soft and yellow.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Now for the best bit — the paint! James chose blue for the walls. Anna chose yellow for the door. Chips chewed the lid off the paint tin.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: The tree house was done! Blue walls, a yellow door, a red star flag and a rope ladder all the way to the ground.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Grumpy's Secret
uses.pageText: Big red flowers. Big yellow flowers.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: That night their legs ached. But they were both smiling. "Same time tomorrow?" said James. Anna was already asleep.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Aiden had started a new notebook that evening — not the Socks field study, but a nature notebook. He had titled it with the date. Betty had started a matching one, without them discussing it. Both were already half a page in.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Dozy was up! I was just resting my eyes, said Dozy. Dozy's eyes were already closing again.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: MY SAIL! cried Fancy. Sorry! called Bouncy, already bouncing away.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy! called Sunny. Where are you going? I DON'T KNOW! called Zippy, already gone.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a pile of extra berries for Chompy. Someone knows me very well, said Chompy, already eating them.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a leafy fan for Dozy. This is perfect, said Dozy, already asleep with it.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Clumsy stood tall and looked out over the whole Hollow. The storm is coming from the east, said Clumsy. The tall ferns are already bending. That gives us time.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly. They always did.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They arrived at the Whispering Meadow.
It was exactly where they had been going.
Flint wrote something on his map.
"Mushroom trail," he said.
"I should have had that already."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
A pink pig.
A pink flower.

uses.title: A Seed Grows
uses.pageText:
A flower!
A seed can grow big.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A flower blooms! The seed has grown into a plant.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A flower has petals. A flower has a stem. A flower has roots.

uses.pageText: A flower has petals. A flower has a stem. A flower has roots.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A flower has petals. A flower has a stem. A flower has roots.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: A tree is big. A flower is small.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: After pollination, the flower makes seeds. The seeds grow inside the plant protected by a pod, a fruit, or a shell.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Chips jumped over the flower bed. Bella jumped after him. Daisies and petals flew in all directions.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Sunny found Zippy. I was looking at a flower, said Zippy. I went past it twelve times first.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: He sneezed in the Whispering Meadow. Every flower changed colour at the same moment. The meadow turned entirely blue. It was very quiet.

uses.title: The Sky
uses.pageText:
A bird is up.
It can fly.

uses.title: Animals Can!
uses.pageText:
A bird can fly.
Fly, fly!

uses.pageText:
A bird can fly.
Fly, fly!

uses.title: Animals Can!
uses.pageText:
A bird can fly.
Fly, fly!

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
A bug is little.
It can fly.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: In autumn, animals get ready. A squirrel hides nuts. Birds fly south.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is windy. The wind blows hard. Leaves fly in the air.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are birds — but they cannot fly. Instead, they use their wings as flippers. They are brilliant swimmers.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Seeds travel away from the parent plant. Some fly on the wind. Some stick to animals' fur. Some are eaten by birds and fall far away. Some float on water.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are home to many animals. Bats sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings by day. At dusk, thousands of bats fly out together to feed on insects in the night air.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: "Let us make a rocket!" said James. "We can fly all the way into space!"

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy woke up and tried to fly. Flappy got three wing-flaps up. Then landed in the mud.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: I should be able to fly, said Flappy. I have wings. You are also a dinosaur, said Grumpy. Dinosaurs do not fly.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: I should be able to fly, said Flappy. I have wings. You are also a dinosaur, said Grumpy. Dinosaurs do not fly.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer and Spark made a deal.
Spark would teach Glimmer to breathe fire properly.
Glimmer would teach Spark to fly.
They shook on it.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Reptiles
uses.pageText: Turtles have a hard shell.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is windy. The wind blows hard. Leaves fly in the air.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A crab has a hard shell. A crab walks sideways.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Rocks are hard. Rocks can be big or small.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees work hard every day. They help flowers grow. They make our world sweeter. Bees are amazing.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage three: the caterpillar makes a hard shell around itself. This is called a chrysalis. Inside, an extraordinary change is about to happen.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At home, Mum made lunch. After, they had their cakes. Chips ate the paper bag. "CHIPS!" they said. But they were laughing too hard to be cross.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mrs. Chen stood at the garden gate and laughed so hard that she had to sit down on the grass.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the armoury, there was a full suit of plate armour. It was smaller than Aiden expected. The guide told them that real knights were roughly the same size as Dad, which was very hard to imagine. Aiden tried on a gauntlet under supervision. His hand barely fit inside.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Honky tried very hard to be quiet. Hello, whispered Honky. It still blew Chompy's bib sideways.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: The second runner came over. Good race, they said. You too, said Zippy, breathing hard for the first time ever.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer did not think. Glimmer just ran toward the fox. Glimmer breathed in as hard as possible.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow was digging a new tunnel. He dug down, and he dug sideways, and he dug carefully around the roots. Then his spade hit something hard and wooden.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna woke up knowing she had forgotten something important. She sat on her branch. She thought very hard. She could not remember what it was.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it with water.
She pushed as hard as she could.
The boulder did not move.
"I am not strong enough," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"Spark," said Glimmer.
"You are trying too hard."
"Fire is not thinking."
"It is feeling."
Spark looked at Glimmer for a long time.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it loose.
She sent the water flowing hard against the rocks.
The fish did not move.
"I need help," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Sunny found Zippy. I was looking at a flower, said Zippy. I went past it twelve times first.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Bouncy thought it was a ghost. Zippy ran everywhere looking, very fast. Honky called out asking. Every leaf fell off.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Has anyone seen my pillow? said Dozy. Dozy had been looking for it all morning. This was serious.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: It could be anywhere, said Bossy, looking at the clipboard. Sunny Hollow is very big.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: It was exactly like this, said Dozy, looking at all of them, but cloudier. Dozy's eyes closed again. Wake me for supper.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Whatever you do, said Fern, looking at the Crystal Stream, do NOT sneeze near the water.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop was at the Crystal Stream.
She was looking at something in the water.
It was a large fish.
It was stuck.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"Hello," said Fern.
The tiny creature looked up.
"Have you seen my spectacles?" she said.
"I've been looking for three days."

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The creature ran to its family.
The family gathered around it.
They looked at the Moonwood creatures.
Not afraid.
Just looking.
Then one of them blinked.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: My five senses help me learn!

uses.title: Healthy Habits
uses.pageText: Healthy habits make me strong!

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I have five senses. They help me know the world.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can see. My eyes let me see colours and shapes.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can hear. My ears let me hear sounds.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can smell. My nose lets me smell nice things.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can taste. My mouth lets me taste food.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: "I can help," said Dad, "but you two are in charge. You tell me the plan."

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: I like your tail, said Dozy sleepily. It fans me while I nap. The Dino Pals all agreed.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a pile of extra berries for Chompy. Someone knows me very well, said Chompy, already eating them.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Clumsy looked in from a great height. It looks fine to me, said Clumsy. You cannot even see your own feet, said Fancy.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: It was exactly like this, said Dozy, looking at all of them, but cloudier. Dozy's eyes closed again. Wake me for supper.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: One day, Burrow got stuck on the other side of the stream. "Help!" called Burrow. "I cannot find the tunnel. Everything looks the same to me!"

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow went up to find Luna.
"Come with me," he said.
"Bring a light."
Luna said nothing.
She came.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
It was very late when Burrow noticed.
"Will you tell me the rest?" he asked.
"Yes," said Luna.
"There is quite a lot."
They both settled in.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Chips was coming too. He had his own little blanket and his bell, which jingled every single time he moved.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Honky offered to shout at it until it moved. Everyone agreed this would make things much worse.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Grumpy has a strong tail, said Sunny. Grumpy swung the club tail at the rocks. CLONK. One small rock moved. There were fifty more.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Everyone move back, said Grumpy. They moved back.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose could smell the rain from far away. Twenty minutes, said Sneezy. Maybe fifteen. Everyone moved faster.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He checked his map. According to the map, he was standing in the Whispering Meadow. He was not in the Whispering Meadow. The paths had moved.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip walked toward the Fog Marsh.
He looked back.
Stone had not moved.
Stone had moved one foot.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip walked toward the Fog Marsh.
He looked back.
Stone had not moved.
Stone had moved one foot.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the Hollow Oak, everyone heard it.
"The stream is singing again!" said Pip.
"We just moved a stone," said Fern.
"And asked the water nicely," said Dewdrop.
"It did the rest."

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
One morning, things had moved in the night.
Pip's boots were not where he had left them.
A bench was tipped over.
Someone had been in the clearing.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
The next night, it happened again.
More things had moved.
"Was it you?" asked Stone.
"No," said Pip.
"Was it you?" asked Pip.
"No," said everyone.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Burrow bumped the bench.
It fell over.
Burrow kept walking.
He found Pip's door.
He moved the boots with his paws.
He did not wake up.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Stone pushed.
The rock moved.
The mud let go.
The fish was free.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Now Cheeky was muddy. The Dino Pals looked at Cheeky. Cheeky looked at the Dino Pals.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy is in the mud.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy is very muddy.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy is very muddy.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy got in the bath.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: The bath got very muddy.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy got out.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy ran to the mud.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy is muddy again.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy is muddy again.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy is happy.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: "I am too muddy!" said Muddy.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: "I am too muddy!" said Muddy.

uses.title: Muddy and Splashy Make a Mess
uses.pageText: Muddy has some mud.

uses.title: Muddy and Splashy Make a Mess
uses.pageText: Muddy jumped in. Splashy jumped in.

uses.title: Muddy and Splashy Make a Mess
uses.pageText: Muddy likes mud. Splashy likes mud too.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Muddy made a mud cake.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored. We know more about the surface of the Moon than we do about the deep ocean. There is so much left to discover.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A frog's skin is always damp. Frogs can breathe through their skin as well as through their lungs. They must never dry out.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden added a new page to his field notebook: WHAT MAKES A GOOD EXPERIMENT. He had six points. Socks sat on the desk and watched him write, which Aiden had never seen him do before.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy stopped. Where was Sunny Hollow? Zippy had never stopped before.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Oh, said Zippy. This is... nice. Zippy sat down. Zippy had never sat down before.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Inside the dream, Dozy was wide awake. Dozy had never been so awake. Everything was golden and warm and soft.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer sat down. "I will never breathe fire," said Glimmer. "I have tried every day and it is never fire."

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer sat down. "I will never breathe fire," said Glimmer. "I have tried every day and it is never fire."

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: One morning, a new fish appeared. It was silver with a bright blue stripe. Dewdrop had never seen a fish like it.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
The room had carvings on every wall.
It had small glowing stones in the ceiling.
It smelled of old wood and old magic.
Burrow had never seen it before.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip noticed it on a Tuesday.
The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer did it again.
Longer.
The fire was steady.
It was warm.
Glimmer's scales caught the light.
Glimmer had never looked so much like a dragon.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have one nose.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: I smell with my nose.

uses.title: Our Five Senses
uses.pageText: We use our nose to smell.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText:
I have a nose.
I can smell.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can smell. My nose lets me smell nice things.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have eyes to see. I have ears to hear. I have a nose to smell.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Anna grabbed her pen and drew the plan. "It needs big wings," she said, "and a pointed nose cone at the top."

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "Oh, Chips!" said Anna. But she gave him a big hug. Chips licked her right on the nose.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James pressed his nose flat to the glass. "That one looks just like a tiny striped rocket!" he said.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma had a big brown horse called Bess. She was huge and gentle. Her nose was the softest thing James had ever felt.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the day of try-outs, James roared so loud that Mrs. Green's glasses slid right down her nose. He got the part!

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: At last, both Chips and Bella lay down on the lawn side by side, panting. Chips licked Bella's ear. Bella licked Chips's nose.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose began to twitch. The Dino Pals turned to look. Oh no, said Bossy. Oh yes, said Wiggly.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose could smell the rain from far away. Twenty minutes, said Sneezy. Maybe fifteen. Everyone moved faster.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Don't sneeze again, said Wren. I will try not to, said Spark. His nose twitched.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Spark. The flowers looked at him. He looked at them. His nose twitched again.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Pip, Wren, Burrow, and Fern went inside to search.
They searched every room.
They found nothing.
Then Burrow's nose twitched.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: By lunchtime, they could both ride all the way down the long lane and back without stopping once.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: The next morning, Fancy left a beautifully woven bracelet outside Wiggly's cave. Wiggly's tail knocked it away at once. Sorry! said Wiggly. It is fine, said Fancy. And meant it.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Sneezy, dabbing with the handkerchief. Every leaf had fallen off every tree. Do not apologise, said Grumpy. For once, Grumpy was actually smiling.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: We need to get ready, said Bossy. For once, nobody argued. They needed the plan.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
The mushroom's glow changed.
It pulsed once — pointing.
Another mushroom far away pulsed the same way.
And another.
A trail of glowing mushrooms lit up through the trees.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"Why didn't we try that first?" asked Flint.
"I don't know," said Wren.
She looked back at the mushroom trail.
"They seemed happy about it though."
The last mushroom blinked once and went out.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
They sat by the stream together.
Stone dripped for a long time.
The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.
And meant it.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They tried to sleep. Chips leaned on James. James leaned on Anna. Anna leaned on the tent wall. Nobody was quite comfortable.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden wrote in his notebook: When something is unfair, you have two choices — pretend it isn't happening, or decide what to do. He starred the second option. He didn't quite know yet what doing something looked like.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried stomping. Flappy's feet were quite small. Nobody noticed.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried nesting in a tree. This part actually worked quite well. Flappy was surprised.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy went back to the tree. Got three wing-flaps up. Landed neatly on a branch. Sat very high up and looked at all of Sunny Hollow below. Oh, said Flappy quietly. That is quite good actually.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: Luna smiled. "That is quite nice, actually," said Luna. Fern smiled. She was very tired.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: I have been here longer than the Hollow Oak, said the fish. Dewdrop looked carefully. The fish was, if anything, quite new-looking. I know all the secrets of the Deep Dark, the fish added.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: What is inside? said Pip. Luna was quiet. Good things, I think, she said finally. I cannot quite remember what kind.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it a meeting? asked Fern. I don't think so, said Luna. Was it something to collect? asked Burrow. Possibly, said Luna. I cannot quite say.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Flint opened his satchel.
Seven maps fell out.
One was of the coast.
One was upside down.
None of them were quite right.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
It was very late when Burrow noticed.
"Will you tell me the rest?" he asked.
"Yes," said Luna.
"There is quite a lot."
They both settled in.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
They all sat in the clearing.
Glimmer stood at the front.
It was very quiet.
"Ready," said Glimmer.
It did not quite feel true.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire faded slowly.
Moonwood kept its glow.
Luna looked at Glimmer over her glasses.
"Quite controlled," said Luna.
"Thank you," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: Chompy woke up. I am hungry, said Chompy.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy woke up. Bouncy bounced straight into the cave wall. BONK!

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly woke up carefully. Today, said Wiggly, I will not knock anything over.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Then a thunderstorm came. Dozy woke up frightened. All the Dino Pals hid.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Fancy woke up and found something terrible. Fancy's sail was bent. Not a little bent. Very bent.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy woke up and tried to fly. Flappy got three wing-flaps up. Then landed in the mud.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Dozy slept through most of the events and woke up in time for the picnic. Did I win anything? said Dozy. Most restful competitor, said Bossy. Deserved, said Dozy, and fell asleep again.

uses.title: Noisy Wakes Everyone Up
uses.pageText: Grumpy woke up. Woolly woke up. Clucky woke up.

uses.title: Noisy Wakes Everyone Up
uses.pageText: Grumpy woke up. Woolly woke up. Clucky woke up.

uses.title: Noisy Wakes Everyone Up
uses.pageText: Grumpy woke up. Woolly woke up. Clucky woke up.

uses.title: Noisy Wakes Everyone Up
uses.pageText: Sleepy woke up.

uses.title: Sleepy's Big Dream
uses.pageText: Then Sleepy woke up.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna woke up knowing she had forgotten something important. She sat on her branch. She thought very hard. She could not remember what it was.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
In the morning, Burrow woke up.
He looked around.
Pip and Glimmer were standing in front of him.
"Good morning," said Burrow.
There was a long pause.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Pip woke Wren.
They listened together.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
"...they were right here..."
"Something is in the walls," said Wren.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip brought it inside.
Everyone woke up.
Stone brought a piece of acorn biscuit.
The creature ate it very carefully.
It watched everyone with its large silver eyes.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Three weeks later, the new tooth began to come through. It was enormous relative to the gap — a proper square adult tooth in a mouth that had been full of small rounded baby ones. Aiden looked at himself in the mirror and felt extremely strange.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly dampened the sail gently and pressed it very softly. Slowly, slowly, it began to straighten.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose began to twitch. The Dino Pals turned to look. Oh no, said Bossy. Oh yes, said Wiggly.

uses.title: Giggly Has the Hiccups
uses.pageText:
Giggly began to giggle.
Hic! Hee! Hic! Hee!

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "Try something scary," said Burrow. So Pip walked to the Tumblerock Cliffs. He found the high ledge and began to climb.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: The plant stopped growing. The leaves curled gently inward. Then, slowly, it began to shrink.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren picked up her spell book. She turned to the next spell. "But I am going to find a better one," she said. She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark tried to hold the sneeze in. His eyes went watery. His magic began to build and build. The sparkles around him grew very bright.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
The water rushed over the singing stones.
And the Crystal Stream began to sing.
First very quietly.
Then louder.
Then loud enough to hear all the way to the Hollow Oak.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna settled on a ledge.
She folded her wings.
She looked at the carvings for a moment.
"The first story of Moonwood," she began,
"is this."

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then Burrow sat down.
Against the big mushroom.
Pip and Glimmer were still behind it.
Burrow began to snore.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Then all the plants began to walk.
They were very polite about it.
They walked around Fern.
They walked around Wren.
They went for a stroll.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We'll clear it," said Pip.
"Now," said Fern.
They spent the afternoon clearing the marsh edge.
As they worked, the spirit watched.
Slowly, it began to sit up.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
That evening, the fog stayed at the line.
The mushrooms began to come back on.
One by one.
Pip watched them light up.
The marsh was where it should be.
The forest was where it should be.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Well done, both of you," said Mum. "You were so brave today." They each got a sticker — James got a rocket, Anna got a star.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: "I can get up," said Brave.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: Brave fell off.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: "I can get up," said Brave.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: Brave fell off again.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: "I can get up," said Brave.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: Brave got up!

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: "I am up!" said Brave.

uses.title: Brave Climbs the Hay Bale
uses.pageText: Then Brave fell off.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: "I will help," said Brave.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: "Oh," said Brave.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Burrow appeared from a nearby tunnel. "That is a Bravery Stone," said Burrow. "Whoever holds it will feel brave."

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone. "But I don't feel brave," he said. "I feel the same as always."

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "Did it run out of brave?" asked Pip.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Burrow smiled. "The stone doesn't do anything," he said. "I wanted to see what you would do. And you were brave."

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

uses.title: Animal Homes
uses.pageText: A bear sleeps in a cave.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Over time, tunnels and chambers form underground. Some cave systems stretch for hundreds of kilometres. The Mammoth Cave system in America has more than 650 kilometres of passages.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Over time, tunnels and chambers form underground. Some cave systems stretch for hundreds of kilometres. The Mammoth Cave system in America has more than 650 kilometres of passages.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When a stalactite and a stalagmite meet, they form a column. A cave column can take tens of thousands of years to grow. Each one is unique.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Caves are home to many animals. Bats sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings by day. At dusk, thousands of bats fly out together to feed on insects in the night air.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy woke up. Bouncy bounced straight into the cave wall. BONK!

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: I cannot leave the cave, said Fancy. Not like this. Fancy sat very still and stared at the cave wall.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: I cannot leave the cave, said Fancy. Not like this. Fancy sat very still and stared at the cave wall.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: The next morning, Fancy left a beautifully woven bracelet outside Wiggly's cave. Wiggly's tail knocked it away at once. Sorry! said Wiggly. It is fine, said Fancy. And meant it.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Shy, who knew every hidden corner of the Fernwood, led everyone to the deepest part of Cozy Cave. Shy knew exactly where it was warmest.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They climbed inside. James held up five fingers. "Five... four... three... two... one... BLAST OFF!"

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: James was not so sure. He made his most worried face all the way there. Anna held his hand.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Dad did the tricky high bits — the tall planks and the big nails. James and Anna passed the tools and held the wood still.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Next came the floor — flat planks, all in a row. "Walk on it!" said Dad. They did. It held firm!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He held it up for a long time. It was tiny. It was the smallest thing that had ever felt significant. He put it in the small envelope Mum left for him, and when he placed it under his pillow it felt ceremonial.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
