uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "What is this?" said Pip. He picked it up carefully. The glow made his fingers feel warm.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone reached the other side. Stone reached down and picked up Burrow very carefully. "Oh, thank you," said Burrow. "I was going in circles."

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren picked up her spell book. She turned to the next spell. "But I am going to find a better one," she said. She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow found a blank patch of wall. He picked up a small flat stone. Very carefully, he drew the Hollow Oak. Now we are in it too, he said.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Yes, said Luna. I remember now. She picked it up. I put it there to keep it safe. For today.

uses.title: Magnets
uses.pageText: Same poles push apart!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: A push moves things away. Push!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: A push moves things away. Push!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: You push a door open. You pull a door open too.

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: You push a swing. The swing goes up high!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: Magnets push and pull too! A magnet can pull a pin.

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: Push and pull are forces. Forces make things move.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it with water.
She pushed as hard as she could.
The boulder did not move.
"I am not strong enough," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern tried to push with her hands.
The boulder did not move.
Fern stepped back and thought.
"We need each other," said Fern.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it loose.
She sent the water flowing hard against the rocks.
The fish did not move.
"I need help," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Stone raised their hands high.
Pip and Spark added a little push.
The star spirits lifted.
Up.
And up.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText:
The tree has branches.
They reach up.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Mum sent up a tray of juice and biscuits on a rope. Dad waved from below. Chips jangled at the base of the tree, trying to reach the biscuits.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: The pool was too deep to reach in. I cannot see my feet, said Clumsy. I certainly cannot reach the bottom.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: The pool was too deep to reach in. I cannot see my feet, said Clumsy. I certainly cannot reach the bottom.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: We make a good team, said Clumsy. You see the problem. I reach the problem. Exactly, said Clumsy, and accidentally knocked off Wiggly's hat. Sorry.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Bouncy bounced up to reach the high branches and secure anything at risk. Only bumped into three things. A new record, said Bouncy.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny cannot reach the top.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop found Stone at the Hollow Oak.
"I need your hands," she said.
"Just to reach in and move a rock."
Stone understood immediately.
Then Stone understood all of it.

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText: Shapes are all around!

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText:
I see shapes!
Shapes are all around.

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText:
I see shapes!
Shapes are all around.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: This is a seed. It is tiny. Seeds come in many shapes.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: Shapes are everywhere! Can you find shapes today?

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: Shapes are everywhere! Can you find shapes today?

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can see. My eyes let me see colours and shapes.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks different every night. Sometimes it is a full, bright circle. Sometimes it is a thin crescent. These different shapes are called the phases of the Moon.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Almost every plant starts as a tiny seed. Seeds come in hundreds of different shapes and sizes. Each one holds everything a plant needs to begin life.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Most caves form when rainwater seeps into limestone rock. The water is slightly acidic. It slowly dissolves the rock away. This takes thousands and thousands of years.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: It was quiet. Nobody laughed. Marcus said something low, but nobody around him responded. Aiden walked on. His legs were slightly shaky — but he hadn't shown it, and he was extremely proud of himself.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: In 1969, astronauts travelled to the Moon. Neil Armstrong was the first human to walk on its surface. "That's one small step for man," he said.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They crossed back together. Stone did not look at the water. Stone looked at the far end of the bridge. One step, then another.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark breathed in carefully. I think, he said, I might need to sneeze again. Everyone took a large step back.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren poured the potion on the plants.
The plants stood very straight.
Then they leaned.
Then one of them took a step.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip knelt down.
He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.

uses.title: Healthy Habits
uses.pageText: Healthy habits make me strong!

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText:
Little animals grow big!
Big and strong.

uses.title: Animals on the Farm
uses.pageText: A horse is strong. Horses can pull and carry things.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I eat well to grow. Food helps my body get big and strong.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: My body is mine. I keep it safe and strong.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Most spiders can make silk. The silk comes out of tiny organs called spinnerets. Spider silk is incredibly strong — stronger than steel wire of the same thickness!

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Chompy is strong, said Sunny. Chompy tried. Chompy ate a nearby berry bush instead. Sorry, said Chompy.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Grumpy has a strong tail, said Sunny. Grumpy swung the club tail at the rocks. CLONK. One small rock moved. There were fifty more.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it with water.
She pushed as hard as she could.
The boulder did not move.
"I am not strong enough," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.
"Ready?" said Fern.
"Ready," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.title: Animals on the Farm
uses.pageText: Farms give us food. Thank you, farm animals!

uses.title: Hello, Sun!
uses.pageText: The sun is our nearest star. Thank you, sun!

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Grumpy. Not that I needed it. But Grumpy was smiling. Just a little.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Maybe Honky's voice is very useful after all, said Bossy. THANK YOU! said Honky. Every leaf fell off again.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Fancy looked in the pool. Oh, said Fancy. Oh, that is much better. Fancy looked at Wiggly. Thank you. A real thank you.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Fancy looked in the pool. Oh, said Fancy. Oh, that is much better. Fancy looked at Wiggly. Thank you. A real thank you.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Dozy hugged the pillow. Thank you, said Dozy. Both of you. Then Dozy fell asleep, right there, on the spot.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Chompy. Hmph, said Grumpy. They sat on the rock together. Less peaceful with Chompy. But not actually terrible.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone reached the other side. Stone reached down and picked up Burrow very carefully. "Oh, thank you," said Burrow. "I was going in circles."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
When the edge was clear, the spirit stood.
Its shape was clearer now.
"Thank you," said the spirit.
It was not mist anymore.
It was something more solid.
Something more itself.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire faded slowly.
Moonwood kept its glow.
Luna looked at Glimmer over her glasses.
"Quite controlled," said Luna.
"Thank you," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: In the dream, Sunny Hollow was made of clouds. Dozy was walking on clouds. The clouds were warm and soft, which was very agreeable.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip was walking through Moonwood when his foot kicked something small. It was a tiny stone. It glowed with a soft gold light.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: The fog was thick and grey. Something rustled in the reeds nearby. Pip kept walking. He came out the other side.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Halfway across, Stone looked straight ahead. The bridge swayed a little. The Crystal Stream sang below. Stone kept walking.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it something to do with the Crystal Stream? asked Dewdrop. Luna stopped walking. She looked at the stream for a moment. Wait, said Luna.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
It was Burrow.
His eyes were closed.
He was fast asleep.
He was walking.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Burrow bumped the bench.
It fell over.
Burrow kept walking.
He found Pip's door.
He moved the boots with his paws.
He did not wake up.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Oh," said Wren.
"Oh no," said Fern.
"The plants are walking."
Wren checked her book.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants walked into the Hollow Oak.
Some walked toward the Crystal Stream.
A very small plant walked very slowly toward Burrow's tunnel.
They were not in a hurry.
They were just walking.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Halfway through, everyone was somewhere different.
Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They tried to sleep. Chips leaned on James. James leaned on Anna. Anna leaned on the tent wall. Nobody was quite comfortable.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy woke up. Bouncy bounced straight into the cave wall. BONK!

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: I cannot leave the cave, said Fancy. Not like this. Fancy sat very still and stared at the cave wall.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: The memory room, said Luna. That is what it was called. She touched the wall very gently. I remember now.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow found a blank patch of wall. He picked up a small flat stone. Very carefully, he drew the Hollow Oak. Now we are in it too, he said.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
The room had carvings on every wall.
It had small glowing stones in the ceiling.
It smelled of old wood and old magic.
Burrow had never seen it before.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy bounced to the waterfall. Bouncy bumped into Fancy. BOING!

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy ran to the waterfall. Zippy ran back. Zippy ran to the meadow. Zippy ran back.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Zippy ran so fast that Zippy ran right past the picnic. And the waterfall. And Sunny Hollow.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly fetched water from the waterfall very carefully. The tail only knocked over two things. Sorry, said Wiggly.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Clumsy could see over all the ferns, past the waterfall, all the way to the Long Meadow and beyond.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Can you see the pillow? said Dozy. There was a long pause. Oh, said Clumsy. Yes. It is in the waterfall.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: One morning, Rainbow Waterfall was not making rainbows. It was not making anything at all. The waterfall had stopped.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: One morning, Rainbow Waterfall was not making rainbows. It was not making anything at all. The waterfall had stopped.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: AAAAAAACHOOOOOO! The sneeze hit the rocks like a wave. Rocks scattered in every direction. The stream burst free. The waterfall roared back. A rainbow appeared.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy floated on a cloud past the Rainbow Waterfall. But in the dream, the waterfall was made of warm golden light. Oh, said Dozy. This is very nice.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy floated on a cloud past the Rainbow Waterfall. But in the dream, the waterfall was made of warm golden light. Oh, said Dozy. This is very nice.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A butterfly has four wings. Its wings have bright patterns.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A butterfly has four wings. Its wings have bright patterns.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are birds — but they cannot fly. Instead, they use their wings as flippers. They are brilliant swimmers.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies are insects. Like all insects, they have six legs, four wings, and a body in three parts. They also have two long antennae.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage four: the butterfly pushes out of the chrysalis. Its wings are wet and crumpled. The butterfly hangs still and waits. Slowly, its wings unfurl and dry.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage four: the butterfly pushes out of the chrysalis. Its wings are wet and crumpled. The butterfly hangs still and waits. Slowly, its wings unfurl and dry.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Anna grabbed her pen and drew the plan. "It needs big wings," she said, "and a pointed nose cone at the top."

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: I should be able to fly, said Flappy. I have wings. You are also a dinosaur, said Grumpy. Dinosaurs do not fly.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
That afternoon, it was Glimmer's turn to teach.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer hovered for a moment.
Then landed.
"Like that," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer ran.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer jumped.
Glimmer glided five whole steps.
"That's more," said Spark.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna settled on a ledge.
She folded her wings.
She looked at the carvings for a moment.
"The first story of Moonwood," she began,
"is this."

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They cut and snipped and stuck and taped. They worked all morning long.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Bossy, said Sunny, can we try YOUR way AND our way? They worked together. It worked!

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Bossy, said Sunny, can we try YOUR way AND our way? They worked together. It worked!

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried nesting in a tree. This part actually worked quite well. Flappy was surprised.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: She looked at herself carefully. She was exactly the same height as before. The growing spell had not worked at all.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: The remedy worked. Spark's cold was gone. The flowers slowly turned back to their usual colours. The fish returned to normal.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We'll clear it," said Pip.
"Now," said Fern.
They spent the afternoon clearing the marsh edge.
As they worked, the spirit watched.
Slowly, it began to sit up.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Through the binoculars, Betty saw a kingfisher — a bright impossible dart of blue-orange above the water, there and then gone. She had to put the binoculars down and close her eyes for a moment. She had seen it. She wrote it in the log book.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: The Dino Pals went to look. A huge pile of rocks had fallen in the night and blocked the stream above.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dream Bouncy bounced so high that Bouncy went above the clouds and kept going. Everyone watched. Nobody was surprised.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They set off down the lane. Chips trotted along and stopped to munch the long grass at the sides.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: She said a growing spell. Just a small one. Just to help it along.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer stared at their own mouth. "Oh," said Glimmer. The fire had been inside all along. "I just needed to really mean it."

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They walked along the walls slowly. There were drawings of things no one had seen in hundreds of years. What is this place? asked Fern.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The small things landed and bounced.
They bounced along the ground.
They made a sound like giggling.
They left gold trails where they bounced.
"What ARE they?" said Pip.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern looked around the room.
Then she looked at Twig.
The spectacles were on top of Twig's head.
They had been there all along.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText: The apple is red.

uses.title: Fruits
uses.pageText: An apple is a fruit.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
An apple is red.
It is sweet.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Red. A red apple. A red robin.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They got home just in time for lunch. James filled Chips's bowl with fresh grass and sliced apple.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna got to brush Bess's mane. James gave her a big red apple. Bess sniffed it — then snaffled the whole thing in one go!

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mum brought out two bowls — water for Bella, chopped apple for Chips. Bella drank hers. Chips ate his. Then Chips ate Bella's water too.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
A blue cup.
A blue bag.

uses.title: Bob and Nan's First Day at School
uses.pageText: Bob has his bag.

uses.title: Bob and Nan's First Day at School
uses.pageText: Nan has her bag.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At home, Mum made lunch. After, they had their cakes. Chips ate the paper bag. "CHIPS!" they said. But they were laughing too hard to be cross.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: The summer holidays were over at last. Aiden sat on his bed and stared at his new school bag. Grade 1. The words sounded bigger than they looked.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny can fit in the bag.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Most penguins live in cold places. Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, the coldest and windiest place on Earth. Temperatures can drop below minus 60 degrees!

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean has different layers. Near the surface, there is plenty of sunlight and warmth. Further down, it grows colder and darker. Below 200 metres, no sunlight reaches at all.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Mum sent up a tray of juice and biscuits on a rope. Dad waved from below. Chips jangled at the base of the tree, trying to reach the biscuits.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The view from the top was unlike anything Aiden had seen. The whole coastline curved away in both directions — bays and headlands, a small fishing village far below, and the sea stretching to the horizon, catching the light like crinkled silver foil.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy went back to the tree. Got three wing-flaps up. Landed neatly on a branch. Sat very high up and looked at all of Sunny Hollow below. Oh, said Flappy quietly. That is quite good actually.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: His legs felt wobbly. The ground was a long way below. But he did not stop. He reached the top.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Halfway across, Stone looked straight ahead. The bridge swayed a little. The Crystal Stream sang below. Stone kept walking.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I grew bigger. I could sit up and crawl.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: Now I am bigger. I can do so many things!

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's surface is covered in craters. Craters are bowl-shaped holes made by space rocks crashing into the Moon long ago. Some craters are bigger than cities.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage one: the butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf. The eggs are very small — some are no bigger than a pinhead. The leaf is food for the caterpillar inside.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: The summer holidays were over at last. Aiden sat on his bed and stared at his new school bag. Grade 1. The words sounded bigger than they looked.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They followed the stream upstream.
The forest grew older.
The roots grew bigger.
The stream grew quieter.

uses.title: Pets
uses.pageText: A bird is a pet.

uses.title: Animal Homes
uses.pageText: A bird lives in a nest.

uses.title: The Sky
uses.pageText:
A bird is up.
It can fly.

uses.title: Animals Can!
uses.pageText:
A bird can fly.
Fly, fly!

uses.title: My Pet
uses.pageText:
My bird has a cage.
It can sing.

uses.title: Nan and Bob go to the Zoo
uses.pageText: Nan sees a red bird.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Grumpy, said Flappy. Am I a dinosaur or a bird? Grumpy thought for a very long time. You are Flappy, said Grumpy. That is enough.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: He sneezed at breakfast. The porridge turned into a bird. The bird flew out of the window. Spark stared at his empty bowl.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: He sneezed at breakfast. The porridge turned into a bird. The bird flew out of the window. Spark stared at his empty bowl.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said Dad. Chips blinked. He chewed. He looked the other way.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: That night, they brushed their teeth for a very long time. Chips sat at the bathroom door and watched. "Good night, Chips," said Anna. Chips blinked.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
"Why were you shouting?" asked Pip.
The toadling blinked.
"I am lost," it said.
"I was calling for my family."
Its voice was very small now.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"Why didn't we try that first?" asked Flint.
"I don't know," said Wren.
She looked back at the mushroom trail.
"They seemed happy about it though."
The last mushroom blinked once and went out.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"What are you?" asked Pip.
The star spirit blinked its large gold eyes.
"Star," it said.
Its voice was very small.
"Fell," it added.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The creature ran to its family.
The family gathered around it.
They looked at the Moonwood creatures.
Not afraid.
Just looking.
Then one of them blinked.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the fifth day, Glimmer breathed in as deeply as possible. A warm puff came out. It smelled of cinnamon. "That's something," said Pip.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer did not think. Glimmer just ran toward the fox. Glimmer breathed in as hard as possible.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark breathed in carefully. I think, he said, I might need to sneeze again. Everyone took a large step back.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer breathed in.
Deeply.
Glimmer breathed out.
A jet of orange fire came out.
Small.
Perfect.
Real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer breathed in.
Deeply.
Glimmer breathed out.
A jet of orange fire came out.
Small.
Perfect.
Real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips had a blue bell on his collar. JINGLE! JINGLE! JINGLE! You could hear him coming from far away!

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Chips was coming too. He had his own little blanket and his bell, which jingled every single time he moved.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Storm coming, said Grumpy. Big one. Grumpy was almost always right about weather. Everyone believed Grumpy.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Clumsy stood tall and looked out over the whole Hollow. The storm is coming from the east, said Clumsy. The tall ferns are already bending. That gives us time.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: The next morning, the plant had grown so much it filled the Hollow Oak doorway. Leaves were coming out of every window. "Oh," said Fern.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: On the way home, James and Anna raced. They crossed the gate post at exactly the same time. A perfect tie.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy crossed the line first. Just. The second runner arrived a heartbeat later.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: There was a rope bridge over the Crystal Stream. Everyone crossed it without thinking. Everyone except Stone.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They crossed back together. Stone did not look at the water. Stone looked at the far end of the bridge. One step, then another.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: "You crossed the bridge," said Pip. "Yes," said Stone. "But there might still be a troll under it." Stone looked at the bridge. "I should probably check."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop crossed the finish line.
She had glided the whole way.
She was not wet.
She was not ruffled.
"Finished," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: Shapes are everywhere! Can you find shapes today?

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Rocks are everywhere! They are part of our Earth.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: Water is everywhere! Our Earth is a water planet.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Female spiders lay eggs in a silk sac. The sac protects the eggs. When they hatch, tiny spiderlings emerge. Some mothers carry the sac everywhere.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Bouncy thought it was a ghost. Zippy ran everywhere looking, very fast. Honky called out asking. Every leaf fell off.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Everyone searched. Bouncy bounced into every corner. Zippy ran everywhere twice. Cheeky looked in all the hiding spots. Nothing.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Inside the marsh, the noise was everywhere.
The reeds shook.
The water rippled.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark tried.
Sparkles shot everywhere.
His hat fell off.
His feet stayed on the ground.
"I think I need more practice," said Spark.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Glimmer could not stop.
Glimmer hit Spark.
Sparkles went everywhere.
They both kept moving.
Very fast.
In new directions.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: My five senses help me learn!

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A star has five points. We see stars in the night sky.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I have five senses. They help me know the world.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: Five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. I use them every day!

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They climbed inside. James held up five fingers. "Five... four... three... two... one... BLAST OFF!"

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They climbed inside. James held up five fingers. "Five... four... three... two... one... BLAST OFF!"

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James ran to see the hens. "They have laid five eggs!" he said. He put them one by one — very, very carefully — into a basket.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy ran three circuits of Sunny Hollow. Then four. Then five. Then kept going.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer ran.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer jumped.
Glimmer glided five whole steps.
"That's more," said Spark.

uses.title: Fruits
uses.pageText: An apple is a fruit.

uses.title: Fruits
uses.pageText: A banana is a fruit.

uses.title: Fruits
uses.pageText: A grape is a fruit.

uses.title: Fruits
uses.pageText: An orange is a fruit.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
Fruit is good to eat!
Yum, yum!

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
It is red! It is yellow!
I love fruit!

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: In summer, plants grow tall. Bees buzz. Fruit grows.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: After pollination, the flower makes seeds. The seeds grow inside the plant protected by a pod, a fruit, or a shell.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: The shop was big and bright. It smelled of fresh bread and ripe fruit.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Put the seed in soil. Pat it down gently.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Bouncy offered to bounce on it gently. That is not what gently means, said Fancy.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Bouncy offered to bounce on it gently. That is not what gently means, said Fancy.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly dampened the sail gently and pressed it very softly. Slowly, slowly, it began to straighten.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: The plant stopped growing. The leaves curled gently inward. Then, slowly, it began to shrink.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: The memory room, said Luna. That is what it was called. She touched the wall very gently. I remember now.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna gave one to each creature. One for each of them. The seeds glowed gently in their hands. Plant them this afternoon, said Luna.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
"It was you," said Pip gently. "You sleep-dig."
"I am very sorry," said Burrow.
He put his boot by the door.
"Will that stop you?" asked Glimmer.
"I don't know," said Burrow.
"I am asleep."

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Wren and Spark tried search spells.
The spells pointed at each other.
Stone looked under every log.
Gently.
There were no seeds under the logs.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
"Where is your home?" asked Burrow, gently.
The creature looked at its paws.
Then at the window.
"Deep," it said.
"Deep dark."

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I grew bigger. I could sit up and crawl.

uses.title: How I Grow
uses.pageText: I learned to run and jump. I grew more every day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He walked for three days. He did not stop. His map grew longer and longer. It was full of detail.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark tried to hold the sneeze in. His eyes went watery. His magic began to build and build. The sparkles around him grew very bright.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They followed the stream upstream.
The forest grew older.
The roots grew bigger.
The stream grew quieter.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They followed the stream upstream.
The forest grew older.
The roots grew bigger.
The stream grew quieter.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They followed the stream upstream.
The forest grew older.
The roots grew bigger.
The stream grew quieter.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.
"Ready?" said Fern.
"Ready," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow sat very still and listened.
The room grew warmer.
The carvings lit up one by one.
Luna's voice was quiet and certain.
She had always known these stories.

uses.title: Pets We Love
uses.pageText: A cat is a pet. Cats purr when they are happy.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath
uses.pageText: Muddy is happy.

uses.title: Splashy Finds a Puddle
uses.pageText: Splashy is very happy.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Both of them are happy.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Everyone is happy.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly. They always did.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"Why didn't we try that first?" asked Flint.
"I don't know," said Wren.
She looked back at the mushroom trail.
"They seemed happy about it though."
The last mushroom blinked once and went out.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
They sat by the stream together.
Stone dripped for a long time.
The fish surfaced once.
It seemed happy.
"Good," said Stone.
And meant it.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"I am Twig," said the tiny creature.
"I live here."
"I have always lived here."
She seemed perfectly happy about this.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Wiggly's tail knocked everything over. Wiggly! said Bossy.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy bumped into Wiggly. CRASH! Wiggly knocked over everything. Again.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked over Chompy's breakfast. Sorry, Chompy!

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked very carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked Grumpy's favourite rock. Hmph! said Grumpy.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked SO carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked Fancy into the mud puddle. Oh no.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly sat very, very still. The tail still knocked over three berries and a leaf.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly fetched water from the waterfall very carefully. The tail only knocked over two things. Sorry, said Wiggly.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: The next morning, Fancy left a beautifully woven bracelet outside Wiggly's cave. Wiggly's tail knocked it away at once. Sorry! said Wiggly. It is fine, said Fancy. And meant it.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: We make a good team, said Clumsy. You see the problem. I reach the problem. Exactly, said Clumsy, and accidentally knocked off Wiggly's hat. Sorry.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Wiggly tried to win the tidiest corner. The tail knocked everything over while tidying. I am giving myself zero points, said Wiggly.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mrs. Green told the class: "We are putting on a school play! It is called 'The Lost Dragon'."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Mum said it was completely normal and that they had both lost teeth before when they were smaller — Aiden had even eaten one inside a peanut butter sandwich and not noticed for an hour. Aiden was not certain this was reassuring.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy held the small winner's pebble and looked at it. Zippy, said Sunny, are you all right? I nearly lost, said Zippy.

uses.title: Speedy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Speedy is lost.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: Tiny has lost a hat.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
"Why were you shouting?" asked Pip.
The toadling blinked.
"I am lost," it said.
"I was calling for my family."
Its voice was very small now.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They sat down under a large mushroom.
They were tired.
They were lost.
The mushroom glowed cheerfully.
Wren looked at it.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Halfway through, everyone was somewhere different.
Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They got home just in time for lunch. James filled Chips's bowl with fresh grass and sliced apple.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At home, Mum made lunch. After, they had their cakes. Chips ate the paper bag. "CHIPS!" they said. But they were laughing too hard to be cross.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: Sunny shared her lunch. Here you go, Chompy! said Sunny.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Chompy had an idea. Chompy found the biggest, yummiest lunch in Sunny Hollow.

uses.title: Dozy Won't Wake Up
uses.pageText: Dozy sniffed. Dozy opened one eye. Is that... lunch? said Dozy.

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: You push a door open. You pull a door open too.

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: You push a door open. You pull a door open too.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor announced the Science Fair on a grey Wednesday in February. Every pair in Grade 1 would present a project. Aiden had his notebook open before she had finished the sentence.

uses.title: Tiny is Very Small
uses.pageText: Tiny cannot open the big door.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Then his tunnel fell open.
He tumbled into a room.
It was large.
It was old.
It was not a tunnel.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
The magic seeds were gone.
The box that held them was open and empty.
Luna looked at the box for a long time.
"This is not good," she said.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Go outside and find a rock! Look at it carefully.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They put on their helmets and walked the bikes outside. James could not wait. Anna checked the brakes first.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: At midnight, a fox barked in the lane. Chips went very still. James shone the torch outside. Nothing was there.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: The next morning, Fancy left a beautifully woven bracelet outside Wiggly's cave. Wiggly's tail knocked it away at once. Sorry! said Wiggly. It is fine, said Fancy. And meant it.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly. They always did.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What do you remember about it? asked Pip. I remember it was today, said Luna. And it was important. And... she paused. I think it was outside.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip and Stone were sitting outside the Hollow Oak.
Then a noise came from the Fog Marsh.
It was very, very loud.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

uses.pageText: We wear boots in the rain.

uses.pageText:
Rain falls.
Water soaks in.

uses.pageText: Rumble! Flash! A storm is here. Then the rain falls.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: After rain, look up! A rainbow! Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: Sun, rain, wind, snow. Weather changes every day. What is the weather today?

uses.pageText: Water is all around us. Oceans, rivers, and rain.

uses.pageText: Rain falls from the clouds. Drip, drip, drip.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: Rain fills rivers and lakes. Animals drink the water.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose could smell the rain from far away. Twenty minutes, said Sneezy. Maybe fifteen. Everyone moved faster.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: They reached the meadow. Grumpy found the flat rock and sat on it. Chompy found a berry patch immediately.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: His legs felt wobbly. The ground was a long way below. But he did not stop. He reached the top.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone reached the other side. Stone reached down and picked up Burrow very carefully. "Oh, thank you," said Burrow. "I was going in circles."

uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Pip reached the Crystal Stream.
He leaped from stone to stone.
One stone was slippery.
Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone for a long time. "I'll keep it," he said. "To remember."

uses.pageText: What is inside? said Pip. Luna was quiet. Good things, I think, she said finally. I cannot quite remember what kind.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: The memory room, said Luna. That is what it was called. She touched the wall very gently. I remember now.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna woke up knowing she had forgotten something important. She sat on her branch. She thought very hard. She could not remember what it was.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: This was the problem with forgetting things. You couldn't always remember what you had forgotten. Luna knew it was important. She knew it was today.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What do you remember about it? asked Pip. I remember it was today, said Luna. And it was important. And... she paused. I think it was outside.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Yes, said Luna. I remember now. She picked it up. I put it there to keep it safe. For today.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: The Tree
uses.pageText:
The tree has roots.
They go down.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A flower has petals. A flower has a stem. A flower has roots.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Trees have roots under the soil. Roots hold the tree up.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Trees have roots under the soil. Roots hold the tree up.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow was digging a new tunnel. He dug down, and he dug sideways, and he dug carefully around the roots. Then his spade hit something hard and wooden.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: He polished his glasses and looked more closely. On the door was a small carving. A tree with roots going in every direction. It was very old.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They followed the stream upstream.
The forest grew older.
The roots grew bigger.
The stream grew quieter.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Beyond the roots, a small clearing.
Silver moss lit the ground.
It was warm.
Other creatures were there.
They looked up.
They had the same enormous silver eyes.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: A small green alien ran to say hello. "My name is Zim!" it said. "Do you want to play?"

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden didn't say anything. He went home and sat on his bed and stared at the ceiling. He wasn't crying, but he wasn't fine either. He didn't really want to talk about it — which Betty noticed immediately.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop went back to the Crystal Stream. Why do you say things that are not true? she asked. She said it kindly. She just wanted to know.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it a meeting? asked Fern. I don't think so, said Luna. Was it something to collect? asked Burrow. Possibly, said Luna. I cannot quite say.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna was very large for a tunnel.
She came anyway.
She did not say anything about this.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: At last, both Chips and Bella lay down on the lawn side by side, panting. Chips licked Bella's ear. Bella licked Chips's nose.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: The fog was thick and grey. Something rustled in the reeds nearby. Pip kept walking. He came out the other side.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: One day, Burrow got stuck on the other side of the stream. "Help!" called Burrow. "I cannot find the tunnel. Everything looks the same to me!"

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone looked at the bridge. Stone looked at the water. Stone looked at Burrow on the other side.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone reached the other side. Stone reached down and picked up Burrow very carefully. "Oh, thank you," said Burrow. "I was going in circles."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They reached the other side. Burrow found his glasses. Stone stood up straight.

uses.pageText:
Stone stood up and called out across the marsh.
It was the loudest sound Pip had ever heard.
Louder than the toadling.
Much louder.
Something answered from the far side of the marsh.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Pip reached the Crystal Stream.
He leaped from stone to stone.
One stone was slippery.
Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.

uses.pageText: Five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. I use them every day!

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have eyes to see. I have ears to hear. I have a nose to smell.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose could smell the rain from far away. Twenty minutes, said Sneezy. Maybe fifteen. Everyone moved faster.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Burrow found the underground path.
He could smell the way.
The creature stepped forward.
It knew this place.
"Here," it said.

uses.pageText: Stars twinkle in the sky.

uses.title: The Sky
uses.pageText:
The stars are up.
They shine.

uses.pageText:
Stars come out.
They are bright.

Stars are far away.
There are so many.

uses.pageText: A star has five points. We see stars in the night sky.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: The moon and stars come out. They shine in the dark sky.

uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.pageText: That night, Chompy looked at the stars. I wonder what breakfast will be, said Chompy.

The sky was full of stars above.

The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They cut and snipped and stuck and taped. They worked all morning long.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Grumpy pulled and pulled. Grumpy was still stuck.

uses.pageText: Wiggly walked off. BOING! Wiggly bounced back. My tail is stuck! HEE HEE HEE! said Cheeky.

uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."
