uses.pageText: Zippy ran back and forth collecting everything needed before anyone could finish asking. Twelve trips in four minutes. Done, said Zippy.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: She opened the box. Inside were twelve small seeds. Each one glowed with a soft gold light. Oh, said Fern, very quietly.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: I like your tail, said Dozy sleepily. It fans me while I nap. The Dino Pals all agreed.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Wiggly tried to win the tidiest corner. The tail knocked everything over while tidying. I am giving myself zero points, said Wiggly.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: The fish was quiet for a while. It swam a small, slow circle. Then it came back. Because I am new here, said the fish. And I wanted to sound interesting.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They flew past big round planets. Some had red spots. Some had wide, shining rings!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Inside the dream, Dozy was wide awake. Dozy had never been so awake. Everything was golden and warm and soft.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna stood in the doorway.
She was very still.
Her eyes went wide.
Then soft.
"Oh," said Luna.
Very quietly.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Wiggly's tail knocked everything over. Wiggly! said Bossy.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked over Chompy's breakfast. Sorry, Chompy!

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked very carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked Grumpy's favourite rock. Hmph! said Grumpy.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked SO carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked Fancy into the mud puddle. Oh no.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky hid in the ferns. Cheeky tied Wiggly's tail to a tree. Hee hee, said Cheeky.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: The next morning, Fancy left a beautifully woven bracelet outside Wiggly's cave. Wiggly's tail knocked it away at once. Sorry! said Wiggly. It is fine, said Fancy. And meant it.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: The next morning, Fancy left a beautifully woven bracelet outside Wiggly's cave. Wiggly's tail knocked it away at once. Sorry! said Wiggly. It is fine, said Fancy. And meant it.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: We make a good team, said Clumsy. You see the problem. I reach the problem. Exactly, said Clumsy, and accidentally knocked off Wiggly's hat. Sorry.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Wiggly's long tail swept the Big Flat Rock clear in seconds. Food, supplies, anything that could blow away. Sorry, said Wiggly, sweeping everything. This time everyone was grateful.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: Bugs help our world. They are very important!

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I have five senses. They help me know the world.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: There are thousands of kinds of bees. The honeybee is one of the most helpful bees in the world.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees work hard every day. They help flowers grow. They make our world sweeter. Bees are amazing.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Famous volcanoes can be found all around the world. Iceland, Hawaii and Italy all have active volcanoes. Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: The young frog climbs out of the water. It can now breathe air through its lungs. It can also live on land. The whole world opens up.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs sing to find a mate. Each species has its own call. The ribbit of a tree frog, the deep croak of a bullfrog — their calls fill warm evenings around the world.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Betty had the guide map. She navigated with precise efficiency — Great Hall, Armoury, North Tower, King's Chamber, Dungeon — the best order for minimum backtracking. Aiden followed behind her, reading every information board they passed, completely at home in a world of facts.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: The first lesson was handwriting — joined-up letters, which were completely new and seemed designed to be tricky. Aiden's pen slipped and he made a large blot right across the middle of the page. He went very red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Halfway across, Stone looked straight ahead. The bridge swayed a little. The Crystal Stream sang below. Stone kept walking.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Stone stood up and called out across the marsh.
It was the loudest sound Pip had ever heard.
Louder than the toadling.
Much louder.
Something answered from the far side of the marsh.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the source, they found it.
A great boulder had fallen.
It lay across the singing stones.
The stones could not sing.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The far bank was different — thicker trees, softer ground, a field of tall meadow grass beyond the treeline. Socks bounded ahead, turning back every few steps to make sure they were following.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Halfway across, Stone looked straight ahead. The bridge swayed a little. The Crystal Stream sang below. Stone kept walking.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
"The song comes from the source," said Dewdrop.
"We must follow the stream up."
Fern looked at the deep forest ahead.
"Then we go," said Fern.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Flint's map said go left.
Wren's spell said go right.
"Straight ahead," they agreed.
This turned out to be wrong.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint followed the mushroom trail.
The forest opened up.
The golden light of the Whispering Meadow was ahead.
"Oh," said Flint.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"This way," said Flint.
He was right.
The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.
"I always find things," said Flint.
"Eventually."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The Deep Dark was very dark.
The trees had no glow.
The light went only a little way ahead.
They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: My body is amazing!

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText: Space is big and amazing!

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: So many animals live in the sea! The ocean is amazing.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: My body is amazing! I look after it every day.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees work hard every day. They help flowers grow. They make our world sweeter. Bees are amazing.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Anna ran to find the bread. She picked the big round loaf with seeds on top. It smelled amazing!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: They crossed back together. Stone did not look at the water. Stone looked at the far end of the bridge. One step, then another.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: There was another flash of blue. Wren was back to her normal size. She brushed off her robe. She straightened her hat.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint took out a new piece of parchment. "I'll make another one," he said. He was not upset about this. He had always known the paths would move.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
The mushroom's glow changed.
It pulsed once — pointing.
Another mushroom far away pulsed the same way.
And another.
A trail of glowing mushrooms lit up through the trees.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
The mushroom's glow changed.
It pulsed once — pointing.
Another mushroom far away pulsed the same way.
And another.
A trail of glowing mushrooms lit up through the trees.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
It was the middle of the night.
Everyone was nearly asleep.
Then a light flashed.
Then another.
Then small glowing things began to fall from the sky.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip knelt down.
He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They had set up a lemonade stand beside the sale table — Betty's idea, planned the previous Thursday. Aiden poured from a glass jug. Betty collected the money and kept the queue moving. By one o'clock they had sold every cup and run entirely out of lemons.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By evening, it was a large, beautiful plant beside the Hollow Oak. Not too small. Not too large. Luna came out through the door.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: He wrote in his notebook that evening: Saying a true thing clearly is harder than it looks and better than it sounds. He underlined it twice.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He told Betty. Betty got the torch and studied it with great interest. "It's definitely loose," she said. "It'll fall out and a permanent one will grow. That's much better, actually." Aiden was not entirely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Fancy looked in the pool. Oh, said Fancy. Oh, that is much better. Fancy looked at Wiggly. Thank you. A real thank you.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren picked up her spell book. She turned to the next spell. "But I am going to find a better one," she said. She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
A black cat.
A black bat.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
A black cat.
A black bat.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A ladybird is red with black spots. It eats tiny greenfly.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are black on top and white underneath. This is called countershading. From above, their dark back blends with the deep water. From below, their white front looks like the bright surface.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The ocean makes more than half the oxygen we breathe. Tiny plants called phytoplankton float near the surface. They use sunlight to make oxygen. Every other breath you take came from the ocean.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James took a deep breath. He thought of his best roar. Then he let it out — the biggest, loudest roar he had ever done.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy bumped into Sneezy. Sneezy took a HUGE breath in...

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy took a breath in. The biggest breath anyone in Sunny Hollow had ever taken. The ferns bent backwards.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy took a breath in. The biggest breath anyone in Sunny Hollow had ever taken. The ferns bent backwards.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the tenth day, Glimmer went to the Crystal Stream alone. Again and again. Smoke. Sparks. Warm cinnamon breath. Still no fire.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Then Chips saw a big rose bush. He ran at it. CRUNCH! MUNCH! SNAP! The rose bush was gone.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Then Chips saw a big rose bush. He ran at it. CRUNCH! MUNCH! SNAP! The rose bush was gone.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Then James tried riding with NO hands. He made it exactly three seconds before heading straight into the same bush.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Chompy is strong, said Sunny. Chompy tried. Chompy ate a nearby berry bush instead. Sorry, said Chompy.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: At the Farm
uses.pageText:
I see a little chick.
Peep!

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText:
A little chick.
It is yellow.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: In spring, baby animals are born. A lamb skips. A chick hatches.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText: A baby hen is a chick. A chick is soft and yellow.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText: A baby hen is a chick. A chick is soft and yellow.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: When the egg hatches, a tiny chick comes out. The chick has thick grey fluffy feathers. It cuddles close to its parent to stay warm.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: When the egg hatches, a tiny chick comes out. The chick has thick grey fluffy feathers. It cuddles close to its parent to stay warm.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins live in large groups called colonies. Some colonies have hundreds of thousands of penguins! Each penguin recognises its partner and its chick by their call.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: The moon comes up.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A green shoot comes up! It has two small leaves.

uses.title: Hello, Sun!
uses.pageText: In the morning, the sun comes up. Good morning, sun!

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: When the egg hatches, a tiny chick comes out. The chick has thick grey fluffy feathers. It cuddles close to its parent to stay warm.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans. This causes the tides. When the tide comes in, the sea rises up the beach. When it goes out, it pulls back.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Most spiders can make silk. The silk comes out of tiny organs called spinnerets. Spider silk is incredibly strong — stronger than steel wire of the same thickness!

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "What if it comes back?" said James. "Then we will scare it," said Anna. She picked up the air horn Dad had packed.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
"The song comes from the source," said Dewdrop.
"We must follow the stream up."
Fern looked at the deep forest ahead.
"Then we go," said Fern.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "The dentist is very kind," said Mum. "She just takes a little look inside your mouth. That is all."

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: At the dentist, there was a big fish tank in the waiting room! Bright fish darted in and out of rocks and weeds.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "James!" called the dentist. He stood up. He walked in. The big chair went up and down like a ride!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Well done, both of you," said Mum. "You were so brave today." They each got a sticker — James got a rocket, Anna got a star.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: The tree house was done! Blue walls, a yellow door, a red star flag and a rope ladder all the way to the ground.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James took a deep breath. He thought of his best roar. Then he let it out — the biggest, loudest roar he had ever done.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Zippy ran back and forth collecting everything needed before anyone could finish asking. Twelve trips in four minutes. Done, said Zippy.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mrs. Green told the class: "We are putting on a school play! It is called 'The Lost Dragon'."

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James put his hand straight up. "I want to be the dragon!" Six other children put their hands up too. They would all have to try out.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna did not want to be the dragon. She wanted to paint the big backdrop — the scenery behind the stage.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James practised his dragon roar all week. It shook the windows. Mum wore earmuffs. Chips ran under the sofa.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the night of the play, James wore a green scale costume and a red dragon mask. He looked completely brilliant.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Every morning, Glimmer practised. Fire breathing was the most important thing a dragon could do. And Glimmer could not do it yet.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the third day, the diagrams had multiplied.
There were charts about heat.
Charts about breathing.
Charts about dragon anatomy.
Glimmer stared at them all.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer did it again.
Longer.
The fire was steady.
It was warm.
Glimmer's scales caught the light.
Glimmer had never looked so much like a dragon.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Next came the floor — flat planks, all in a row. "Walk on it!" said Dad. They did. It held firm!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor had noticed, in the way that good teachers always notice. She started a class discussion about what it means to be fair, and what you do when things aren't. Several children looked at the floor. Marcus looked at the window.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Some spiders do not use webs at all. Jumping spiders leap onto their food. They have big eyes that face forward to judge distance. A jumping spider can leap 20 times its own body length!

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James tried again. Eyes forward. Pedal. Wobble. Wobble. Then — he was doing it! He was really, properly doing it!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow opened the door. A warm golden light came from inside. Everyone leaned forward.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Stone rolled up one sleeve.
The arm was very large.
Stone leaned forward.
The hand went toward the water.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Burrow found the underground path.
He could smell the way.
The creature stepped forward.
It knew this place.
"Here," it said.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Orange. An orange fox. An orange pumpkin.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: A fox hunts at night. It has big ears. It moves quietly.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: At midnight, a fox barked in the lane. Chips went very still. James shone the torch outside. Nothing was there.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: That evening, a Fog Marsh fox came creeping into Moonwood. It had found Fern's seed collection. The seeds were small and precious. Glimmer saw the fox.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: That evening, a Fog Marsh fox came creeping into Moonwood. It had found Fern's seed collection. The seeds were small and precious. Glimmer saw the fox.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: Glimmer did not think. Glimmer just ran toward the fox. Glimmer breathed in as hard as possible.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: And a jet of brilliant orange fire came out. The fox ran. The seeds were safe.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: They sat outside as the sun went down. Bess looked over her gate. Percy slept in the mud. Chips ate the fence post. It had been the best farm day ever.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: James brought Chips into the garden. Anna opened the gate. Bella bounded in like a very large, very furry rocket.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Mrs. Chen stood at the garden gate and laughed so hard that she had to sit down on the grass.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: On the way home, James and Anna raced. They crossed the gate post at exactly the same time. A perfect tie.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At home time, Mum was waiting at the gate. She crouched down with an expectant look. "Well?" she said. They both started talking at exactly the same moment and didn't stop for ten minutes.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: There are 18 species of penguin. Not all live in cold places. Little blue penguins live in Australia. African penguins live on warm, sunny beaches. Every kind of penguin is remarkable.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Not all webs look the same. Sheet webs are flat like a hammock. Cobwebs are messy tangles. Every type of spider makes its own kind of web.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "The dentist is very kind," said Mum. "She just takes a little look inside your mouth. That is all."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: What is inside? said Pip. Luna was quiet. Good things, I think, she said finally. I cannot quite remember what kind.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy crossed the line first. Just. The second runner arrived a heartbeat later.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop crossed the finish line.
She had glided the whole way.
She was not wet.
She was not ruffled.
"Finished," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
That evening, the fog stayed at the line.
The mushrooms began to come back on.
One by one.
Pip watched them light up.
The marsh was where it should be.
The forest was where it should be.

uses.title: Nan and Bob: Bob's Birthday Party
uses.pageText: Mum lit the big cake.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
The mushroom's glow changed.
It pulsed once — pointing.
Another mushroom far away pulsed the same way.
And another.
A trail of glowing mushrooms lit up through the trees.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna walked slowly around the room.
She touched the carvings.
They lit up where she touched.
Blue and gold.
She had been here before.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow sat very still and listened.
The room grew warmer.
The carvings lit up one by one.
Luna's voice was quiet and certain.
She had always known these stories.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire was very large.
It was taller than Glimmer.
It caught the torch on the Hollow Oak door.
The torch lit the first lamp.
The lamp lit a mushroom.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire was very large.
It was taller than Glimmer.
It caught the torch on the Hollow Oak door.
The torch lit the first lamp.
The lamp lit a mushroom.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Beyond the roots, a small clearing.
Silver moss lit the ground.
It was warm.
Other creatures were there.
They looked up.
They had the same enormous silver eyes.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Maybe I should bounce in the meadow, said Bouncy. BOING! BOING! BOING!

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Maybe Honky's voice is very useful after all, said Bossy. THANK YOU! said Honky. Every leaf fell off again.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky helped clean Fancy's rock. Will you do any more pranks? asked Fancy. Maybe just one more, said Cheeky. And winked.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Sneezy's nose could smell the rain from far away. Twenty minutes, said Sneezy. Maybe fifteen. Everyone moved faster.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "Maybe you need to try harder," said Spark. Spark's own magic crackled around his ears. Glimmer tried harder. More smoke came out. Still no fire.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They played cards in the tent by torchlight. Chips ate two cards before they noticed. The game got harder after that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden didn't say anything. He went home and sat on his bed and stared at the ceiling. He wasn't crying, but he wasn't fine either. He didn't really want to talk about it — which Betty noticed immediately.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor had noticed, in the way that good teachers always notice. She started a class discussion about what it means to be fair, and what you do when things aren't. Several children looked at the floor. Marcus looked at the window.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Mum said it was completely normal and that they had both lost teeth before when they were smaller — Aiden had even eaten one inside a peanut butter sandwich and not noticed for an hour. Aiden was not certain this was reassuring.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried stomping. Flappy's feet were quite small. Nobody noticed.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
It was very late when Burrow noticed.
"Will you tell me the rest?" he asked.
"Yes," said Luna.
"There is quite a lot."
They both settled in.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip noticed it on a Tuesday.
The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage two: the egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar's only job is to eat. It eats and eats and grows and grows. Some caterpillars eat their own eggshell first!

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly fetched water from the waterfall very carefully. The tail only knocked over two things. Sorry, said Wiggly.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Fancy held a Best Sail competition. Fancy was the only one with a sail. Fancy gave themselves first prize. This seems fair, said Fancy.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Bouncy bounced up to reach the high branches and secure anything at risk. Only bumped into three things. A new record, said Bouncy.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: You are interesting, said Dewdrop. You are the only fish in this stream with a blue stripe. The fish looked at its own stripe. That is true, it said.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Is being the only blue-stripe fish enough? asked the fish. Yes, said Dewdrop. It is very enough.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
The Deep Dark was very dark.
The trees had no glow.
The light went only a little way ahead.
They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Some spiders do not use webs at all. Jumping spiders leap onto their food. They have big eyes that face forward to judge distance. A jumping spider can leap 20 times its own body length!

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs are amphibians. Amphibians can live in water and on land. Frogs begin their life in water and later move onto land.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone stepped onto the bridge. It creaked under Stone's weight. Stone kept going.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren found her spell book. It was enormous now. She climbed up onto it and looked at the spell. She had read it backwards.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He checked his map. According to the map, he was standing in the Whispering Meadow. He was not in the Whispering Meadow. The paths had moved.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint took out a new piece of parchment. "I'll make another one," he said. He was not upset about this. He had always known the paths would move.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly. They always did.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Inside was a small round room. The walls were covered in tiny glowing drawings. Trees and streams. Creatures and old paths. Every living thing that had ever been in Moonwood.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Everyone helped. They checked the Hollow Oak from top to bottom. They walked the paths. They looked in the Whispering Meadow. Nothing triggered the memory.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
An hour later, nothing looked right.
The trees were wrong.
The paths had gone.
"Where are we?" asked Wren.
Flint checked his map.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
A pink pig.
A pink flower.

uses.title: Colors
uses.pageText:
A pink pig.
A pink flower.

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
A worm is pink.
It can dig.

uses.title: Animals on the Farm
uses.pageText: A pig is pink. A pig rolls in mud. Oink!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James chose a big slice of lemon cake with thick white icing. Anna chose a pink strawberry jam tart.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Sunny saw two small eyes behind a rock. And two small pink paws placing a tiny woven grass bracelet on the rock.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Shy! said Sunny, softly. The gifts are from you, aren't they? Shy nodded, going very pink.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: Anna grabbed her pen and drew the plan. "It needs big wings," she said, "and a pointed nose cone at the top."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: This is a good rock, said Chompy. Yes, said Grumpy. Is there anything to eat near it? said Chompy. Grumpy pointed at the berry patch. Chompy went happily.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"We are here," said Flint.
He pointed at the map.
Wren looked around.
Grey fog was appearing between the trees.
"That is the Fog Marsh," said Wren.
"We are not near the meadow."

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Wren and Spark tried search spells.
The spells pointed at each other.
Stone looked under every log.
Gently.
There were no seeds under the logs.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

uses.title: Fruit
uses.pageText:
A plum is purple.
It is little.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Purple. Purple grapes. Purple lavender.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Purple. Purple grapes. Purple lavender.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Purple. Purple grapes. Purple lavender.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: After rain, look up! A rainbow! Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: For their birthdays, James and Anna each got a new bike. James's was red. Anna's was purple.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Every fish in the stream turned purple. The water sang in a different key. One fish turned into a frog for a moment, and then turned back.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren stirred the potion.
It was meant to be green.
It was more purple.
Wren did not notice this.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Everyone searched. Bouncy bounced into every corner. Zippy ran everywhere twice. Cheeky looked in all the hiding spots. Nothing.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Pip searched the Fog Marsh.
He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Pip searched the Fog Marsh.
He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Burrow went underground.
He searched every tunnel.
He found three interesting things.
He did not find any seeds.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop searched the stream.
Fern walked slowly around the clearing.
She was not searching.
She was listening.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Pip, Wren, Burrow, and Fern went inside to search.
They searched every room.
They found nothing.
Then Burrow's nose twitched.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: James and Anna helped bang in the tent pegs and thread the poles through. Chips ate one peg. Then he tried to eat a second.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They decided to grow crystals. It was Betty's original idea and Aiden's second choice, which Betty said made it the obvious answer. They ordered the kit and spent four days watching for the post.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden wrote in his notebook: When something is unfair, you have two choices — pretend it isn't happening, or decide what to do. He starred the second option. He didn't quite know yet what doing something looked like.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy crossed the line first. Just. The second runner arrived a heartbeat later.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: The second runner came over. Good race, they said. You too, said Zippy, breathing hard for the first time ever.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Day and Night
uses.pageText: Day, then night, then day again. Every single day!

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Chips was coming too. He had his own little blanket and his bell, which jingled every single time he moved.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Their first customer was Mr Perkins from next door, who was very old and took a very long time about everything. He picked up every single item on the table, turned it over carefully, and put it back. After twenty minutes, he held up one small rubber duck. It cost twenty cents.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The North Tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They counted every one, out loud, all together. The staircase was so narrow they had to go single file. At the top: the whole landscape, the river, the town, a motorway miles away. The same view and entirely different.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint had decided to map every single path in Moonwood. He had a new roll of parchment and a good quill. He started at the Hollow Oak and walked north.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Back in the meadow, Dozy's eyes opened. All the Dino Pals were sitting in a circle, waiting. What was it like? said Sunny.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip and Stone were sitting outside the Hollow Oak.
Then a noise came from the Fog Marsh.
It was very, very loud.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Everyone came back with nothing.
Then they saw Fern.
She was sitting in the middle of the clearing.
Small glowing seedlings were growing all around her.
"Oh," said everyone.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: The shop was big and bright. It smelled of fresh bread and ripe fruit.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Anna ran to find the bread. She picked the big round loaf with seeds on top. It smelled amazing!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The dungeon was underground and smelled of cold stone and old air. Betty read every board by torchlight. Aiden stood still in the near-dark for a moment and thought about how this exact place had been here through everything — and felt briefly, appropriately small.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the fifth day, Glimmer breathed in as deeply as possible. A warm puff came out. It smelled of cinnamon. "That's something," said Pip.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
The room had carvings on every wall.
It had small glowing stones in the ceiling.
It smelled of old wood and old magic.
Burrow had never seen it before.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy bumped into Sneezy. Sneezy took a HUGE breath in...

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Most spiders can make silk. The silk comes out of tiny organs called spinnerets. Spider silk is incredibly strong — stronger than steel wire of the same thickness!

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Not all webs look the same. Sheet webs are flat like a hammock. Cobwebs are messy tangles. Every type of spider makes its own kind of web.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Some spiders do not use webs at all. Jumping spiders leap onto their food. They have big eyes that face forward to judge distance. A jumping spider can leap 20 times its own body length!

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Spiders have eight eyes, but many cannot see well. Instead, they feel vibrations through their legs. When something touches the web, the spider feels it instantly.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: When an insect is caught, the spider wraps it in silk. This keeps it still. Then the spider injects venom to begin digesting its meal.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: A butterfly's life has four stages. This is called a lifecycle. Each stage looks completely different from the one before.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage one: the butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf. The eggs are very small — some are no bigger than a pinhead. The leaf is food for the caterpillar inside.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage two: the egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar's only job is to eat. It eats and eats and grows and grows. Some caterpillars eat their own eggshell first!

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage three: the caterpillar makes a hard shell around itself. This is called a chrysalis. Inside, an extraordinary change is about to happen.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage four: the butterfly pushes out of the chrysalis. Its wings are wet and crumpled. The butterfly hangs still and waits. Slowly, its wings unfurl and dry.
