uses.title: Speedy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Speedy runs to the barn.

uses.title: Bouncy and Speedy Have a Race
uses.pageText: They ran past the barn.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: They went to the barn. No hat.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Shy hid behind the barn.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles: SELL, KEEP and MAYBE. The MAYBE pile kept losing things to SELL, because, as Betty pointed out, they hadn't touched any of them in over a year. By nine o'clock, the MAYBE pile had completely disappeared.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: The fish was quiet for a while. It swam a small, slow circle. Then it came back. Because I am new here, said the fish. And I wanted to sound interesting.

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
A bee is yellow.
It can sting.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A bee collects pollen. Bees make honey. Bees are important.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees live together in a hive. One hive can hold up to 60,000 bees. The queen bee lays all the eggs.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: Chompy ate some berries. More, please! said Chompy.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Chompy: get berries. Sunny: get leaves. Wiggly: carry things. Dozy: try to stay awake.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Everyone got to work. Chompy ate the berries. Chompy! said Bossy.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: AAAACHOOOO! Leaves, berries, and Bossy's clipboard all blew away.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly sat very, very still. The tail still knocked over three berries and a leaf.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a pile of extra berries for Chompy. Someone knows me very well, said Chompy, already eating them.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "What shall we spend it on?" Betty asked. They sat on the front step with the money tin between them and talked it through the way they talked through important things — slowly and carefully, considering every option.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Are you practising? said Wiggly. I am thinking, said Zippy. You run to think? I always run. The thinking happens in between.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"We are here," said Flint.
He pointed at the map.
Wren looked around.
Grey fog was appearing between the trees.
"That is the Fog Marsh," said Wren.
"We are not near the meadow."

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
The fish was wedged between two rocks.
It had been there since morning.
Its tail kept flicking.
It could not get free.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: BANG! BANG! BANG! went the hammer. WHIRR! went the drill. The frame went up bit by bit.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: BANG! BANG! BANG! went the hammer. WHIRR! went the drill. The frame went up bit by bit.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Now for the best bit — the paint! James chose blue for the walls. Anna chose yellow for the door. Chips chewed the lid off the paint tin.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Hungry Eats Everything
uses.pageText: Hungry ate one more bit of grass.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Clucky had a bit. Then Clucky giggled too.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They made their display board on a rainy Saturday — a bright blue background, a photograph of each day's crystal growth, Betty's data chart, and a title in Aiden's best six-colour lettering: HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW?

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Betty had the guide map. She navigated with precise efficiency — Great Hall, Armoury, North Tower, King's Chamber, Dungeon — the best order for minimum backtracking. Aiden followed behind her, reading every information board they passed, completely at home in a world of facts.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The dungeon was underground and smelled of cold stone and old air. Betty read every board by torchlight. Aiden stood still in the near-dark for a moment and thought about how this exact place had been here through everything — and felt briefly, appropriately small.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They packed their sleeping bags, a torch, a pack of cards, two books and lots of snacks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Everything was back.
"I'm sorry," said Wren.
"Did you learn something?" asked Fern.
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Everything was back.
"I'm sorry," said Wren.
"Did you learn something?" asked Fern.
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Penguins are birds — but they cannot fly. Instead, they use their wings as flippers. They are brilliant swimmers.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the night of the play, James wore a green scale costume and a red dragon mask. He looked completely brilliant.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: And a jet of brilliant orange fire came out. The fox ran. The seeds were safe.

uses.title: Tools
uses.pageText: Tools help us build!

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: We use rocks to build things. Walls and roads are made of rock.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: "We should build a tree house!" said James. He got his notebook and drew the plan right away. It had a door, a window, a flag and a rope ladder.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark tried to hold the sneeze in. His eyes went watery. His magic began to build and build. The sparkles around him grew very bright.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark tried to hold the sneeze in. His eyes went watery. His magic began to build and build. The sparkles around him grew very bright.

uses.title: How Things Grow
uses.pageText: A caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A butterfly has four wings. Its wings have bright patterns.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage one: the butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf. The eggs are very small — some are no bigger than a pinhead. The leaf is food for the caterpillar inside.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage four: the butterfly pushes out of the chrysalis. Its wings are wet and crumpled. The butterfly hangs still and waits. Slowly, its wings unfurl and dry.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Stage four: the butterfly pushes out of the chrysalis. Its wings are wet and crumpled. The butterfly hangs still and waits. Slowly, its wings unfurl and dry.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Some butterflies migrate thousands of kilometres. The monarch butterfly flies from Canada to Mexico every year — a journey of 4,000 kilometres. They always find the same trees.

uses.title: Big and Little
uses.pageText:
A big bus.
A little car.

uses.title: Fast and Slow
uses.pageText:
A car can go fast.
Zoom!

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: A bus is big. A toy car is small.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James and Anna were going to stay at Grandma's farm for the week. They packed their bags — and Chips got in the car too.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Animals on the Farm
uses.pageText: A horse is strong. Horses can pull and carry things.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: An ant is tiny. Ants work together. Ants carry food.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: A boat floats on the water. It can carry things.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: As the plant grows bigger, it makes flowers. Flowers attract bees and butterflies. These visitors carry pollen from flower to flower. This is called pollination.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Female spiders lay eggs in a silk sac. The sac protects the eggs. When they hatch, tiny spiderlings emerge. Some mothers carry the sac everywhere.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Chompy: get berries. Sunny: get leaves. Wiggly: carry things. Dozy: try to stay awake.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: When an insect is caught, the spider wraps it in silk. This keeps it still. Then the spider injects venom to begin digesting its meal.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The marshmallow on Chips's stick got too close to the fire. It caught light. Chips ate the whole thing — stick and all.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Grumpy was stuck. Grumpy's tail was caught under a big rock.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Pip caught one.
It was warm.
It had very large golden eyes.
It looked up at Pip and giggled.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer did it again.
Longer.
The fire was steady.
It was warm.
Glimmer's scales caught the light.
Glimmer had never looked so much like a dragon.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire was very large.
It was taller than Glimmer.
It caught the torch on the Hollow Oak door.
The torch lit the first lamp.
The lamp lit a mushroom.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They put on their helmets and walked the bikes outside. James could not wait. Anna checked the brakes first.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He checked his map. According to the map, he was standing in the Whispering Meadow. He was not in the Whispering Meadow. The paths had moved.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Everyone helped. They checked the Hollow Oak from top to bottom. They walked the paths. They looked in the Whispering Meadow. Nothing triggered the memory.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
An hour later, nothing looked right.
The trees were wrong.
The paths had gone.
"Where are we?" asked Wren.
Flint checked his map.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Oh," said Wren.
"Oh no," said Fern.
"The plants are walking."
Wren checked her book.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: You can see the Moon most nights. On a clear night with a telescope, you can see the craters clearly. Look up tonight — the Moon is always there.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A female frog lays hundreds of eggs in water. The eggs are called frogspawn. Each egg is surrounded by clear jelly that protects it and keeps it safe.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: By midday, more than half the table was clear. Betty sat down on the front step and counted the money tin carefully, then counted it again. "Forty-eight dollars and thirty cents," she announced. Aiden let out a long, astonished breath, which was all he could manage.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Wiggly's long tail swept the Big Flat Rock clear in seconds. Food, supplies, anything that could blow away. Sorry, said Wiggly, sweeping everything. This time everyone was grateful.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We'll clear it," said Pip.
"Now," said Fern.
They spent the afternoon clearing the marsh edge.
As they worked, the spirit watched.
Slowly, it began to sit up.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
When the edge was clear, the spirit stood.
Its shape was clearer now.
"Thank you," said the spirit.
It was not mist anymore.
It was something more solid.
Something more itself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Aiden spent the whole first morning at a rock pool near the headland. He found three kinds of crab, a sea anemone that closed when you touched it, and a tiny fish he thought might be a blenny. He wrote everything down in his field notebook in careful columns.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: I am going to the Long Meadow, said Grumpy. There is a good flat rock there. Peaceful. No one around. Chompy appeared. Can I come? said Chompy. Grumpy closed their eyes. Fine.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: It was exactly like this, said Dozy, looking at all of them, but cloudier. Dozy's eyes closed again. Wake me for supper.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"I wonder," said Wren.
She closed her spell book.
She spoke to the mushroom.
Very quietly.
She asked it the way.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
It was Burrow.
His eyes were closed.
He was fast asleep.
He was walking.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern went to the middle of the clearing.
She closed her eyes.
She sang.
Very softly.
The same song from long ago.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Colours are all around us! What colour can you see?

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can see. My eyes let me see colours and shapes.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Rocks can be many colours. Grey, brown, red, and white.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: The remedy worked. Spark's cold was gone. The flowers slowly turned back to their usual colours. The fish returned to normal.

uses.title: Clothes
uses.pageText: We wear hats on sunny days.

uses.title: Clothes
uses.pageText: We wear coats on cold days.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: At the end of the garden stood a big old oak tree. James and Anna had been staring at it for days.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They decided to grow crystals. It was Betty's original idea and Aiden's second choice, which Betty said made it the obvious answer. They ordered the kit and spent four days watching for the post.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He walked for three days. He did not stop. His map grew longer and longer. It was full of detail.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"Hello," said Fern.
The tiny creature looked up.
"Have you seen my spectacles?" she said.
"I've been looking for three days."

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They decided to grow crystals. It was Betty's original idea and Aiden's second choice, which Betty said made it the obvious answer. They ordered the kit and spent four days watching for the post.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: There would be a running race, a jumping contest, a loudness competition, and a prize for the tidiest corner of the Hollow. More events to be decided, said Bossy. I have a clipboard.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint had decided to map every single path in Moonwood. He had a new roll of parchment and a good quill. He started at the Hollow Oak and walked north.

uses.title: Bob and Nan's First Day at School
uses.pageText: Bob and Nan sit at a desk.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden added a new page to his field notebook: WHAT MAKES A GOOD EXPERIMENT. He had six points. Socks sat on the desk and watched him write, which Aiden had never seen him do before.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Betty read it over his shoulder. She didn't comment on it. She put her hand on his shoulder for a moment and went back to her own desk. That was enough.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Luna flew in through the window. She looked at the desk. She looked more closely. "Wren?" said Luna.

uses.title: Animals Can!
uses.pageText:
A worm can dig.
Dig, dig!

uses.title: Animals Can!
uses.pageText:
A worm can dig.
Dig, dig!

uses.title: Animals Can!
uses.pageText:
A worm can dig.
Dig, dig!

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
An ant is red.
It can dig.

uses.title: Bugs
uses.pageText:
