uses.pageText: Bob and Nan had fun at school!

uses.title: Nan and Bob go to the Zoo
uses.pageText: Nan and Bob had a lot of fun!

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: The play went brilliantly after that. James roared and stomped and the little ones in the front row screamed and giggled.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Clucky got the eggs. Giggly giggled at the eggs.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Clucky got the flour. Giggly giggled at the flour.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Giggly giggled at the cake.

uses.title: Giggly and Clucky Bake a Cake
uses.pageText: Clucky had a bit. Then Clucky giggled too.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Pip caught one.
It was warm.
It had very large golden eyes.
It looked up at Pip and giggled.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Inside the dream, Dozy was wide awake. Dozy had never been so awake. Everything was golden and warm and soft.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy floated on a cloud past the Rainbow Waterfall. But in the dream, the waterfall was made of warm golden light. Oh, said Dozy. This is very nice.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow opened the door. A warm golden light came from inside. Everyone leaned forward.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: They planted the seeds in a ring around the Hollow Oak. One from each of them. In the golden afternoon light.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint followed the mushroom trail.
The forest opened up.
The golden light of the Whispering Meadow was ahead.
"Oh," said Flint.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Pip caught one.
It was warm.
It had very large golden eyes.
It looked up at Pip and giggled.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They played cards in the tent by torchlight. Chips ate two cards before they noticed. The game got harder after that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: He wrote in his notebook that evening: Saying a true thing clearly is harder than it looks and better than it sounds. He underlined it twice.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy ran harder. The scarf was flat out behind. Everything was a blur.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "Maybe you need to try harder," said Spark. Spark's own magic crackled around his ears. Glimmer tried harder. More smoke came out. Still no fire.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "Maybe you need to try harder," said Spark. Spark's own magic crackled around his ears. Glimmer tried harder. More smoke came out. Still no fire.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Then a thunderstorm came. Dozy woke up frightened. All the Dino Pals hid.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky hid in the ferns. Cheeky tied Wiggly's tail to a tree. Hee hee, said Cheeky.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText:
Bouncy went past.
"Come and play!"
Shy hid.

uses.title: Shy Comes Out to Play
uses.pageText:
Tiny went past.
"Come and play!"
Shy hid.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Shy hid behind the barn.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Night fell.
Moonwood glowed softly.
Pip and Glimmer hid behind the big mushroom.
They watched.
Nothing happened.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: Trees have roots under the soil. Roots hold the tree up.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees live together in a hive. One hive can hold up to 60,000 bees. The queen bee lays all the eggs.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy looked at Chompy in the ditch. Grumpy looked at the perfect flat rock. Grumpy sighed. Hold on.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark tried to hold the sneeze in. His eyes went watery. His magic began to build and build. The sparkles around him grew very bright.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "Oh, Chips!" said Anna. But she gave him a big hug. Chips licked her right on the nose.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: Cuddly wants a hug.

uses.title: Cuddly Wants a Hug
uses.pageText: Woolly gave Cuddly a big hug.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Cuddly wants a hug. Cuddly looks and looks.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Cuddly got a hug.

uses.title: Shy and Cuddly Find Each Other
uses.pageText: Shy got a hug too.

uses.title: In the Sea
uses.pageText:
A whale can swim far.
It is huge.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A whale is huge! It is the biggest animal. Whales swim to the top to breathe.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma had a big brown horse called Bess. She was huge and gentle. Her nose was the softest thing James had ever felt.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: Bouncy bumped into Sneezy. Sneezy took a HUGE breath in...

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: The Dino Pals went to look. A huge pile of rocks had fallen in the night and blocked the stream above.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "Socks!" said Aiden and Betty. Socks examined the jar from every angle, turning it slowly. He handed it back eventually — and the crystals were, miraculously, completely intact.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The fire was very large.
It was taller than Glimmer.
It caught the torch on the Hollow Oak door.
The torch lit the first lamp.
The lamp lit a mushroom.

It caught the torch on the Hollow Oak door.
The torch lit the first lamp.
The lamp lit a mushroom.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The light spread.
Mushroom to mushroom.
Lamp to lamp.
Through every path.
Through every dark corner of Moonwood.
All of it lighting up.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The light spread.
Mushroom to mushroom.
Lamp to lamp.
Through every path.
Through every dark corner of Moonwood.
All of it lighting up.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Moonwood blazed with gold.
Every mushroom.
Every lamp.
Every glowing stone.
The forest was more beautiful than anyone had ever seen it.

uses.title: Our Earth
uses.pageText: Earth has land and water.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can be found on land and under the sea. When an underwater volcano keeps erupting, the lava builds up and can make a brand new island!

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can seem frightening. But they have helped shape our planet. They make new land, rich soil and even new islands. They have been doing this for billions of years.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs are amphibians. Amphibians can live in water and on land. Frogs begin their life in water and later move onto land.

uses.title: Frogs

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Three weeks later, the new tooth began to come through. It was enormous relative to the gap — a proper square adult tooth in a mouth that had been full of small rounded baby ones. Aiden looked at himself in the mirror and felt extremely strange.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy crossed the line first. Just. The second runner arrived a heartbeat later.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
An hour later, nothing looked right.
The trees were wrong.
The paths had gone.
"Where are we?" asked Wren.
Flint checked his map.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Almost every plant starts as a tiny seed. Seeds come in hundreds of different shapes and sizes. Each one holds everything a plant needs to begin life.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The top layer is full of life. Coral reefs grow in warm, shallow water. They are home to thousands of kinds of fish and animal. A coral reef is like an underwater city.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: A butterfly's life has four stages. This is called a lifecycle. Each stage looks completely different from the one before.

uses.title: Frogs

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow sat very still and listened.
The room grew warmer.
The carvings lit up one by one.
Luna's voice was quiet and certain.
She had always known these stories.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Pip woke Wren.
They listened together.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
"...they were right here..."
"Something is in the walls," said Wren.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip told Luna.
Luna listened carefully.
"Something is wrong at the marsh," she said.
"We must go in."
Pip, Fern, and Dewdrop came too.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A frog's skin is always damp. Frogs can breathe through their skin as well as through their lungs. They must never dry out.

uses.pageText: It was time to go to the dentist. James did NOT want to go. Anna did NOT want to go. But Mum said they must.

uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream

"Then we go," said Fern.

uses.pageText: A seed needs three things to start growing: water, warmth, and air. When it gets all three, it wakes up and begins to grow.

uses.pageText: Dozy offered a pillow. It needs weight, not softness, said Fancy. Dozy went back to sleep.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip and Stone were sitting outside the Hollow Oak.
Then a noise came from the Fog Marsh.
It was very, very loud.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
At the edge of the marsh, the noise came again.
It was even louder.
Pip's hair stood on end.
Stone appeared behind him.
"I came anyway," said Stone.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
They stood at the edge together.
The fog was thick and grey-green.
The noise bounced off the twisted trees.
"Together," said Stone.
Pip nodded.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Inside the marsh, the noise was everywhere.
The reeds shook.
The water rippled.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James found the grapes. Red ones or green ones? He put both bunches in the basket — just to be safe.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
The plants slowed.
The far ones turned.
They walked back.
Slowly.
Like sleepy creatures going home.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: The first lesson was handwriting — joined-up letters, which were completely new and seemed designed to be tricky. Aiden's pen slipped and he made a large blot right across the middle of the page. He went very red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden added a new page to his field notebook: WHAT MAKES A GOOD EXPERIMENT. He had six points. Socks sat on the desk and watched him write, which Aiden had never seen him do before.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Aiden had started a new notebook that evening — not the Socks field study, but a nature notebook. He had titled it with the date. Betty had started a matching one, without them discussing it. Both were already half a page in.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Pebbles are small, smooth rocks. Water makes them smooth.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a smooth pebble for Grumpy. Someone knows I like pebbles, said Grumpy, suspicious but pleased.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: The tidiest corner prize went to Shy. Shy had arranged twelve perfect pebbles behind a rock where nobody could see them. It counts, said Bossy carefully.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop knew every fish in the Crystal Stream. She talked to them every morning. They told her things: where the water was cold, where the best pebbles were.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: After that, the fish told Dewdrop true things. Small things, mostly. Where the water was coldest. Where the most unusual pebbles were. These things were true.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Community Helpers
uses.pageText: A doctor helps sick people.

uses.title: Water
uses.pageText: People need water to live.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: People have been to the moon! They wore big white suits.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Most spiders are harmless to people. They eat insects that damage our plants. Without spiders, our gardens and crops would be full of pests. Spiders are very helpful friends.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.
Wren had a direction spell.
"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"I am Twig," said the tiny creature.
"I live here."
"I have always lived here."
She seemed perfectly happy about this.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He held it up for a long time. It was tiny. It was the smallest thing that had ever felt significant. He put it in the small envelope Mum left for him, and when he placed it under his pillow it felt ceremonial.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Dozy offered a pillow. It needs weight, not softness, said Fancy. Dozy went back to sleep.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Has anyone seen my pillow? said Dozy. Dozy had been looking for it all morning. This was serious.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Can you see the pillow? said Dozy. There was a long pause. Oh, said Clumsy. Yes. It is in the waterfall.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: I can reach it, said Wiggly. Wiggly stretched the long neck down, down, down. The tail swept three rocks and a berry bush. Sorry. But Wiggly had the pillow.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Dozy hugged the pillow. Thank you, said Dozy. Both of you. Then Dozy fell asleep, right there, on the spot.

uses.title: Reptiles
uses.pageText: Lizards live in warm places.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: Most penguins live in cold places. Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, the coldest and windiest place on Earth. Temperatures can drop below minus 60 degrees!

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: There are 18 species of penguin. Not all live in cold places. Little blue penguins live in Australia. African penguins live on warm, sunny beaches. Every kind of penguin is remarkable.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow went up to find Luna.
"Come with me," he said.
"Bring a light."
Luna said nothing.
She came.

uses.title: Baby Animals
uses.pageText:
A little cub.
It is round and brown.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Rocks can be many colours. Grey, brown, red, and white.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: James and Anna had a pet goat. His name was Chips. He was small and white with big brown patches.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Grandma had a big brown horse called Bess. She was huge and gentle. Her nose was the softest thing James had ever felt.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: These animals come out at night. We are asleep when they are busy!

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Their new classroom was bright and busy, with bookshelves along every wall and a large window that looked out onto the playing field. Their teacher was called Miss Okafor. She had bright yellow glasses and smiled like she really meant it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Mum said it was completely normal and that they had both lost teeth before when they were smaller — Aiden had even eaten one inside a peanut butter sandwich and not noticed for an hour. Aiden was not certain this was reassuring.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow sat very still and listened.
The room grew warmer.
The carvings lit up one by one.
Luna's voice was quiet and certain.
She had always known these stories.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: Sun, rain, wind, snow. Weather changes every day. What is the weather today?

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The moon changes shape. Sometimes it looks like a banana.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: Water can be liquid, ice, or steam. Water changes!

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Slowly, the tadpole changes. Back legs appear first. Then front legs. The tail shrinks away. After about twelve weeks, it is a frog!

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: I think, said Dewdrop slowly, we should find you a cold remedy before anything else changes.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James put his hand straight up. "I want to be the dragon!" Six other children put their hands up too. They would all have to try out.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor had noticed, in the way that good teachers always notice. She started a class discussion about what it means to be fair, and what you do when things aren't. Several children looked at the floor. Marcus looked at the window.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Our Earth
uses.pageText: We must keep Earth clean!

uses.title: Pets We Love
uses.pageText: A goldfish swims in a tank. Fish need clean, fresh water.

uses.title: Staying Healthy
uses.pageText: Wash your hands. Clean hands keep germs away.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: We wash in water. Water keeps us clean.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky helped clean Fancy's rock. Will you do any more pranks? asked Fancy. Maybe just one more, said Cheeky. And winked.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: You can see the Moon most nights. On a clear night with a telescope, you can see the craters clearly. Look up tonight — the Moon is always there.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Monday, Marcus said it one more time, in front of a small group. Aiden turned around. He looked at Marcus directly for a moment. Then he said, clearly: "My name is Aiden." That was all. He turned back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: He wrote in his notebook that evening: Saying a true thing clearly is harder than it looks and better than it sounds. He underlined it twice.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They climbed inside. James held up five fingers. "Five... four... three... two... one... BLAST OFF!"

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: James and Anna climbed up and sat at the little window. "This is the best thing we have ever made," said Anna.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren found her spell book. It was enormous now. She climbed up onto it and looked at the spell. She had read it backwards.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: There would be a running race, a jumping contest, a loudness competition, and a prize for the tidiest corner of the Hollow. More events to be decided, said Bossy. I have a clipboard.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Honky won the loudness competition. Every leaf fell off every tree. We all knew that would happen, said Grumpy.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Grumpy won the grumpiest face competition that Cheeky invented. Grumpy won immediately. I am not sure that is a compliment, said Grumpy. It absolutely is, said Cheeky.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Fancy held a Best Sail competition. Fancy was the only one with a sail. Fancy gave themselves first prize. This seems fair, said Fancy.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Sneezy entered the farthest-blast competition. Sneezy's sneeze sent the test leaf all the way to the Long Meadow. The judge had to run to collect the result. Zippy collected it. Obviously.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: "Imagine standing here," said Betty quietly, "and not knowing what was coming." Aiden thought about that for a long time, looking out. There was something important in it he couldn't quite hold yet. He wrote it in his notebook anyway, to think about later.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: This was the problem with forgetting things. You couldn't always remember what you had forgotten. Luna knew it was important. She knew it was today.

uses.title: Big and Little
uses.pageText:
A big fish.
A little crab.

uses.title: In the Sea
uses.pageText:
A crab can crawl.
Snip, snip!

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A crab has a hard shell. A crab walks sideways.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A crab has a hard shell. A crab walks sideways.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Aiden spent the whole first morning at a rock pool near the headland. He found three kinds of crab, a sea anemone that closed when you touched it, and a tiny fish he thought might be a blenny. He wrote everything down in his field notebook in careful columns.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Socks was fascinated by both of them through this whole period. He kept trying to look in their mouths. He seemed to find it deeply interesting, which Aiden added to the field notebook under: Primate-specific dental curiosity — possible.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the fifth day, Glimmer breathed in as deeply as possible. A warm puff came out. It smelled of cinnamon. "That's something," said Pip.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer breathed in.
Deeply.
Glimmer breathed out.
A jet of orange fire came out.
Small.
Perfect.
Real.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Seeds travel away from the parent plant. Some fly on the wind. Some stick to animals' fur. Some are eaten by birds and fall far away. Some float on water.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: In the morning, dew was on the grass and the birds sang. Chips had eaten a corner of the tent in the night.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Mum said it was completely normal and that they had both lost teeth before when they were smaller — Aiden had even eaten one inside a peanut butter sandwich and not noticed for an hour. Aiden was not certain this was reassuring.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.title: A Seed Grows
uses.pageText:
Rain falls.
Water soaks in.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is winter. It is cold. Snow falls.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: Rumble! Flash! A storm is here. Then the rain falls.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: Rain falls from the clouds. Drip, drip, drip.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky hid in the ferns. Cheeky tied Wiggly's tail to a tree. Hee hee, said Cheeky.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Clumsy could see over all the ferns, past the waterfall, all the way to the Long Meadow and beyond.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy had been very quiet. Sneezy could feel something building. High up. In the pollen from the ferns.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sneezy took a breath in. The biggest breath anyone in Sunny Hollow had ever taken. The ferns bent backwards.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Clumsy stood tall and looked out over the whole Hollow. The storm is coming from the east, said Clumsy. The tall ferns are already bending. That gives us time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor announced the Science Fair on a grey Wednesday in February. Every pair in Grade 1 would present a project. Aiden had his notebook open before she had finished the sentence.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: On the fourth day, Flint held up his finished map. "There," he said. "Every path in Moonwood. All of it."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop crossed the finish line.
She had glided the whole way.
She was not wet.
She was not ruffled.
"Finished," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: Anna found a book about sharks on the shelf. She sat down and read and read. She forgot to feel scared.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: He led them to a shallow pool in a mossy clearing — fed by a spring, perfectly clear and still. Two dragonflies skimmed the surface, electric blue. Aiden crouched at the edge and looked in. Small things moved in the shallows. He forgot to breathe.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: Fruits
uses.pageText: Fruits are good to eat.

uses.title: Fruits
uses.pageText: I love fruits!

uses.title: Healthy Habits
uses.pageText: I eat fruits and vegetables.

uses.title: Staying Healthy
uses.pageText: Eat good food. Fruits and vegetables are good for you.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: This is called pollination. Without bees, many plants could not make seeds. No seeds means no fruits or vegetables. We need bees very much.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Deep underground, rock gets so hot that it melts. This melted rock is called magma. Magma is hotter than anything you can imagine.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A seed needs three things to start growing: water, warmth, and air. When it gets all three, it wakes up and begins to grow.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He loves shiny objects," Uncle Eddie explained at dinner. "He adores warm spots — the airing cupboard is a particular risk. And if he gets bored, he will find a way to become interesting." Everyone filed this information away carefully.

The puddle gets big.
The puddle gets very big.

uses.pageText:

uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Who is leaving these gifts? said Bossy. I need to know. It is not on my clipboard.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Shy! said Sunny, softly. The gifts are from you, aren't they? Shy nodded, going very pink.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: They were the best gifts we ever had, said Sunny. Will you come and sit with us? Shy came out. Just a little way. But it was something.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: The next morning, eleven gifts were on the Big Flat Rock. One from each Dino Pal. A small pink paw reached out and took them, one by one.

uses.title: Magnets
uses.pageText: Magnets do not pull glass.

uses.pageText: James pressed his nose flat to the glass. "That one looks just like a tiny striped rocket!" he said.

uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They had set up a lemonade stand beside the sale table — Betty's idea, planned the previous Thursday. Aiden poured from a glass jug. Betty collected the money and kept the queue moving. By one o'clock they had sold every cup and run entirely out of lemons.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Grumpy was stuck. Grumpy's tail was caught under a big rock.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly walked very carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked Grumpy's favourite rock. Hmph! said Grumpy.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy's club tail lowered into the ditch. Chompy grabbed on. Grumpy pulled. Chompy came out covered in mud.

uses.title: Grumpy Gets a Surprise
uses.pageText: It is Grumpy's birthday.

uses.title: Woolly and Grumpy Are Stuck
uses.pageText: Woolly's wool is on Grumpy's horn.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The judges spent a very long time with Aiden and Betty's crystals — because Betty could explain not just what had happened but why, which turned out to be the whole point of the exercise.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
The next night, it happened again.
More things had moved.
"Was it you?" asked Stone.
"No," said Pip.
"Was it you?" asked Pip.
"No," said everyone.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Night fell.
Moonwood glowed softly.
Pip and Glimmer hid behind the big mushroom.
They watched.
Nothing happened.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have a head. I have a face. I can smile!

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Hello, said Dewdrop. I am the oldest fish in Moonwood, said the fish. Dewdrop tilted her head. The fish was not very large.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern looked around the room.
Then she looked at Twig.
The spectacles were on top of Twig's head.
They had been there all along.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: A small green alien ran to say hello. "My name is Zim!" it said. "Do you want to play?"

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Honky tried very hard to be quiet. Hello, whispered Honky. It still blew Chompy's bib sideways.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Hello, said Dewdrop. I am the oldest fish in Moonwood, said the fish. Dewdrop tilted her head. The fish was not very large.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
"Hello," said Fern.
The tiny creature looked up.
"Have you seen my spectacles?" she said.
"I've been looking for three days."

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
Pip knelt down.
He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.

uses.title: Bob and Nan go to the Park
uses.pageText: Bob and Nan ran up the big hill.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Speedy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Speedy runs to the big hill.

uses.title: Bouncy and Speedy Have a Race
uses.pageText: They ran past the big hill.

uses.title: Tiny and Brave Go on an Adventure
uses.pageText: They went to the big hill. No hat.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: AAAAAAACHOOOOOO! The sneeze hit the rocks like a wave. Rocks scattered in every direction. The stream burst free. The waterfall roared back. A rainbow appeared.

Very fast.
In new directions.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The North Tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They counted every one, out loud, all together. The staircase was so narrow they had to go single file. At the top: the whole landscape, the river, the town, a motorway miles away. The same view and entirely different.

She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

The clearing was empty.
Glimmer's eyes kept closing.
"Don't fall asleep," whispered Pip.

Glimmer was almost asleep.

Everyone was asleep.

Scratch.

The trees drooped.
The water did not move.
Dewdrop led them through the fog.
She could feel the water.

The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.pageText: They had set up a lemonade stand beside the sale table — Betty's idea, planned the previous Thursday. Aiden poured from a glass jug. Betty collected the money and kept the queue moving. By one o'clock they had sold every cup and run entirely out of lemons.

uses.pageText: There would be a running race, a jumping contest, a loudness competition, and a prize for the tidiest corner of the Hollow. More events to be decided, said Bossy. I have a clipboard.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Zippy won the running race before anyone else had started. Does it count if no one saw the finish? asked Bossy. It counts, said Zippy.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Pip reached the Crystal Stream.
He leaped from stone to stone.
One stone was slippery.
Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They made their display board on a rainy Saturday — a bright blue background, a photograph of each day's crystal growth, Betty's data chart, and a title in Aiden's best six-colour lettering: HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW?

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: Some things float. Some things sink. Science is fun!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor announced the Science Fair on a grey Wednesday in February. Every pair in Grade 1 would present a project. Aiden had his notebook open before she had finished the sentence.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: On the morning of the Science Fair, Betty packed the display board in a folder while Aiden carried the crystal jar carefully in both hands. Socks watched from the hallway with what Aiden's notebook called 'intense strategic interest.'

uses.title: Nan and Bob go to the Zoo
uses.pageText: Bob sees a big cat.

uses.title: Nan and Bob go to the Zoo
uses.pageText: Nan sees a red bird.

uses.title: Nan and Bob go to the Zoo
uses.pageText: Nan sees a fat frog on a log.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Splashy Finds a Puddle
uses.pageText: Splashy sees a puddle.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Mum sent up a tray of juice and biscuits on a rope. Dad waved from below. Chips jangled at the base of the tree, trying to reach the biscuits.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Sneezy entered the farthest-blast competition. Sneezy's sneeze sent the test leaf all the way to the Long Meadow. The judge had to run to collect the result. Zippy collected it. Obviously.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.
"Ready?" said Fern.
"Ready," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it loose.
She sent the water flowing hard against the rocks.
The fish did not move.
"I need help," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Reptiles
uses.pageText: Turtles have a hard shell.

uses.pageText: A crab has a hard shell. A crab walks sideways.

uses.pageText: A snail has a shell on its back. A snail moves very slowly.

uses.pageText: After pollination, the flower makes seeds. The seeds grow inside the plant protected by a pod, a fruit, or a shell.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: The female emperor penguin lays one egg. The father balances it on his feet and covers it with a warm flap of skin. He keeps it safe from the freezing cold.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: A frog's skin is always damp. Frogs can breathe through their skin as well as through their lungs. They must never dry out.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: They packed their sleeping bags, a torch, a pack of cards, two books and lots of snacks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy has been asleep for three hours, said Bossy. Should we be worried? said Bossy. Dozy looks very peaceful, said Sunny. They watched Dozy sleeping. Dozy was definitely very peaceful.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Mum said it was completely normal and that they had both lost teeth before when they were smaller — Aiden had even eaten one inside a peanut butter sandwich and not noticed for an hour. Aiden was not certain this was reassuring.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the armoury, there was a full suit of plate armour. It was smaller than Aiden expected. The guide told them that real knights were roughly the same size as Dad, which was very hard to imagine. Aiden tried on a gauntlet under supervision. His hand barely fit inside.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop went close.
"What is wrong?" she asked.
The spirit looked up slowly.
Its eyes were dim.
"My home," it said.
"Every year, smaller."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they both said. But they could not stop smiling. Chips was naughty and cheeky and silly — and they loved him so much.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: That night their legs ached. But they were both smiling. "Same time tomorrow?" said James. Anna was already asleep.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Thank you, said Grumpy. Not that I needed it. But Grumpy was smiling. Just a little.

uses.title: Bouncy Bumps Into Everything
uses.pageText: All the Dino Pals looked at Bouncy. Sorry, said Bouncy, smiling.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Sneezy, dabbing with the handkerchief. Every leaf had fallen off every tree. Do not apologise, said Grumpy. For once, Grumpy was actually smiling.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can touch. My hands can feel if things are rough or smooth, hot or cold.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Pebbles are small, smooth rocks. Water makes them smooth.

uses.title: Rocks and Pebbles
uses.pageText: Pebbles are small, smooth rocks. Water makes them smooth.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a smooth pebble for Grumpy. Someone knows I like pebbles, said Grumpy, suspicious but pleased.

uses.title: Hot and Cold
uses.pageText:
Snow is cold.
It is white.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: This is winter. It is cold. Snow falls.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: Sun, rain, wind, snow. Weather changes every day. What is the weather today?

uses.title: Hot and Cold
uses.pageText: Ice is cold. Snow is cold. Brrr!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna sat next to the bush. "Same bush as before," she said. James laughed from somewhere inside it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
They split into groups.
Each group took a different path.
Each path led somewhere different.
"Find the seeds," said Luna.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Halfway through, everyone was somewhere different.
Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.

uses.title: In the Sea
uses.pageText:
I can swim too!
Splash!

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: Sunny jumped in the puddles. SPLASH! SPLASH! SPLASH!

uses.pageText: Sunny jumped in the puddles. SPLASH! SPLASH! SPLASH!

uses.pageText: Sunny jumped in the puddles. SPLASH! SPLASH! SPLASH!

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
The fish made a very large splash.
Stone was completely wet.
All of Stone.
Dewdrop was not wet.
"I'm sorry," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A ladybird is red with black spots. It eats tiny greenfly.

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They flew past big round planets. Some had red spots. Some had wide, shining rings!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He loves shiny objects," Uncle Eddie explained at dinner. "He adores warm spots — the airing cupboard is a particular risk. And if he gets bored, he will find a way to become interesting." Everyone filed this information away carefully.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: Everyone searched. Bouncy bounced into every corner. Zippy ran everywhere twice. Cheeky looked in all the hiding spots. Nothing.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
That afternoon, it was Glimmer's turn to teach.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer hovered for a moment.
Then landed.
"Like that," said Glimmer.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer ran.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer jumped.
Glimmer glided five whole steps.
"That's more," said Spark.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
The light spread.
Mushroom to mushroom.
Lamp to lamp.
Through every path.
Through every dark corner of Moonwood.
All of it lighting up.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: Seeds travel away from the parent plant. Some fly on the wind. Some stick to animals' fur. Some are eaten by birds and fall far away. Some float on water.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The marshmallow on Chips's stick got too close to the fire. It caught light. Chips ate the whole thing — stick and all.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: The marshmallow on Chips's stick got too close to the fire. It caught light. Chips ate the whole thing — stick and all.

The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James set off first. He got going — then wobbled — then wobbled more — then crashed softly into the hedge. He was fine. Just surprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: On Friday, Marcus said it again in the lunch queue. Betty was right there. She looked at Marcus with exactly one raised eyebrow and said, clearly: "His name is Aiden. Which you know." Marcus looked surprised. He didn't say anything else.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried nesting in a tree. This part actually worked quite well. Flappy was surprised.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Flappy tried eating leaves. Fine. Flappy tried catching insects mid-air. Remarkably good at this. Flappy was more surprised.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dream Bouncy bounced so high that Bouncy went above the clouds and kept going. Everyone watched. Nobody was surprised.

uses.title: How Things Grow
uses.pageText: Growing takes time and care!

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: Butterflies
uses.pageText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Most caves form when rainwater seeps into limestone rock. The water is slightly acidic. It slowly dissolves the rock away. This takes thousands and thousands of years.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "The dentist is very kind," said Mum. "She just takes a little look inside your mouth. That is all."

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At home time, Mum was waiting at the gate. She crouched down with an expectant look. "Well?" she said. They both started talking at exactly the same moment and didn't stop for ten minutes.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Some spiders do not use webs at all. Jumping spiders leap onto their food. They have big eyes that face forward to judge distance. A jumping spider can leap 20 times its own body length!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The school hall was full of projects — a volcano that erupted three times, a model solar system, a survey about favourite foods with real graphs. Betty looked at all of them carefully and said nothing. Aiden chewed the inside of his cheek.

uses.title: Zippy Slows Down
uses.pageText: Sunny found Zippy. I was looking at a flower, said Zippy. I went past it twelve times first.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Are you sure?" said Fern.
"Completely," said Wren.
She had practised many times.
Mostly.

uses.pageText: We use our skin to touch.

uses.pageText: Five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. I use them every day!

uses.pageText: At night, the sun goes away. The sky turns dark.

uses.pageText: Bees carry nectar back to the hive. They pass it from bee to bee. Slowly, it turns into honey.

uses.pageText: When I was a baby, I was tiny. I could not walk or talk.

uses.pageText: In 1969, astronauts travelled to the Moon. Neil Armstrong was the first human to walk on its surface. "That's one small step for man," he said.

uses.pageText: Next came the floor — flat planks, all in a row. "Walk on it!" said Dad. They did. It held firm!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Then all the plants began to walk.
They were very polite about it.
They walked around Fern.
They walked around Wren.
They went for a stroll.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden didn't say anything. He went home and sat on his bed and stared at the ceiling. He wasn't crying, but he wasn't fine either. He didn't really want to talk about it — which Betty noticed immediately.

uses.pageText: We wear pajamas to sleep.

uses.pageText: James and Anna were going to stay at Grandma's farm for the week. They packed their bags — and Chips got in the car too.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James practised his dragon roar all week. It shook the windows. Mum wore earmuffs. Chips ran under the sofa.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
By the end of the week, the fog had crept closer.
The mushrooms at the edge were going out.
One by one.
The fog was not stopping.

uses.title: Butterflies
