uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: After a few weeks, tadpoles wriggle out of the eggs. Tadpoles have tails and no legs. They breathe underwater using gills, like fish.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Slowly, the tadpole changes. Back legs appear first. Then front legs. The tail shrinks away. After about twelve weeks, it is a frog!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Three weeks later, the new tooth began to come through. It was enormous relative to the gap — a proper square adult tooth in a mouth that had been full of small rounded baby ones. Aiden looked at himself in the mirror and felt extremely strange.

A kite is a triangle.

uses.title: Pets We Love
uses.pageText: A hamster is small and fluffy. Hamsters run on a wheel.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A circle is round. The sun is a circle. A wheel is a circle.

uses.title: Spiders
uses.pageText: Many spiders spin webs to catch food. Orb webs are circular with spokes like a wheel. The spider starts with the spokes, then spins a sticky spiral between them.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Then Socks found the crystal jar. He did not eat it. He simply moved it from the windowsill to a high shelf, where he sat beside it with the expression of someone who had just acquired something important.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.pageText: They went out onto the pavement and called his name. "Socks! Socks!" The October wind moved through the trees and sent leaves skittering across the path. No small monkey appeared. Aiden put his hands in his pockets and tried not to feel too worried. It didn't work very well.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden worried about the tooth. It felt wrong — like something was breaking. He wrote in his notebook: Things that are strange: losing a tooth. Also, why teeth? Socks sat on the desk and watched him with great curiosity.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy has been asleep for three hours, said Bossy. Should we be worried? said Bossy. Dozy looks very peaceful, said Sunny. They watched Dozy sleeping. Dozy was definitely very peaceful.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: The summer holidays were over at last. Aiden sat on his bed and stared at his new school bag. Grade 1. The words sounded bigger than they looked.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor announced the Science Fair on a grey Wednesday in February. Every pair in Grade 1 would present a project. Aiden had his notebook open before she had finished the sentence.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

At the centre of the marsh, they found it.
A figure made of grey mist.
It sat against a dead tree.
It was very still.
It looked very sad.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the tenth day, Glimmer went to the Crystal Stream alone. Again and again. Smoke. Sparks. Warm cinnamon breath. Still no fire.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: He looked around to show someone. He was alone. The forest around him looked very different to the forest on his map.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:

The trees had no glow.
The light went only a little way ahead.
They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: An octopus has eight arms. It can change colour. It hides in rocks.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have two arms. I have two hands. I can clap!

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Then Chompy fell into a ditch. HELP, said Chompy. It was not a deep ditch. But Chompy's arms were very tiny.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They climbed to the top.
Moonwood spread below them in the dark.
The sky was full of stars above.
The star spirits reached upward with their tiny arms.

uses.title: Bossy Makes a Plan
uses.pageText: Chompy: get berries. Sunny: get leaves. Wiggly: carry things. Dozy: try to stay awake.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Inside the dream, Dozy was wide awake. Dozy had never been so awake. Everything was golden and warm and soft.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Inside the dream, Dozy was wide awake. Dozy had never been so awake. Everything was golden and warm and soft.

He told Glimmer his plan.
They would stay awake.
They would watch the clearing.
Glimmer said yes immediately.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "I think they like each other," said Anna. "They are just as bad as each other," said James.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: When it passed, Sunny Hollow sparkled. We did that, said Sunny. All of us. Not bad, said Grumpy. From Grumpy, that meant wonderful.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. James grabbed the list. Anna grabbed the bags. Off they went!

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: That night, they got their sleeping bags and climbed up to sleep. Stars shone above them. "Best. Night. Ever," said James. Anna smiled. She agreed.

uses.title: Colors

A red hat.

A ball is round.
It is a circle.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon is a huge ball of rock. It travels around the Earth. It takes about one month to go all the way around. The Moon is our nearest neighbour in space.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks small from Earth, but it is very large. It is about a quarter the size of our whole planet. If Earth were a basketball, the Moon would be a tennis ball.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The far bank was different — thicker trees, softer ground, a field of tall meadow grass beyond the treeline. Socks bounded ahead, turning back every few steps to make sure they were following.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Stone stood at the edge of the Crystal Stream.
The water sparkled.
Stone's feet stayed on the bank.
"I don't like getting wet," said Stone.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
"Just your arm," said Dewdrop.
"Just the one arm."
"Just for a moment."
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the water.
Stone sat down on the bank.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Muddy Has a Bath

uses.pageText: The bath got very muddy.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans. This causes the tides. When the tide comes in, the sea rises up the beach. When it goes out, it pulls back.

uses.title: Bob and Nan go to the Beach
uses.pageText: Bob and Nan go to the beach.

uses.title: Bob and Nan go to the Beach
uses.pageText: Bob and Nan had fun at the beach!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The beach was a five-minute walk down a steep sandy path through tall marram grass. When they came over the last dune and the sea appeared — wide and green and going all the way to the horizon — Aiden stopped walking entirely and just looked for a long moment.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House

He put some in his pocket.
He was still asleep.
Glimmer covered their mouth.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Other volcanoes are very explosive. They blast ash, smoke and rocks high into the sky. The blast can be heard hundreds of kilometres away.

uses.title: Volcanoes

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They climbed inside. James held up five fingers. "Five... four... three... two... one... BLAST OFF!"

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Honky called all the Dino Pals from across the Hollow. One enormous blast. Every leaf fell off. But everyone heard and came running.

uses.title: Things That Float and Sink
uses.pageText: Drop a stone in water. It sinks to the bottom.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: The pool was too deep to reach in. I cannot see my feet, said Clumsy. I certainly cannot reach the bottom.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Everyone helped. They checked the Hollow Oak from top to bottom. They walked the paths. They looked in the Whispering Meadow. Nothing triggered the memory.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon does not make its own light. It has no fire or glow inside. The light we see is sunlight bouncing off the Moon's surface.

uses.pageText: MY SAIL! cried Fancy. Sorry! called Bouncy, already bouncing away.

uses.pageText:
They gathered the star spirits.
There were many of them.
Stone held several.
Wren had two in her hat.
They kept bouncing.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: They got home just in time for lunch. James filled Chips's bowl with fresh grass and sliced apple.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips ate it all in a flash. He looked at the bowl. Then he looked at James. Then he looked at James's jumper.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: He sneezed at breakfast. The porridge turned into a bird. The bird flew out of the window. Spark stared at his empty bowl.

uses.pageText: The shop was big and bright. It smelled of fresh bread and ripe fruit.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "We need bread, grapes, cheese, eggs and orange juice," said James, reading the list carefully.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Anna ran to find the bread. She picked the big round loaf with seeds on top. It smelled amazing!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: On the way home, the bread smelled so good. James started to reach into the bag. Anna gave him a look. He stopped.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" they said. But the sun was warm and breakfast was good and it had been a perfect camp.

uses.title: Chompy's Big Lunch
uses.pageText: That night, Chompy looked at the stars. I wonder what breakfast will be, said Chompy.

uses.pageText: Anna got to brush Bess's mane. James gave her a big red apple. Bess sniffed it — then snaffled the whole thing in one go!

uses.pageText: They found the cheese, the eggs and the juice. James was very careful with the eggs.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At the till, Mum let James put the shopping on the belt. He was VERY careful with the eggs.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Aiden spent the whole first morning at a rock pool near the headland. He found three kinds of crab, a sea anemone that closed when you touched it, and a tiny fish he thought might be a blenny. He wrote everything down in his field notebook in careful columns.

uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.pageText: Bella chased Chips. Chips chased Bella. They ran round and round the garden at an absolutely ridiculous speed.

uses.pageText: Wiggly walked carefully. Wiggly's tail knocked over Chompy's breakfast. Sorry, Chompy!

uses.pageText: Then Chompy fell into a ditch. HELP, said Chompy. It was not a deep ditch. But Chompy's arms were very tiny.

uses.pageText: James chose a big slice of lemon cake with thick white icing. Anna chose a pink strawberry jam tart.

uses.pageText: Now for the best bit — the paint! James chose blue for the walls. Anna chose yellow for the door. Chips chewed the lid off the paint tin.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna found the duck pond. Three white ducks swam in slow circles. One waddled right up and ate seeds from Anna's hand.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: Bella ran in circles round and round Chips. Chips watched her. Then Chips decided to chase Bella.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge
uses.pageText: Stone reached the other side. Stone reached down and picked up Burrow very carefully. "Oh, thank you," said Burrow. "I was going in circles."

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They collect a sweet liquid from inside flowers. This liquid is called nectar.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees also collect yellow dust called pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy legs. When the bee visits the next flower, some pollen falls off. This helps plants make seeds.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Sneezy entered the farthest-blast competition. Sneezy's sneeze sent the test leaf all the way to the Long Meadow. The judge had to run to collect the result. Zippy collected it. Obviously.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it a meeting? asked Fern. I don't think so, said Luna. Was it something to collect? asked Burrow. Possibly, said Luna. I cannot quite say.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Colours are all around us! What colour can you see?

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: An octopus has eight arms. It can change colour. It hides in rocks.

uses.title: Caves
uses.pageText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: He sneezed in the Whispering Meadow. Every flower changed colour at the same moment. The meadow turned entirely blue. It was very quiet.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: They were going to the coast for a whole week — a small blue cottage right on the clifftop, with a gate in the garden wall that opened straight onto the coastal path. Mum had booked it in January. They had been counting down ever since.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty found a small smooth white pebble at the shoreline and turned it over and over in her fingers all the way back to the cottage. She was going to put it on her windowsill at home, so she'd always have a piece of the coast — something real from a real day.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: BANG. They were off. Zippy was first. Of course. But the very fast runner was close. Very close.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.pageText: The plant stopped growing. The leaves curled gently inward. Then, slowly, it began to shrink.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Chips liked to eat. He ate the long green grass. He ate sticks and bits of bark. One day, he ate Dad's best hat!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The lighthouse was Dad's idea. It was tall and white and stood on a headland two miles along the coastal path. There were one hundred and forty-seven steps to the top — they counted every single one, out loud, all together, and arrived slightly out of breath but very proud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie was Dad's younger brother, and he was a wildlife researcher who had spent the last two years living near a tropical rainforest, studying primates. He had, apparently, brought one with him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: In the deepest, darkest water, some creatures make their own light. This is called bioluminescence. The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure to attract prey.

uses.title: Under the Ocean
uses.pageText: The deepest part of the ocean is called the Mariana Trench. It is nearly 11 kilometres deep. If you put the world's tallest mountain inside it, it would still be covered by water.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Shy, who knew every hidden corner of the Fernwood, led everyone to the deepest part of Cozy Cave. Shy knew exactly where it was warmest.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark

It was the deepest part of the night.
Moonwood was very quiet.
Then there was a sound at the edge of the clearing.
Something small was there.

uses.pageText: They ate their sandwiches by the duck pond. Chips waited at home. Chips and bikes were definitely not a good idea.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: He told Betty. Betty got the torch and studied it with great interest. "It's definitely loose," she said. "It'll fall out and a permanent one will grow. That's much better, actually." Aiden was not entirely sure that it was.

uses.pageText: Dozy has been asleep for three hours, said Bossy. Should we be worried? said Bossy. Dozy looks very peaceful, said Sunny. They watched Dozy sleeping. Dozy was definitely very peaceful.

Her eyes went wide.
Then soft.

Very quietly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive took three hours. Betty counted every red car they passed. Aiden read two chapters of his book, fell asleep on his own shoulder, woke up, read another chapter, and then asked "Are we nearly there?" for the fourth time. They were, finally, nearly there.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "Yes!" said James and Anna. James grabbed the list. Anna grabbed the bags. Off they went!

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: "We need bread, grapes, cheese, eggs and orange juice," said James, reading the list carefully.

uses.pageText: Anna made a list. "We will need planks of wood, nails, rope, hinges and paint," she said. "And a flag."

But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

"I am Twig," said the tiny creature.
"I live here."
"I have always lived here."
She seemed perfectly happy about this.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak

Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Inside was a small round room. The walls were covered in tiny glowing drawings. Trees and streams. Creatures and old paths. Every living thing that had ever been in Moonwood.

uses.pageText: Magnets push and pull too! A magnet can pull a pin.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: Wiggly felt sad. My tail has a mind of its own, said Wiggly.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "Does it hurt?" said Aiden. "Not really," said Betty. "It felt strange for a second. Then it was over." She looked at the gap in her mouth in a small mirror. "It's just a tooth," she said. "A very old, very small tooth."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Three weeks later, the new tooth began to come through. It was enormous relative to the gap — a proper square adult tooth in a mouth that had been full of small rounded baby ones. Aiden looked at himself in the mirror and felt extremely strange.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: After that, the fish told Dewdrop true things. Small things, mostly. Where the water was coldest. Where the most unusual pebbles were. These things were true.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Are you sure?" said Fern.
"Completely," said Wren.
She had practised many times.
Mostly.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They had set up a lemonade stand beside the sale table — Betty's idea, planned the previous Thursday. Aiden poured from a glass jug. Betty collected the money and kept the queue moving. By one o'clock they had sold every cup and run entirely out of lemons.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then — a sound.
A shuffling.
A round shape moving through the clearing.
Pip and Glimmer looked at each other.
They crept closer.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Glimmer could not stop.
Glimmer hit Spark.
Sparkles went everywhere.
They both kept moving.
Very fast.
In new directions.

uses.title: Nan and Bob get Sick

uses.title: Nan and Bob get Sick
uses.pageText: Nan has a nap. Fluff has a nap too.

uses.pageText: Fluff had a nap. Good dog, Fluff!

uses.title: Wiggly's Messy Day
uses.pageText: I like your tail, said Dozy sleepily. It fans me while I nap. The Dino Pals all agreed.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The North Tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They counted every one, out loud, all together. The staircase was so narrow they had to go single file. At the top: the whole landscape, the river, the town, a motorway miles away. The same view and entirely different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Everyone had their own desk with a name label. Aiden's said AIDEN in neat blue letters. He ran his finger over it slowly and felt, just slightly, like it might turn out to be all right.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Betty made neat round price stickers on square labels, writing each price in her best handwriting. Aiden made the sign for the front gate — YARD SALE: EVERYTHING MUST GO — in six colours, with three exclamation marks, then a fourth one, just to make sure.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: A week later, Marcus bumped into Aiden's tray at lunch — accidentally this time, genuinely. He said sorry, just once, with his eyes down. Aiden nodded. He didn't make a big thing of it. Some things, he thought, didn't need to become a story.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: Shy! said Sunny, softly. The gifts are from you, aren't they? Shy nodded, going very pink.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
They stood at the edge together.
The fog was thick and grey-green.
The noise bounced off the twisted trees.
"Together," said Stone.
Pip nodded.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"What does flying feel like?" asked Spark.
Glimmer thought.
"Like falling upward," said Glimmer.
Spark nodded slowly.
"I think I understand."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They ran. All four of them, in their socks, without stopping to find shoes, down the pavement to number thirty-seven. They could hear, even from the gate, a small and very determined crunching sound coming from inside.

uses.pageText: Chompy offered to sit on the sail to flatten it. ABSOLUTELY NOT, said Fancy.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Bouncy offered to bounce on it gently. That is not what gently means, said Fancy.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Dozy offered a pillow. It needs weight, not softness, said Fancy. Dozy went back to sleep.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Honky offered to shout at it until it moved. Everyone agreed this would make things much worse.

uses.pageText: The young frog climbs out of the water. It can now breathe air through its lungs. It can also live on land. The whole world opens up.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Betty had the guide map. She navigated with precise efficiency — Great Hall, Armoury, North Tower, King's Chamber, Dungeon — the best order for minimum backtracking. Aiden followed behind her, reading every information board they passed, completely at home in a world of facts.

uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.pageText: Chips had been quiet all morning. Then they found him — in the veggie patch, eating the bean plants.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: They reached the meadow. Grumpy found the flat rock and sat on it. Chompy found a berry patch immediately.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: This is a good rock, said Chompy. Yes, said Grumpy. Is there anything to eat near it? said Chompy. Grumpy pointed at the berry patch. Chompy went happily.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow found a blank patch of wall. He picked up a small flat stone. Very carefully, he drew the Hollow Oak. Now we are in it too, he said.

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: James and Anna helped bang in the tent pegs and thread the poles through. Chips ate one peg. Then he tried to eat a second.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.pageText: They played cards in the tent by torchlight. Chips ate two cards before they noticed. The game got harder after that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

uses.title: The Big Farm Party
uses.pageText: Noisy played the music. It was very, very loud.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Betty lost her first tooth the very next day, which nobody had seen coming. It came out at lunch, and she held it up and examined it with great interest before putting it in her pocket, as if this were a routine scientific procedure.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "The stone did that!" said Pip. He tucked it safely into his pocket. Then he walked toward the Fog Marsh.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
He found the acorn biscuits.
He put some in his pocket.
He was still asleep.
Glimmer covered their mouth.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: There would be a running race, a jumping contest, a loudness competition, and a prize for the tidiest corner of the Hollow. More events to be decided, said Bossy. I have a clipboard.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: The tidiest corner prize went to Shy. Shy had arranged twelve perfect pebbles behind a rock where nobody could see them. It counts, said Bossy carefully.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Fancy held a Best Sail competition. Fancy was the only one with a sail. Fancy gave themselves first prize. This seems fair, said Fancy.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.pageText: Grumpy pulled and pulled. Grumpy was still stuck.

uses.title: Grumpy Needs Help
uses.pageText: Grumpy pulled and pulled. Grumpy was still stuck.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy's club tail lowered into the ditch. Chompy grabbed on. Grumpy pulled. Chompy came out covered in mud.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They pushed and pulled together.
The boulder shifted.
The mud let go.
The boulder rolled aside.

uses.title: Pets We Love
uses.pageText: A rabbit is a pet. Rabbits are soft and fluffy. They twitch their noses.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: After rain, look up! A rainbow! Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: One morning, Rainbow Waterfall was not making rainbows. It was not making anything at all. The waterfall had stopped.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: AAAAAAACHOOOOOO! The sneeze hit the rocks like a wave. Rocks scattered in every direction. The stream burst free. The waterfall roared back. A rainbow appeared.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: Dozy floated on a cloud past the Rainbow Waterfall. But in the dream, the waterfall was made of warm golden light. Oh, said Dozy. This is very nice.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie was Dad's younger brother, and he was a wildlife researcher who had spent the last two years living near a tropical rainforest, studying primates. He had, apparently, brought one with him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie explained that he was returning to the rainforest for six months and couldn't bring Socks along this time. He looked at Dad with a hopeful expression. Dad said yes before Mum could say anything at all, which was exactly what Mum had expected him to do.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
"Oh," said Fern.
She remembered.
Two nights ago she had been in the clearing.
She had planted the seeds.
She had not meant to forget.

uses.pageText: "James!" called the dentist. He stood up. He walked in. The big chair went up and down like a ride!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Anna!" called the dentist. Anna walked in. She sat in the big chair. She had to admit — it was like a ride.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: By lunchtime, they could both ride all the way down the long lane and back without stopping once.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Dad got his old bike out and the three of them went for a long ride down to the duck pond.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The morning felt strange. The air was heavy and still. Mount Rumble was not puffing its usual heart-shaped rings.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Socks had other interests. He had crossed a wide fallen tree over the river before anyone had finished the sentence. Aiden said they should follow. Uncle Eddie said absolutely not. Then Uncle Eddie looked at the tree. Then they crossed it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The North Tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They counted every one, out loud, all together. The staircase was so narrow they had to go single file. At the top: the whole landscape, the river, the town, a motorway miles away. The same view and entirely different.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna set off nice and slowly. She did not wobble. She did not crash. She rode all the way to the end of the path and back.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: On the way back, the sun was low and the meadow was full of seed heads catching the light. Socks rode on Uncle Eddie's shoulder, which he had always done but which now looked, here, like a kind of homecoming.

uses.title: Shapes
uses.pageText: A roof is a triangle.

uses.title: Shapes Everywhere
uses.pageText: A triangle has three sides. A pizza slice is a triangle. A roof is a triangle.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: When the paint was dry, Anna cut a red star from felt and glued it on the flag. James fixed the flag to a long stick and tied it to the roof.

uses.title: Fern Grows Too Much
uses.pageText: By afternoon, the plant had grown through the roof. It was still growing. Everyone stood back and watched.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A rose is red. It smells sweet. It has sharp thorns.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Then Chips saw a big rose bush. He ran at it. CRUNCH! MUNCH! SNAP! The rose bush was gone.

uses.title: James and Anna and Chips
uses.pageText: Then Chips saw a big rose bush. He ran at it. CRUNCH! MUNCH! SNAP! The rose bush was gone.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"This way," said Flint.
He was right.
The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.
"I always find things," said Flint.
"Eventually."

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Then Anna spotted the cake stand! Big cakes, small cakes, jam tarts and iced buns — all in a long, shining row.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: Next came the floor — flat planks, all in a row. "Walk on it!" said Dad. They did. It held firm!

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: The play went brilliantly after that. James roared and stomped and the little ones in the front row screamed and giggled.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: Rumble! Flash! A storm is here. Then the rain falls.

uses.title: My Body
uses.pageText: I have a tummy. Food goes into my tummy. Rumble!

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: At the top of Mount Rumble, all the Dino Pals were there. Sitting on the warm peak. Watching all of Sunny Hollow spread out below, tiny and green and perfect.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The morning felt strange. The air was heavy and still. Mount Rumble was not puffing its usual heart-shaped rings.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: By three o'clock, the sky had gone grey and the wind had picked up. Aiden was sitting on the front step, not saying much. He kept thinking about what Uncle Eddie had said once: that animals raised by hand always know where home is. He held onto that thought very carefully.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "What happened?" said Betty. Aiden told her in pieces, looking at the floor. Betty listened to all of it without saying anything. Then she said: "He's wrong. And being wrong loudly is still just being wrong." Aiden thought about that.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: He wrote in his notebook that evening: Saying a true thing clearly is harder than it looks and better than it sounds. He underlined it twice.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Then James tried riding with NO hands. He made it exactly three seconds before heading straight into the same bush.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Wiggly's long tail swept the Big Flat Rock clear in seconds. Food, supplies, anything that could blow away. Sorry, said Wiggly, sweeping everything. This time everyone was grateful.

uses.title: Five Senses
uses.pageText: My five senses help me learn!

uses.title: Our Five Senses
uses.pageText: Our senses help us explore!

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I have five senses. They help me know the world.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: Five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. I use them every day!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna settled on a ledge.
She folded her wings.
She looked at the carvings for a moment.
"The first story of Moonwood," she began,
"is this."

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
It was very late when Burrow noticed.
"Will you tell me the rest?" he asked.
"Yes," said Luna.
"There is quite a lot."
They both settled in.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
One by one they found their places.
Each plant settled.
The smallest sat down last.
It made a small sound.
It seemed happy.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Shh! said Grumpy. SORRY! said Honky. More leaves fell.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "Shh!" said everyone.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "Shh!" said everyone.

uses.title: Noisy Tries to Be Quiet
uses.pageText: "SHH!" said everyone.

uses.title: A Seed Grows
uses.pageText: A green shoot grows up.

uses.title: Little Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: A green shoot comes up! It has two small leaves.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: First, a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Roots drink up water from the ground. Then a small shoot pushes up toward the light above.

uses.title: How Seeds Grow
uses.pageText: The shoot breaks through the soil. It opens its first leaves toward the sun. Now the plant can begin to make its own food.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "How on earth did he get in?" asked Dad. Mrs Obi pointed to the cat flap in her back door. Of course. Socks had worked out the cat flap. He had also — from the state of the shortbread tin — clearly been in before, which nobody had known and which explained certain things about Mrs Obi's biscuit situation.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A crab has a hard shell. A crab walks sideways.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Honky tried very hard to be quiet. Hello, whispered Honky. It still blew Chompy's bib sideways.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: Burrow was digging a new tunnel. He dug down, and he dug sideways, and he dug carefully around the roots. Then his spade hit something hard and wooden.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They all came to look. The tunnel was small. Stone had to go sideways. Luna had to be helped around three corners.

uses.title: My Five Senses
uses.pageText: I can hear. My ears let me hear sounds.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: He wrote in his notebook that evening: Saying a true thing clearly is harder than it looks and better than it sounds. He underlined it twice.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

uses.title: Penguins
uses.pageText: There are 18 species of penguin. Not all live in cold places. Little blue penguins live in Australia. African penguins live on warm, sunny beaches. Every kind of penguin is remarkable.

uses.title: Frogs
uses.pageText: Frogs sing to find a mate. Each species has its own call. The ribbit of a tree frog, the deep croak of a bullfrog — their calls fill warm evenings around the world.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"This is the Memory Room," said Luna.
"This is where Moonwood keeps its oldest stories."
Burrow looked at the carvings.
"All of them?" he asked.
"All of them," said Luna.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow sat very still and listened.
The room grew warmer.
The carvings lit up one by one.
Luna's voice was quiet and certain.
She had always known these stories.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: Rumble! Flash! A storm is here. Then the rain falls.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Storm coming, said Grumpy. Big one. Grumpy was almost always right about weather. Everyone believed Grumpy.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Clumsy stood tall and looked out over the whole Hollow. The storm is coming from the east, said Clumsy. The tall ferns are already bending. That gives us time.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The drive home felt half as long as the drive there, which Aiden thought was mathematically impossible. When they turned into their street, the house looked completely the same as when they'd left it. Aiden noticed he felt, quietly, like he was a little bit different.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: You push a swing. The swing goes up high!

uses.title: Push and Pull
uses.pageText: You push a swing. The swing goes up high!

uses.title: Bob and Nan go to the Park
uses.pageText: Bob got on the big swing.

uses.title: Bob and Nan go to the Park
uses.pageText: Nan got on the big swing.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: Third place, with a commendation for experimental method, went to HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW? The commendation was on a proper certificate with a gold border. Betty read every word of it, twice.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: But you didn't, said Sunny. Zippy ran four more circuits of Sunny Hollow. I know, said Zippy, on the third lap. I just like to make sure.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Spark. This was his third sorry. He meant all three of them very much.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
On the third day, the diagrams had multiplied.
There were charts about heat.
Charts about breathing.
Charts about dragon anatomy.
Glimmer stared at them all.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: One jar of honey needs thousands of bee trips to make. Bees visit two million flowers for just one jar! Next time you eat honey, think of all those busy bees.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Honky, said Bossy, you need an inside voice. What is an inside voice? A quiet one. I do not have one of those.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: We need to move those rocks, said Bossy. Everyone tried pushing. The rocks did not move at all.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"Why didn't we try that first?" asked Flint.
"I don't know," said Wren.
She looked back at the mushroom trail.
"They seemed happy about it though."
The last mushroom blinked once and went out.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Betty had the guide map. She navigated with precise efficiency — Great Hall, Armoury, North Tower, King's Chamber, Dungeon — the best order for minimum backtracking. Aiden followed behind her, reading every information board they passed, completely at home in a world of facts.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The North Tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They counted every one, out loud, all together. The staircase was so narrow they had to go single file. At the top: the whole landscape, the river, the town, a motorway miles away. The same view and entirely different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: At lunch, they sat together by the window. Aiden opened his lunchbox and found a small folded note from Mum tucked under his sandwich. It said: You've got this, star. He smiled all the way through his apple.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden picked him up and held him. Socks was warm and solid and smelled faintly of shortbread. He patted Aiden's cheek twice with one small black hand, the way he sometimes did when he felt like being kind, and then tucked his head under Aiden's chin. Aiden breathed out slowly.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "The stone did that!" said Pip. He tucked it safely into his pocket. Then he walked toward the Fog Marsh.

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: "Open wide!" said the dentist. She used a small mirror and a bright little light. "All done! Ten out of ten!" James grinned.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "You don't look strange," said Betty. "You look older." She said it the way she said true things — simply, as though it were just a fact. Aiden looked in the mirror again. It was going to take some getting used to.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren found the problem.
She had used the wrong book.
"This is the motion recipe," she said.
"Not the growing recipe."
She showed Fern.
They were both quiet for a moment.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The view from the top was unlike anything Aiden had seen. The whole coastline curved away in both directions — bays and headlands, a small fishing village far below, and the sea stretching to the horizon, catching the light like crinkled silver foil.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The North Tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They counted every one, out loud, all together. The staircase was so narrow they had to go single file. At the top: the whole landscape, the river, the town, a motorway miles away. The same view and entirely different.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: That evening, Aiden wrote in his field notebook for a long time — the drawbridge, the worn floor, the arrow loop, the view. At the bottom of the last page he wrote: Things were happening before we got here. They'll keep happening after. That's not sad. That's just how big it is. He underlined it.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Sometimes, magma pushes up through a crack in the Earth. When it bursts out at the surface, we call it a volcano! The melted rock that flows out is called lava.

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: Volcanoes can be found on land and under the sea. When an underwater volcano keeps erupting, the lava builds up and can make a brand new island!

uses.title: Volcanoes
uses.pageText: After a volcano, the cooled lava becomes new rock. Volcanic rock breaks down into rich, dark soil. Many plants and crops grow very well in volcanic soil.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The school hall was full of projects — a volcano that erupted three times, a model solar system, a survey about favourite foods with real graphs. Betty looked at all of them carefully and said nothing. Aiden chewed the inside of his cheek.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: They ate their sandwiches by the duck pond. Chips waited at home. Chips and bikes were definitely not a good idea.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "He is completely impossible," said Mum, as she did most evenings. But she had also started setting a small dish of whatever she was cooking on the corner of the counter every night, because Socks knew exactly where it appeared and waited there very patiently, and she had not been able to bring herself to stop.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Every morning, Socks sat on the kitchen counter and waited while Betty did up the buttons on his little red waistcoat, which always lived on its own peg beside the back door. But on a Tuesday in October, the peg was empty. And when Aiden went to check, Socks's sleeping box in the corner of his room was empty too.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One morning, Sunny stayed very still and very quiet behind a fern. Sunny waited.

uses.title: Healthy Habits
uses.pageText: I wash my hands with soap.

uses.title: Water
uses.pageText: We wash in water.

uses.title: Staying Healthy
uses.pageText: Wash your hands. Clean hands keep germs away.

uses.title: Water Everywhere
uses.pageText: We wash in water. Water keeps us clean.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Wiggly tried to win the tidiest corner. The tail knocked everything over while tidying. I am giving myself zero points, said Wiggly.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Dozy slept through most of the events and woke up in time for the picnic. Did I win anything? said Dozy. Most restful competitor, said Bossy. Deserved, said Dozy, and fell asleep again.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy will win easily, said Sunny. Obviously, said Bossy. Hmph. Probably, said Grumpy. Zippy went very quiet.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: James practised his dragon roar all week. It shook the windows. Mum wore earmuffs. Chips ran under the sofa.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On Wednesday it rained all morning. They played three rounds of Cluedo, drank hot chocolate in large mugs and listened to the rain hammer against the cottage windows. It was, Aiden thought, pressing his mug to his chin, one of the cosiest mornings he could remember.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty found the bird hide first — a long wooden structure with narrow slot windows over the reed bed. Inside: a log book, borrowed binoculars, and a board listing twelve species to find. She was immediately in her element.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: Anna set off nice and slowly. She did not wobble. She did not crash. She rode all the way to the end of the path and back.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James tried again. Eyes forward. Pedal. Wobble. Wobble. Then — he was doing it! He was really, properly doing it!

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: James tried again. Eyes forward. Pedal. Wobble. Wobble. Then — he was doing it! He was really, properly doing it!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: That night, Dad built Socks a cosy sleeping box — a wooden crate lined with a soft fleece blanket — and settled it in the warm corner of the kitchen. In the morning, Socks was not in it. He was curled up fast asleep at the foot of Aiden's bed, his small black hand curled around Aiden's pencil torch.
