uses.pageText: Miss Okafor announced the Science Fair on a grey Wednesday in February. Every pair in Grade 1 would present a project. Aiden had his notebook open before she had finished the sentence.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The school hall was full of projects — a volcano that erupted three times, a model solar system, a survey about favourite foods with real graphs. Betty looked at all of them carefully and said nothing. Aiden chewed the inside of his cheek.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "What shall we study?" said Betty. They sat with the notebook between them and listed every idea they had. Aiden had eleven. Betty had nine. Three of them were exactly the same, which Betty said proved they had good scientific minds.

uses.title: What is Flappy?
uses.pageText: Bossy flies, said Flappy. Bossy is a Pterodactyl. You are an Archaeopteryx. That is different. How is it different? said Flappy. Grumpy did not actually know.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The morning felt strange. The air was heavy and still. Mount Rumble was not puffing its usual heart-shaped rings.

uses.title: Look at the Colours!
uses.pageText: Orange. An orange fox. An orange pumpkin.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: On the way down, Aiden stopped at a narrow slit window in the tower wall — an arrow loop. He looked through it. The angle was exact — a perfect line of sight across the approach. Everything in this building was designed for a specific purpose.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: We need to move those rocks, said Bossy. Everyone tried pushing. The rocks did not move at all.

uses.pageText: The air horn worked. The fox did not come back. Dad DID come — running from the house in his pyjamas, looking very startled.

uses.title: Bees
uses.pageText: Bees live together in a hive. One hive can hold up to 60,000 bees. The queen bee lays all the eggs.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty answered three questions out loud and got them all right. Aiden raised his hand once, very carefully, and he got his right too. Miss Okafor stuck a gold star beside both their names on the board. Aiden looked at his star for quite a long time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: Aiden's tooth came out on a Thursday. Not dramatically — he was reading his book and he touched it and then it was just there in his fingers, which was very quick and very strange and did not hurt at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: "We should have a yard sale," said Betty. She said it the way she said all her best ideas — quickly and firmly, as though the idea had already made up its mind. "We could make actual money." Aiden wasn't certain at first, but when she said the word money, he started to listen.

uses.title: Pets We Love
uses.pageText: A rabbit is a pet. Rabbits are soft and fluffy. They twitch their noses.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: One morning, Rainbow Waterfall was not making rainbows. It was not making anything at all. The waterfall had stopped.

uses.title: Seasons
uses.pageText: In spring, it rains.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Then the phone rang. It was their neighbour Mrs Obi, from number thirty-seven, three houses down. Her voice was very precise. "I believe," she said carefully, "that there may be a small monkey in my kitchen. He appears to be eating my shortbread."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: "I think he'll be disappointed when we stop changing," said Aiden. "He already has all the teeth he'll get," said Betty. Socks demonstrated this by grinning at them both from very close range, showing every single tooth.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Aiden re-read his field notebook carefully, looking for anything useful. He had written: Drawn to shiny objects. Drawn to warm spots. Will follow interesting smells. Exceptionally good at getting into places he shouldn't. He stared at that last line for quite a long time. It did not narrow things down.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: There was a boy in Year 2 called Marcus who thought it was funny to call people names. He had decided, for reasons that made no sense at all, that Aiden's name was Lazy-den. He said it on Wednesday. Two children laughed, which made him say it again on Thursday.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth

uses.pageText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: "I think he might be learning," said Aiden carefully, watching Socks watch the pen. "Don't encourage him," said Betty, from the doorway. Socks blinked once, in a way that suggested he had already learned considerably more than anyone knew.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the armoury, there was a full suit of plate armour. It was smaller than Aiden expected. The guide told them that real knights were roughly the same size as Dad, which was very hard to imagine. Aiden tried on a gauntlet under supervision. His hand barely fit inside.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: People have been to the moon! They wore big white suits.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The crystal-growing worked perfectly. Blue copper sulphate crystals grew on a thread in a jam jar, getting bigger and more geometric every day. Aiden photographed them every morning. Betty kept a careful growth chart.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie left on Sunday evening. He stayed on the doorstep a long time, saying goodbye properly. When the car was gone, Socks sat on the hall windowsill and watched the empty road. Then he came inside and sat on Aiden's lap, which he had never done before. Aiden stayed very still.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A sunflower is tall and yellow. The sun makes it grow.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Anna painted for three whole days. She made mountains, a red sunset sky and a tall castle with a flag. Everyone said it was brilliant.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the armoury, there was a full suit of plate armour. It was smaller than Aiden expected. The guide told them that real knights were roughly the same size as Dad, which was very hard to imagine. Aiden tried on a gauntlet under supervision. His hand barely fit inside.

uses.title: Dozy's Wonderful Dream
uses.pageText: It was exactly like this, said Dozy, looking at all of them, but cloudier. Dozy's eyes closed again. Wake me for supper.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: It started with a slight wobble. Aiden was eating an apple when he felt, for the first time in his life, that one of his front teeth was moving in a way that front teeth were definitely not supposed to move.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: The school hall was full of projects — a volcano that erupted three times, a model solar system, a survey about favourite foods with real graphs. Betty looked at all of them carefully and said nothing. Aiden chewed the inside of his cheek.

uses.title: Shy's Secret Gift
uses.pageText: One day it was a smooth pebble for Grumpy. Someone knows I like pebbles, said Grumpy, suspicious but pleased.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
uses.pageText: In the morning, the tooth was gone and there was a coin in its place. Aiden knew, in the way children who read a lot know things, that it was Mum or Dad who had swapped it. He said nothing, because some things are better left as stories.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Wiggly's long tail swept the Big Flat Rock clear in seconds. Food, supplies, anything that could blow away. Sorry, said Wiggly, sweeping everything. This time everyone was grateful.

uses.title: Sneezy and the Waterfall
uses.pageText: Grumpy has a strong tail, said Sunny. Grumpy swung the club tail at the rocks. CLONK. One small rock moved. There were fifty more.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: They searched everywhere. Aiden checked under every sofa cushion and behind every bookshelf. Betty methodically looked in every high cupboard. Mum turned the garden upside down. Dad searched the garden again, more systematically, with a torch — even though it was daytime. Socks was not anywhere.

uses.title: Nan and Bob Learn to Read
uses.pageText: C - A - T. Cat! Bob can get it!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: Betty designed a MISSING MONKEY poster on her tablet in under five minutes. It had a photograph of Socks in his waistcoat, a written description, and their phone number in large digits. She printed fourteen copies. They posted them through letter boxes up and down both sides of the street without stopping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: James and Anna go to Space
uses.pageText: They cut and snipped and stuck and taped. They worked all morning long.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: James chose a big slice of lemon cake with thick white icing. Anna chose a pink strawberry jam tart.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: Then Anna spotted the cake stand! Big cakes, small cakes, jam tarts and iced buns — all in a long, shining row.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: That evening, Grandma made soup from the garden and fried the eggs James had found. It was the best meal they had ever tasted.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Miss Okafor had noticed, in the way that good teachers always notice. She started a class discussion about what it means to be fair, and what you do when things aren't. Several children looked at the floor. Marcus looked at the window.

uses.title: Clumsy to the Rescue
uses.pageText: We make a good team, said Clumsy. You see the problem. I reach the problem. Exactly, said Clumsy, and accidentally knocked off Wiggly's hat. Sorry.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: Mum and Dad clapped the loudest. Mum had tears. Dad said it was just the bright lights. James and Anna did not believe him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Betty wrote down every species she could identify in the hide log book, which she had technically borrowed without permission. Uncle Eddie said they'd bring it back. She wrote in neat columns: dragonflies, water boatmen, a great diving beetle.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: In the castle shop, Betty bought a small accurate model of the castle as it looked in 1350, before a section of wall fell. Aiden bought a book on medieval building techniques. Dad bought a novelty ceramic goblet that Mum said, quietly but firmly, would not be coming into the kitchen.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks explored the house in eleven minutes. He opened every drawer he could reach, rearranged the fruit bowl into a different order, sat briefly on each windowsill and posted three letters from the hall table into the back of the television. He seemed very pleased with his work.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat. It was the right temperature. The right shape. Grumpy almost smiled.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The last day of the summer term was also the loudest day of the school year. Aiden and Betty burst through the front door and both shouted "HOLIDAY!" at exactly the same moment, which echoed all the way up the stairs and made the dog next door bark.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Sneezy entered the farthest-blast competition. Sneezy's sneeze sent the test leaf all the way to the Long Meadow. The judge had to run to collect the result. Zippy collected it. Obviously.

uses.title: Chompy and Grumpy's Day Out
uses.pageText: Grumpy sat on the rock alone. It was peaceful. But after a while, Grumpy called: There is a good-looking bush to your left. Thanks, Grumpy! said Chompy. Grumpy said nothing. But the corner of the mouth went up. Just slightly.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The far bank was different — thicker trees, softer ground, a field of tall meadow grass beyond the treeline. Socks bounded ahead, turning back every few steps to make sure they were following.

uses.title: The Moon
uses.pageText: The Moon looks different every night. Sometimes it is a full, bright circle. Sometimes it is a thin crescent. These different shapes are called the phases of the Moon.

uses.title: Flowers and Trees
uses.pageText: A rose is red. It smells sweet. It has sharp thorns.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: A girl called Rosa arrived late with her grandmother and spent a thoughtful amount of time choosing. She ended up with three books, a snow globe and the foam sword, which she tucked under her arm like a very satisfied general. Aiden watched the sword go and found he didn't mind at all.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: IT IS OKAY! called Honky. Honky's voice was louder than the thunder. Dozy stopped shaking.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Then a thunderstorm came. Dozy woke up frightened. All the Dino Pals hid.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Wiggly tried to win the tidiest corner. The tail knocked everything over while tidying. I am giving myself zero points, said Wiggly.

uses.title: James and Anna's New Bikes
uses.pageText: On the way home, James and Anna raced. They crossed the gate post at exactly the same time. A perfect tie.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: James and Anna go Shopping
uses.pageText: At the till, Mum let James put the shopping on the belt. He was VERY careful with the eggs.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Science Fair
uses.pageText: They made their display board on a rainy Saturday — a bright blue background, a photograph of each day's crystal growth, Betty's data chart, and a title in Aiden's best six-colour lettering: HOW DO CRYSTALS GROW?

uses.title: James, Anna and Chips go Camping
uses.pageText: Dad made a small camp fire in a safe metal dish. They toasted marshmallows on long sticks over the warm flames.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Honky's Inside Voice
uses.pageText: Honky felt sad. I am just too loud, said Honky. Sorry. TOOT.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

uses.title: Big and Small
uses.pageText: A bus is big. A toy car is small.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: It was the first warm Saturday of spring, and Aiden and Betty stood in the middle of the playroom staring at something that had got entirely out of control. Toys, books, games and puzzles were piled up to the shelves. There was even a foam sword that neither of them remembered buying.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: The reserve was layered with sounds — insects, birds, the river — all at once and all different. Socks sat on Aiden's shoulder and went completely still, his head turning slowly to track each sound. Aiden had never seen him so quiet.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: On the way home, Betty said they needed a tracker collar. Aiden said they needed to block every cat flap on the street. Mum said they needed a more interesting biscuit tin. Dad said they should call Uncle Eddie and tell him what his monkey had been up to. They all laughed, and kept laughing, all the way home — and Socks rode on Aiden's shoulder the whole way, looking, as always, entirely pleased with himself.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: It was an ordinary Saturday in late August when Uncle Eddie arrived at the door with a travelling bag, a very wide smile, and something small and determined making a noise from inside his coat.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie was Dad's younger brother, and he was a wildlife researcher who had spent the last two years living near a tropical rainforest, studying primates. He had, apparently, brought one with him.

uses.title: James and Anna and the School Play
uses.pageText: On the day of try-outs, James roared so loud that Mrs. Green's glasses slid right down her nose. He got the part!

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: The dentist sang a little tune while she checked Anna's teeth. Anna smiled the whole time. "Ten out of ten!" said the dentist.

uses.title: Reptiles
uses.pageText: Turtles have a hard shell.

uses.title: Space
uses.pageText: Stars twinkle in the sky.

uses.title: Animals at Night
uses.pageText: An owl can see in the dark. It hunts at night. Twit-twoo!

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: "His name is Socks," said Uncle Eddie. "He was orphaned when he was very small, and I've raised him from a baby. He understands a lot of what you say, he copies behaviour, and he is completely tame." He paused just a moment. "He is also, just occasionally, a little bit naughty."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: That night, Aiden wrote in his notebook: When something is unfair, you have two choices — pretend it isn't happening, or decide what to do. He starred the second option. He didn't quite know yet what doing something looked like.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: After lunch came Maths. Miss Okafor wrote sums on the board, each one slightly harder than the last. Some of them made Aiden's brain feel stretched in an unfamiliar way. He was discovering that this was not entirely a bad feeling.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The view from the top was unlike anything Aiden had seen. The whole coastline curved away in both directions — bays and headlands, a small fishing village far below, and the sea stretching to the horizon, catching the light like crinkled silver foil.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Bouncy won the jumping contest. Bouncy also won the unplanned bumping-into-things event, which had not been on the clipboard. Bossy added it.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: He was also, as promised, occasionally naughty. He dropped a teaspoon into the toaster. He unravelled the entire roll of cling film in the kitchen drawer. He stole every single one of Betty's hair bobbles and lined them up on the windowsill in a precise order that nobody could explain.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Aiden had been keeping a field notebook — just as Uncle Eddie had shown him. He had titled it: Socks: A Field Study. He had written things like: Prefers grapes to apple. Expresses disapproval by sitting with back turned. Unusually precise about the order of objects. He turned to a fresh page. It was going to take a very long time to fully understand Socks. He hoped, quietly, that he had the time.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Carefully, Uncle Eddie unzipped the carry-case. Inside, curled up like a small comma, was the most compact monkey Aiden had ever seen. He had cream-white fur on his face and chest, darker brown on his back, and small black hands and feet that looked, unmistakably, like he was wearing a pair of extremely neat little socks.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The cottage smelled of sea salt and old wood and something warm that Aiden couldn't name. They raced upstairs to choose rooms. There was a small room and a slightly bigger room. They flipped a coin — Aiden got the bigger room, but Betty got the one with the sea view, which meant it was perfectly even.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: The Dino Pals cheered. Honky cheered loudest. Every leaf fell off every tree in the whole valley.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: A message arrived in Sunny Hollow. Zippy delivered it. It took two seconds. There was going to be a race. A real race. With runners from other valleys.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Chips had been quiet all morning. Then they found him — in the veggie patch, eating the bean plants.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: They agreed on a proper tent for the garden — not a tiny pop-up one but a real one with a porch and a little vent window. Somewhere they could take their books on rainy afternoons and feel like they were somewhere else entirely.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: The view from the top was unlike anything Aiden had seen. The whole coastline curved away in both directions — bays and headlands, a small fishing village far below, and the sea stretching to the horizon, catching the light like crinkled silver foil.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: Anna found the duck pond. Three white ducks swam in slow circles. One waddled right up and ate seeds from Anna's hand.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: Betty was brilliant at boogie boarding from the very first wave. She rode it all the way to shore, fell off, laughed, and waded back in immediately. By the afternoon she was steering around in the foam. Dad tried it once and fell off at once, which everyone found funny, including Dad.

uses.title: Chips's Play Date
uses.pageText: "CHIPS!" said James and Anna. Chips blinked. Bella wagged her tail. It had been the very best play date.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: Shy, who knew every hidden corner of the Fernwood, led everyone to the deepest part of Cozy Cave. Shy knew exactly where it was warmest.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: James and Anna visit Grandma's Farm
uses.pageText: James chased Percy one way. Anna chased Percy the other way. Grandma just stood and laughed until her eyes watered.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty was not worried at all. She had already packed her bag twice. "We're going to have proper lessons and proper homework," she said, bouncing on her toes. "Isn't that brilliant?" Aiden wasn't absolutely sure that it was.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks sat at the table in a tiny red waistcoat that Uncle Eddie had stitched for him. He watched everyone use their fork with great attention. Then he picked up his own fork and used it correctly. Then he threw the fork across the room. "He does that every evening," said Uncle Eddie. "We've never understood why."

uses.title: James and Anna go to the Dentist
uses.pageText: At the dentist, there was a big fish tank in the waiting room! Bright fish darted in and out of rocks and weeds.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie came back for a long weekend in June — browner from the sun, with a new bag of unusual gifts and more stories than they had time to hear. Socks heard the doorbell and ran in circles for forty-five seconds without stopping.

uses.title: Animals in the Ocean
uses.pageText: A whale is huge! It is the biggest animal. Whales swim to the top to breathe.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: There was Socks, sitting on Mrs Obi's kitchen counter beside an open shortbread tin. He was wearing his waistcoat — which they had also assumed was missing — and had crumbs on his face and the expression of someone who sees absolutely no problem with any of this whatsoever.

uses.title: James and Anna build a Tree House
uses.pageText: BANG! BANG! BANG! went the hammer. WHIRR! went the drill. The frame went up bit by bit.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. Betty had already read a book about it.

uses.title: Socks Goes Missing
uses.pageText: "He couldn't have got out," said Dad. "All the windows were shut last night." Then Mum remembered the bathroom window — the small one above the bath, left open just a crack for steam. She looked at Aiden and Aiden looked at Betty. A crack that was, they all realised at the same moment, almost exactly the width of a small monkey.

uses.title: The Big Storm
uses.pageText: The storm arrived. It was loud and wild. But inside Cozy Cave it was warm. Fifteen Dino Pals, very close together. Even Grumpy did not mind.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie was Dad's younger brother, and he was a wildlife researcher who had spent the last two years living near a tropical rainforest, studying primates. He had, apparently, brought one with him.

uses.title: What is Weather?
uses.pageText: It is windy. The wind blows hard. Leaves fly in the air.

uses.title: Cheeky's Prank Goes Wrong
uses.pageText: Cheeky helped clean Fancy's rock. Will you do any more pranks? asked Fancy. Maybe just one more, said Cheeky. And winked.

uses.title: Zippy's Race
uses.pageText: Zippy held the small winner's pebble and looked at it. Zippy, said Sunny, are you all right? I nearly lost, said Zippy.

uses.title: The Sunny Hollow Games
uses.pageText: Who won the Games overall? said Chompy, having eaten most of the prize berries. Everyone won something, said Bossy. That is the point. Even me? said Chompy. Chompy wins: Most Enthusiastic Participant. That is because I ate all the prizes, said Chompy. Yes, said Bossy.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty have a Yard Sale
uses.pageText: Then things got busy. Children came from further up the street with their parents. A woman bought a whole crate of craft supplies without looking at any of them. A small boy bought four plastic dinosaurs and a jigsaw puzzle and carried them away in a tight proud bundle. Things were selling faster than Betty could write them down.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Betty leaned over and showed him her page quietly. Her joined-up writing was also not her best work. "Mine looks like a wonky caterpillar," she whispered. Aiden laughed before he could stop himself, and his face stopped being red.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: Uncle Eddie told them about the nature reserve two miles from town — woodland, a river, meadows, a hide for watching birds. "Socks would understand it completely," he said. Mum said she wasn't certain that made it a good idea. They went anyway.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: Then there was Science — real Science, with a magnifying glass and a tray of soil and seeds. Aiden forgot to be nervous. He was too busy looking at a woodlouse through the magnifying glass and writing down exactly what he saw.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: The summer holidays were over at last. Aiden sat on his bed and stared at his new school bag. Grade 1. The words sounded bigger than they looked.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
uses.pageText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. Aiden crossed it one step at a time, listening to the echo of his footsteps on old wood, thinking about every person who had crossed it before him.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "In Grade 1," said Miss Okafor, "we will read chapter books, solve number puzzles and begin to understand how the world around us works." Aiden thought that sounded like an awful lot — but he found he was leaning forward slightly without meaning to.

uses.title: Bugs All Around Us
uses.pageText: A worm lives in the soil. Worms help plants grow.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty Start Grade 1
uses.pageText: "Grade 1 is brilliant," announced Betty, just before bed. "It's actually not that bad," said Aiden, which from Aiden meant exactly the same thing. He turned his light off, closed his eyes, and was asleep before he could think of anything to worry about.

uses.title: Fancy's Bad Day
uses.pageText: Honky offered to shout at it until it moved. Everyone agreed this would make things much worse.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: "The point," said Miss Okafor, "is not that everyone will always be kind. The point is that you always have a choice about how to respond — and that choice is completely yours." Aiden wrote it down. It felt like something worth keeping.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Over the following weeks, Socks wove himself into the house. He had his own peg for his waistcoat. He met them at the door when they came home from school. He sat on Dad's shoulder while Dad read the newspaper and turned the pages for him, very seriously.

uses.title: The Four Seasons
uses.pageText: In winter, some animals sleep. We wrap up warm.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty go on Holiday
uses.pageText: On their last evening, they sat on the sea wall with fish and chips wrapped in paper. The chips were crispy and perfectly salty. Aiden told Mum they were the best chips he had ever eaten in his entire life, and Mum said that was the sea air doing it, and she was right.

uses.title: Tools
uses.pageText: A wrench turns bolts.

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and Socks
uses.pageText: Socks looked at Aiden. Then he looked at Betty. Then he reached out one small black hand, calmly removed Aiden's watch from Aiden's wrist, and put it on his own. He looked at it with great satisfaction. "Charming," said Mum. "Yes," said Uncle Eddie, completely unsurprised.

uses.title: Sunny's Rainy Day
uses.pageText: Oh no! said Grumpy. Oh no! said Dozy, yawning. Oh no! said Wiggly.

uses.title: Aiden, Betty and Socks's Big Adventure
uses.pageText: "Do you think he misses the rainforest?" Aiden asked one evening. Betty thought for a long time. "I think he's decided this is his rainforest," she said. Aiden looked at Socks on his shoulder. "Yeah," he said. "I think so too."

uses.title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
uses.pageText: Aiden felt two things: grateful for Betty, and also frustrated, because he wanted to have done it himself. Betty, who had been watching him think, said: "Next time you'll do it. I was just practising with you."

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip was walking through Moonwood when his foot kicked something small. It was a tiny stone. It glowed with a soft gold light.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "What is this?" said Pip. He picked it up carefully. The glow made his fingers feel warm.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone. "But I don't feel brave," he said. "I feel the same as always."

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "The stone did that!" said Pip. He tucked it safely into his pocket. Then he walked toward the Fog Marsh.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: The fog was thick and grey. Something rustled in the reeds nearby. Pip kept walking. He came out the other side.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: That evening, Pip sat by the Crystal Stream. He looked at the stone. The gold glow had gone out.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: "Did it run out of brave?" asked Pip.

uses.title: Pip and the Bravery Stone
uses.pageText: Pip looked at the stone for a long time. "I'll keep it," he said. "To remember."

uses.pageText: "How did you make it stop?" asked Pip. "I didn't make it do anything," said Fern. "I asked it nicely."

uses.title: Stone Crosses the Bridge

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip and Stone were sitting outside the Hollow Oak.
Then a noise came from the Fog Marsh.
It was very, very loud.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
"I want to find out what it is," said Pip.
"I do not," said Stone.
"It is very loud."

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Pip walked toward the Fog Marsh.
He looked back.
Stone had not moved.
Stone had moved one foot.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
They stood at the edge together.
The fog was thick and grey-green.
The noise bounced off the twisted trees.
"Together," said Stone.
Pip nodded.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
The toadling stopped when it saw them.
Everything was suddenly very quiet.
"Oh," said Pip.
"Oh," said Stone.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
"Why were you shouting?" asked Pip.
The toadling blinked.
"I am lost," it said.
"I was calling for my family."
Its voice was very small now.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Stone stood up and called out across the marsh.
It was the loudest sound Pip had ever heard.
Louder than the toadling.
Much louder.
Something answered from the far side of the marsh.

uses.title: Pip and Stone and the Loud Thing
uses.pageText:
Back at the Hollow Oak, everyone asked:
"What was the loud thing?"
"Very small," said Pip.
"Very loud," said Stone.
They both smiled.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the Hollow Oak, everyone heard it.
"The stream is singing again!" said Pip.
"We just moved a stone," said Fern.
"And asked the water nicely," said Dewdrop.
"It did the rest."

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
The next night, it happened again.
More things had moved.
"Was it you?" asked Stone.
"No," said Pip.
"Was it you?" asked Pip.
"No," said everyone.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
The next night, it happened again.
More things had moved.
"Was it you?" asked Stone.
"No," said Pip.
"Was it you?" asked Pip.
"No," said everyone.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
"I am going to find out," said Pip.
He told Glimmer his plan.
They would stay awake.
They would watch the clearing.
Glimmer said yes immediately.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Night fell.
Moonwood glowed softly.
Pip and Glimmer hid behind the big mushroom.
They watched.
Nothing happened.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
It was very late.
The clearing was empty.
Glimmer's eyes kept closing.
"Don't fall asleep," whispered Pip.
"I am not asleep," said Glimmer.
Glimmer was almost asleep.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then — a sound.
A shuffling.
A round shape moving through the clearing.
Pip and Glimmer looked at each other.
They crept closer.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
Then Burrow sat down.
Against the big mushroom.
Pip and Glimmer were still behind it.
Burrow began to snore.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
In the morning, Burrow woke up.
He looked around.
Pip and Glimmer were standing in front of him.
"Good morning," said Burrow.
There was a long pause.

uses.title: Pip and Glimmer and the Night Watch
uses.pageText:
"It was you," said Pip gently. "You sleep-dig."
"I am very sorry," said Burrow.
He put his boot by the door.
"Will that stop you?" asked Glimmer.
"I don't know," said Burrow.
"I am asleep."

He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

They bounced along the ground.
They made a sound like giggling.
They left gold trails where they bounced.
"What ARE they?" said Pip.

uses.pageText:

It was warm.
It had very large golden eyes.
It looked up at Pip and giggled.

The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.

"Eventually."

uses.pageText:
Stone raised their hands high.
Pip and Spark added a little push.
The star spirits lifted.
Up.
And up.

Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."

They listened together.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
"...they were right here..."
"Something is in the walls," said Wren.

Pip, Wren, Burrow, and Fern went inside to search.
They searched every room.
They found nothing.
Then Burrow's nose twitched.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:

He leaped from stone to stone.
One stone was slippery.
Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.

Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.

Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.

Pip, Fern, and Dewdrop came too.

"Every year, more things."

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:

They spent the afternoon clearing the marsh edge.
As they worked, the spirit watched.
Slowly, it began to sit up.

The mushrooms began to come back on.
One by one.
Pip watched them light up.
The marsh was where it should be.
The forest was where it should be.

Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.

"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.

A small creature was at the edge of the clearing.
It had very large silver eyes.
It was frightened.
It did not run.

He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.

It watched everyone with its large silver eyes.

"Together," said Stone.

The lamp lit a mushroom.

uses.pageText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.

uses.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
uses.pageText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: They gathered around the door. Luna looked at it for a long time. I know this door, she said slowly. I think. A very long time ago.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: What is inside? said Pip. Luna was quiet. Good things, I think, she said finally. I cannot quite remember what kind.

uses.title: Burrow Finds a Door
uses.pageText: The memory room, said Luna. That is what it was called. She touched the wall very gently. I remember now.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna woke up knowing she had forgotten something important. She sat on her branch. She thought very hard. She could not remember what it was.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: This was the problem with forgetting things. You couldn't always remember what you had forgotten. Luna knew it was important. She knew it was today.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: What do you remember about it? asked Pip. I remember it was today, said Luna. And it was important. And... she paused. I think it was outside.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it a meeting? asked Fern. I don't think so, said Luna. Was it something to collect? asked Burrow. Possibly, said Luna. I cannot quite say.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it a meeting? asked Fern. I don't think so, said Luna. Was it something to collect? asked Burrow. Possibly, said Luna. I cannot quite say.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it something to do with the Crystal Stream? asked Dewdrop. Luna stopped walking. She looked at the stream for a moment. Wait, said Luna.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it something to do with the Crystal Stream? asked Dewdrop. Luna stopped walking. She looked at the stream for a moment. Wait, said Luna.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna flew to the Crystal Stream. She landed on a stepping stone. She looked down into the water.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Under the water, among the pebbles, there was a small silver box. Luna had put it there herself. A very long time ago.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Yes, said Luna. I remember now. She picked it up. I put it there to keep it safe. For today.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Moonwood seeds, said Luna. From the first trees. For the day the old trees grow tired and need new ones beside them.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Luna gave one to each creature. One for each of them. The seeds glowed gently in their hands. Plant them this afternoon, said Luna.

uses.pageText: What would have happened if you hadn't remembered? asked Wren. I did remember, said Luna. With help. She looked at all of them. That is the point.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow went up to find Luna.
"Come with me," he said.
"Bring a light."
Luna said nothing.
She came.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Burrow went up to find Luna.
"Come with me," he said.
"Bring a light."
Luna said nothing.
She came.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna was very large for a tunnel.
She came anyway.
She did not say anything about this.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna stood in the doorway.
She was very still.
Her eyes went wide.
Then soft.
"Oh," said Luna.
Very quietly.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna stood in the doorway.
She was very still.
Her eyes went wide.
Then soft.
"Oh," said Luna.
Very quietly.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna walked slowly around the room.
She touched the carvings.
They lit up where she touched.
Blue and gold.
She had been here before.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"Have you been here before?" asked Burrow.
"Yes," said Luna.
She looked around the room.
"A very long time ago."
"What is it?" asked Burrow.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"This is the Memory Room," said Luna.
"This is where Moonwood keeps its oldest stories."
Burrow looked at the carvings.
"All of them?" he asked.
"All of them," said Luna.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
"This is the Memory Room," said Luna.
"This is where Moonwood keeps its oldest stories."
Burrow looked at the carvings.
"All of them?" he asked.
"All of them," said Luna.

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
Luna settled on a ledge.
She folded her wings.
She looked at the carvings for a moment.
"The first story of Moonwood," she began,
"is this."

uses.title: Burrow and Luna and the Old Secret
uses.pageText:
It was very late when Burrow noticed.
"Will you tell me the rest?" he asked.
"Yes," said Luna.
"There is quite a lot."
They both settled in.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
The magic seeds were gone.
The box that held them was open and empty.
Luna looked at the box for a long time.
"This is not good," she said.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna called everyone together.
"The seeds keep Moonwood glowing," she said.
"Without them, the forest will grow dark."
Everyone looked at each other.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
They split into groups.
Each group took a different path.
Each path led somewhere different.
"Find the seeds," said Luna.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

Luna bent down to look.
The seedlings were strong.
They were growing along the paths.
Around the Hollow Oak.
All through the clearing.
"Better than a box," said Luna.

uses.pageText:
That night, Moonwood glowed more than ever.
The seedlings lit the ground.
Everyone sat outside the Hollow Oak.
"I'm sorry I forgot," said Fern.
"Don't be," said Luna.
"They like it better here."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Luna pushed forward.
She looked at the star spirit over her glasses.
"I know what these are," said Luna.
"They lose their grip once a year."
"They need to go back before dawn."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.pageText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip told Luna.
Luna listened carefully.
"Something is wrong at the marsh," she said.
"We must go in."
Pip, Fern, and Dewdrop came too.

uses.pageText:
Pip told Luna.
Luna listened carefully.
"Something is wrong at the marsh," she said.
"We must go in."
Pip, Fern, and Dewdrop came too.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
They marked the boundary at the Hollow Oak.
Everyone placed a stone.
"The marsh is the marsh," said Luna.
"Moonwood is Moonwood."
"And we leave space for both."

uses.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
uses.pageText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren wanted to be taller. She had found a spell in her book. A growing spell, she was sure. She read it very carefully.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren looked at her hands. Her hands were a very long way away. She was not taller. She was one inch tall.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Oh, said Wren. Her voice came out very small. Everything around her was enormous.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren found her spell book. It was enormous now. She climbed up onto it and looked at the spell. She had read it backwards.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Right, said Wren. She walked to the beginning of the spell. She read it again. This time, she read it forwards.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Luna flew in through the window. She looked at the desk. She looked more closely. "Wren?" said Luna.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: "Fixing it," said tiny Wren. She raised her tiny hands. She said the spell again. Forwards, this time.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: There was another flash of blue. Wren was back to her normal size. She brushed off her robe. She straightened her hat.

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: "Did it work?" asked Pip. "No," said Wren. "I am exactly the same height."

uses.title: Wren and the Backwards Spell
uses.pageText: Wren picked up her spell book. She turned to the next spell. "But I am going to find a better one," she said. She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Don't sneeze again, said Wren. I will try not to, said Spark. His nose twitched.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Wren found a cold remedy in her spell book. She read it very, very carefully. Forwards? said Spark. Forwards, said Wren.

Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.
Wren had a direction spell.
"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.
Wren had a direction spell.
"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

uses.pageText:
An hour later, nothing looked right.
The trees were wrong.
The paths had gone.
"Where are we?" asked Wren.
Flint checked his map.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"We are here," said Flint.
He pointed at the map.
Wren looked around.
Grey fog was appearing between the trees.
"That is the Fog Marsh," said Wren.
"We are not near the meadow."

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"We are here," said Flint.
He pointed at the map.
Wren looked around.
Grey fog was appearing between the trees.
"That is the Fog Marsh," said Wren.
"We are not near the meadow."

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They sat down under a large mushroom.
They were tired.
They were lost.
The mushroom glowed cheerfully.
Wren looked at it.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"I wonder," said Wren.
She closed her spell book.
She spoke to the mushroom.
Very quietly.
She asked it the way.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint followed the mushroom trail.
The forest opened up.
The golden light of the Whispering Meadow was ahead.
"Oh," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"Why didn't we try that first?" asked Flint.
"I don't know," said Wren.
She looked back at the mushroom trail.
"They seemed happy about it though."
The last mushroom blinked once and went out.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern's garden was her favourite place.
One morning, Wren arrived with a cauldron.
"I have a potion," said Wren.
"It will help your plants."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Fern's garden was her favourite place.
One morning, Wren arrived with a cauldron.
"I have a potion," said Wren.
"It will help your plants."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Are you sure?" said Fern.
"Completely," said Wren.
She had practised many times.
Mostly.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren stirred the potion.
It was meant to be green.
It was more purple.
Wren did not notice this.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren stirred the potion.
It was meant to be green.
It was more purple.
Wren did not notice this.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren poured the potion on the plants.
The plants stood very straight.
Then they leaned.
Then one of them took a step.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Then all the plants began to walk.
They were very polite about it.
They walked around Fern.
They walked around Wren.
They went for a stroll.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Oh," said Wren.
"Oh no," said Fern.
"The plants are walking."
Wren checked her book.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
"Oh," said Wren.
"Oh no," said Fern.
"The plants are walking."
Wren checked her book.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Wren found the problem.
She had used the wrong book.
"This is the motion recipe," she said.
"Not the growing recipe."
She showed Fern.
They were both quiet for a moment.

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Everything was back.
"I'm sorry," said Wren.
"Did you learn something?" asked Fern.
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."

uses.title: Fern and Wren and the Wrong Potion
uses.pageText:
Everything was back.
"I'm sorry," said Wren.
"Did you learn something?" asked Fern.
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Wren and Spark tried search spells.
The spells pointed at each other.
Stone looked under every log.
Gently.
There were no seeds under the logs.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
They gathered the star spirits.
There were many of them.
Stone held several.
Wren had two in her hat.
They kept bouncing.

uses.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
uses.pageText:
Pip woke Wren.
They listened together.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
"...they were right here..."
"Something is in the walls," said Wren.

uses.pageText:

They listened together.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
"...they were right here..."
"Something is in the walls," said Wren.

They searched every room.
They found nothing.
Then Burrow's nose twitched.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race

They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.

Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race

Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.

Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.

uses.pageText:
"We'll take you home," said Pip.
"But the Deep Dark—" said Wren.
"We'll go together," said Pip.
Everyone looked at each other.
"Together," said Stone.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop knew every fish in the Crystal Stream. She talked to them every morning. They told her things: where the water was cold, where the best pebbles were.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: One morning, a new fish appeared. It was silver with a bright blue stripe. Dewdrop had never seen a fish like it.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Hello, said Dewdrop. I am the oldest fish in Moonwood, said the fish. Dewdrop tilted her head. The fish was not very large.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Hello, said Dewdrop. I am the oldest fish in Moonwood, said the fish. Dewdrop tilted her head. The fish was not very large.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: I have been here longer than the Hollow Oak, said the fish. Dewdrop looked carefully. The fish was, if anything, quite new-looking. I know all the secrets of the Deep Dark, the fish added.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop was not sure any of this was true. She knew the Deep Dark secrets. They were kept by a very old badger, not a fish.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Can fish lie? Dewdrop asked Burrow. Some of them can, said Burrow. Which fish? The new one with the blue stripe, said Dewdrop. Burrow had not seen a new fish.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Can fish lie? Dewdrop asked Burrow. Some of them can, said Burrow. Which fish? The new one with the blue stripe, said Dewdrop. Burrow had not seen a new fish.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Dewdrop went back to the Crystal Stream. Why do you say things that are not true? she asked. She said it kindly. She just wanted to know.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: You are interesting, said Dewdrop. You are the only fish in this stream with a blue stripe. The fish looked at its own stripe. That is true, it said.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: Is being the only blue-stripe fish enough? asked the fish. Yes, said Dewdrop. It is very enough.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: After that, the fish told Dewdrop true things. Small things, mostly. Where the water was coldest. Where the most unusual pebbles were. These things were true.

uses.title: Dewdrop and the Lying Fish
uses.pageText: What is the fish called? asked Pip. I... said Dewdrop. She stopped. She had forgotten to ask. She turned back toward the water.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: I think, said Dewdrop slowly, we should find you a cold remedy before anything else changes.

uses.title: What Luna Forgot
uses.pageText: Was it something to do with the Crystal Stream? asked Dewdrop. Luna stopped walking. She looked at the stream for a moment. Wait, said Luna.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
The Crystal Stream was not singing.
Fern heard it first.
Or rather — she heard nothing.
She went to find Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
"It flows," said Fern.
"But it does not sing," said Dewdrop.
"Something is wrong at the source."

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
"The song comes from the source," said Dewdrop.
"We must follow the stream up."
Fern looked at the deep forest ahead.
"Then we go," said Fern.

uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it with water.
She pushed as hard as she could.
The boulder did not move.
"I am not strong enough," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it with water.
She pushed as hard as she could.
The boulder did not move.
"I am not strong enough," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.
"Ready?" said Fern.
"Ready," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream

Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.
"Ready?" said Fern.
"Ready," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
They sat on the bank and listened.
The stream sang around them.
"We did it," said Fern.
Dewdrop smiled.
"It sang itself. We just moved the stone."

uses.title: Fern and Dewdrop Save the Stream
uses.pageText:
At the Hollow Oak, everyone heard it.
"The stream is singing again!" said Pip.
"We just moved a stone," said Fern.
"And asked the water nicely," said Dewdrop.
"It did the rest."

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop was at the Crystal Stream.
She was looking at something in the water.
It was a large fish.
It was stuck.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it loose.
She sent the water flowing hard against the rocks.
The fish did not move.
"I need help," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop tried to push it loose.
She sent the water flowing hard against the rocks.
The fish did not move.
"I need help," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop found Stone at the Hollow Oak.
"I need your hands," she said.
"Just to reach in and move a rock."
Stone understood immediately.
Then Stone understood all of it.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
"Just your arm," said Dewdrop.
"Just the one arm."
"Just for a moment."
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the water.
Stone sat down on the bank.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
The fish made a very large splash.
Stone was completely wet.
All of Stone.
Dewdrop was not wet.
"I'm sorry," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
The fish made a very large splash.
Stone was completely wet.
All of Stone.
Dewdrop was not wet.
"I'm sorry," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: Stone and Dewdrop and the Stuck Fish
uses.pageText:
Stone sat and dripped.
Stone looked at the arm.
Stone looked at the rest of Stone.
"The fish is free," said Stone.
"Yes," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop searched the stream.
Fern walked slowly around the clearing.
She was not searching.
She was listening.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop crossed the finish line.
She had glided the whole way.
She was not wet.
She was not ruffled.
"Finished," said Dewdrop.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop crossed the finish line.
She had glided the whole way.
She was not wet.
She was not ruffled.
"Finished," said Dewdrop.

uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Pip told Luna.
Luna listened carefully.
"Something is wrong at the marsh," she said.
"We must go in."
Pip, Fern, and Dewdrop came too.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Inside the marsh, it was colder.
The trees drooped.
The water did not move.
Dewdrop led them through the fog.
She could feel the water.

uses.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop went close.
"What is wrong?" she asked.
The spirit looked up slowly.
Its eyes were dim.
"My home," it said.
"Every year, smaller."

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint had decided to map every single path in Moonwood. He had a new roll of parchment and a good quill. He started at the Hollow Oak and walked north.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: On the fourth day, Flint held up his finished map. "There," he said. "Every path in Moonwood. All of it."

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint sat down on a mossy rock. He looked at the map for a long time. It was very beautiful. It was also completely wrong.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint took out a new piece of parchment. "I'll make another one," he said. He was not upset about this. He had always known the paths would move.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: By the time Flint found his way home, he was, as usual, slightly lost. The new map was already three pages long. He had taken a very interesting route.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: "How was the mapping?" asked Pip. "Perfect," said Flint. "I know exactly where everything was."

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Flint pinned the first map up inside the Hollow Oak. It was very beautiful. Everyone agreed it was the best wrong map they had ever seen.

uses.title: Flint Makes a Map
uses.pageText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly. They always did.

uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.
Wren had a direction spell.
"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.

"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

Wren and Flint were going to the Whispering Meadow.
Flint had a map.
Wren had a direction spell.
"We will be perfectly fine," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
An hour later, nothing looked right.
The trees were wrong.
The paths had gone.
"Where are we?" asked Wren.
Flint checked his map.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"We are here," said Flint.
He pointed at the map.
Wren looked around.
Grey fog was appearing between the trees.
"That is the Fog Marsh," said Wren.
"We are not near the meadow."

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren tried her direction spell.
The arrow spun three times.
Then it pointed at Flint.
"That's you," said Wren.
"I know I'm here," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Flint opened his satchel.
Seven maps fell out.
One was of the coast.
One was upside down.
None of them were quite right.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint followed the mushroom trail.
The forest opened up.
The golden light of the Whispering Meadow was ahead.
"Oh," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
Wren and Flint followed the mushroom trail.
The forest opened up.
The golden light of the Whispering Meadow was ahead.
"Oh," said Flint.

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
They arrived at the Whispering Meadow.
It was exactly where they had been going.
Flint wrote something on his map.
"Mushroom trail," he said.
"I should have had that already."

uses.title: Wren and Flint Get Lost
uses.pageText:
"Why didn't we try that first?" asked Flint.
"I don't know," said Wren.
She looked back at the mushroom trail.
"They seemed happy about it though."
The last mushroom blinked once and went out.

uses.title: The Missing Magic Seeds
uses.pageText:
Pip searched the Fog Marsh.
He found no seeds.
He found mud.
Flint searched the Tumblerock Cliffs.
He found no seeds.
He found three new things to map.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.pageText:
"They need height," said Luna.
"The highest point in Moonwood."
Flint reached for his satchel.
Everyone looked at Flint.
"I know exactly where it is," said Flint.
Everyone kept looking at him.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"This way," said Flint.
He was right.
The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.
"I always find things," said Flint.
"Eventually."

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
"This way," said Flint.
He was right.
The Tumblerock Cliffs rose ahead.
"You found it," said Pip.
"I always find things," said Flint.
"Eventually."

They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Halfway through, everyone was somewhere different.
Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: On the second day: a tiny spark. It landed on a leaf. It glowed for one second. Then it went out.

uses.title: Glimmer Tries and Tries
uses.pageText: "Maybe you need to try harder," said Spark. Spark's own magic crackled around his ears. Glimmer tried harder. More smoke came out. Still no fire.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark had a cold. Usually a cold was nothing much. But Spark's magic crackled around him all the time. A cold, for Spark, was a very big problem.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: He sneezed at breakfast. The porridge turned into a bird. The bird flew out of the window. Spark stared at his empty bowl.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Don't sneeze again, said Wren. I will try not to, said Spark. His nose twitched.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Spark. The flowers looked at him. He looked at them. His nose twitched again.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark tried to hold the sneeze in. His eyes went watery. His magic began to build and build. The sparkles around him grew very bright.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark sneezed near the Crystal Stream.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Sorry, said Spark. This was his third sorry. He meant all three of them very much.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Wren found a cold remedy in her spell book. She read it very, very carefully. Forwards? said Spark. Forwards, said Wren.

uses.title: Spark's Very Big Sneeze
uses.pageText: Spark breathed in carefully. I think, he said, I might need to sneeze again. Everyone took a large step back.

Glimmer and Spark made a deal.
Spark would teach Glimmer to breathe fire properly.
Glimmer would teach Spark to fly.
They shook on it.

He drew many diagrams.
The diagrams were very complicated.
Glimmer did not understand any of them.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Glimmer tried.
Smoke came out.
Just smoke.
"Interesting," said Spark, and wrote things down.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark tried.
Sparkles shot everywhere.
His hat fell off.
His feet stayed on the ground.
"I think I need more practice," said Spark.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark tried.
Sparkles shot everywhere.
His hat fell off.
His feet stayed on the ground.
"I think I need more practice," said Spark.

uses.pageText:
"Spark," said Glimmer.
"You are trying too hard."
"Fire is not thinking."
"It is feeling."
Spark looked at Glimmer for a long time.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"Spark," said Glimmer.
"You are trying too hard."
"Fire is not thinking."
"It is feeling."
Spark looked at Glimmer for a long time.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
Spark put down his wand.
He put down his notes.
He stood very still.
He stopped thinking.
A small real flame came.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"What does flying feel like?" asked Spark.
Glimmer thought.
"Like falling upward," said Glimmer.
Spark nodded slowly.
"I think I understand."

uses.pageText:

Glimmer thought.
"Like falling upward," said Glimmer.
Spark nodded slowly.
"I think I understand."

uses.pageText:
Glimmer ran.
Glimmer spread both wings.
Glimmer jumped.
Glimmer glided five whole steps.
"That's more," said Spark.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
At the end of the day, they sat down.
Spark could not fly.
Glimmer had not breathed fire properly yet.
But something was different.
Neither of them could say exactly what.

uses.title: Glimmer and Spark Make a Deal
uses.pageText:
"Did we succeed?" asked Spark.
"I don't know," said Glimmer.
"Let's try again tomorrow."
"Yes," said Spark.
They both smiled.

uses.pageText:

"I don't know," said Glimmer.
"Let's try again tomorrow."
"Yes," said Spark.

The spells pointed at each other.
Stone looked under every log.
Gently.
There were no seeds under the logs.

uses.title: The Night the Stars Fell
uses.pageText:
Stone raised their hands high.
Pip and Spark added a little push.
The star spirits lifted.
Up.
And up.

uses.title: The Big Moonwood Race
uses.pageText:
Glimmer could not stop.
Glimmer hit Spark.
Sparkles went everywhere.
They both kept moving.
Very fast.
In new directions.

Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.

Eventually.

She sat in the nest.
"Not yet," said Clucky.
